text:
I recently had the check engine light appear on my car with a warning about my breaks. I took it to the Mini Cooper repair shop and they recommended a bunch of services that would have cost over $4500. I decided to take my car for a second opinion and brought it over to K & C due to the good reviews.

It turns out that some of the services were needed, but not all of them. The ones that were needed didn't need performed immediately. Steven was very honest. He took a bunch of photographs to show me what he saw (that I didn't receive from the Mini repair center) and interviewed my driving style. Based on the information, he helped me come up with a repair calendar that would keep me safe and give me the time to save and make the repairs. 

The best part is his rates were significantly cheaper than the Mini repair shop, anywhere from a difference of 35% to 50% in price difference. I took the car to the dealer because there had been a limited warranty, but I won't return there since the warranty has expired. 

Steven was very fast in diagnosing my car and repaired my breaks very quickly. I'm happy with the service and will continue to work with Steven on the remaining repairs.

text:
So I'll be the first to admit that I don't know anything about how to fix vehicles or how to gauge how much it should cost to repair a vehicle. So I have no idea if I got a good deal on my service. I do know that they had to replace a part on my car for a 2nd time that they replaced only 18 months ago. It cost $650.

So what really upset me and will keep me from going back there is that when I got into my vehicle I immediately felt that there was something wrong. I noticed that all my mirrors had been changed, my seat had been moved-not just forward or back, but it had been raise up, moved forward and the back support at been lowered, my steering wheel had been moved, my radio stations had been changed and all my AC controls had been changed. Then I realized that my car had 60-70 miles put on it. I had just filled up the tank only a few days before dropping my car off and I had a half a tank when I picked up my car only 2 days later (mind you I have only driven it maybe 15 - 20 miles on my 7 minute commute to work since filling it up.) 

I immediately called them and asked, "did you guys drive my car around?"
Steven replied "oh yes we take it out on two freeway test drives." I can understand and appreciate a couple of test drives and I would have over looked 20 miles or so put on my car. 
Then I asked "how far did you drive it 'cause I'm wondering why I dropped it off with a full tank of gas and its returned me to me with only half." 
He replies, "oh well sometimes we take them home with us." 
"I kind of wished that I would have known you took my car out for such a long commute. I don't think I would have come to you guys if I'd know that nor do I think I will be returning as a client." 
To which Steven replies, "oh uhh we should have reimbursed you for the gas, if you want to come back we'll give you $20." For which I did.

Its not so much the money really, its more that I feel violated in a way. Like I'm momma bear and someone had been sleeping in my bed. It was obvious to me as soon as I got into my car that someone had gotten REALLY comfortable in it and I had no idea what, where or with whom they were driving my car. It left me with a really bad taste in my mouth.

text:
I'm sorry to say, these guys may be inexpensive, convenient and reasonable technicians, but they overlook the easy and important stuff, so I can only give them two stars. 

My Audi A4, Blue, and I have been together for a long time. When we first met, it was love at first sight, and knew I would have him forever. Well, like so many relationships, people change and they grow apart. He's not the same guy he used to be. Blue used to be quick, comfortable and fairly reliable. Lately, he's decided that he needs to see other guys (such as the ones that wear blue and grey and give him little motor oil and fluid treats). But I still love him, so I still want the best for him. 

Some time ago, Blue started making this horrible whining - groaning noise on a Saturday morning. This was pretty alarming, so I took him to the only Audi place that I knew was open, namely 123 Auto Service. 

I left him there for a couple hours and returned to be told that he unequivocally needed and new steering rack right away. That would be $1500, and we can do it on Monday first thing. Now, I couldn't believe that the part couldn't be had for less (it can't. Blue has expensive tastes) and I wanted my regular guys at Advanced Audi to weigh in, so I passed and told Steve I would call him Monday. 

Monday I called Advanced and they said that it the steering fluid was probably low (hence the noise) but that I should come by just to let them check it out. They had a look, decided the problem wasn't dire, topped off the fluid so the noise would stop and the steering pump wouldn't burn out, and sent me on my way with a complimentary bottle of fluid and instructions to come back in a few months or if the leak got worse. 

So here's the thing. Steve was right, I need a new rack, but I didn't need one right that second. It's now 7 months later and I'm ready to have it done now. More importantly. Steve neglected to do the easiest and most important thing, which was to make sure that the fluid was topped off at the time. Had I not gone over to Advanced, I could have easily burned out the steering pump in the few days I was driving around, and that would have doubled the price of the repair. 

Sorry, it's one thing to know what to fix and how, but it's another thing to have the sense to know what's important at the time. 

If you know what needs to be done to your car, you can probably trust them to do it properly, but I wouldn't count on them to actually help you.

Update: Steven was very eager to earn my business back, so I gave him a list of things that needed to be done for the car, and we worked out a price for all of it. They did all the work well, on time, and at reasonable rates. Sometime they're great at figuring stuff out (like noting that the fact that I was wearing out wheel bearings at a feverish rate was related to the hub being slightly out of round - expensive, but hopefully worth it), while other times they miss the easy stuff (like worn spark plug wires that were causing the check engine light to come on). They are always respectful, and as far as I can tell, really want to be honest and do a good job, even if it doesn't always work out perfectly. At the end of the day, they've treated me quite well, so I'll keep going. If you have an Audi or VW and you know the car, and what it needs and what questions to ask, see them, they'll fix you up. If you know very little about cars, take a friend who does.

text:
I found 123 Auto Service during a search for mechanics in the City that have a good reputation working on Subarus. This place came to the top of the list, so I brought in my car (I have 2005 Outback XT with 96,000 miles) to have my brakes (they were screeching) and engine (it was screeching while idling) looked at. Bottom line: This place rocks. They're fairly priced, very courteous, trustworthy and fast. 

As expected, my timing belt need to be replaced, as did my drive belt. Steven said that my brakes (pads and rotors) had plenty of life on them and that they didn't need to be replaced. He said they were squealing because they were a little rusty (which I'd noticed prior to dropping off the car), but this rust didn't impact the braking. A shadier mechanic could have used the rust, or just my complaint about the noise, to convince me to replace the brakes, but Steven just shot it to me straight. He said that if I found it too annoying, I could replace them, but it wasn't necessary. 

He also discovered that the front left axle boot (CV boot joint) had ruptured and needed to be replaced. I'd had the front right replaced two years ago, and, after comparing the two invoices I saw that the costs on the part was roughly the same, which make me believe he charges fairly for parts. Additionally, he noticed that I had some leaky gaskets - which I hadn't told him about, but had noticed because of the scents of burning oil I would get from time to time and some small oil leaks. This led me to believe that he's good at identifying problems without being told to look for them. 

Lastly, Steven noticed some dried coolant at the top of my radiator, but after conducting a pressure to test, he couldn't find any leaks or cracks in the system. He took the time to showed me the evidence so I understood what and where the problem was. A sketchy mechanic probably would have used this as an opportunity to create more business by suggesting that I need to replace my radior (which isn't cheap), but Steven said said we should just wait and see, since he couldn't pin down a problem.

When I was paying, he took the time to show me all of the parts he replaced and what was wrong with them. I think this says a lot about a good mechanic: he's willing to show what the problems were, what he did about it, and he's happy to explain in as much detail as you need why he did what he did. 

THEN, two days later, I had another great experience with Steven. The day after 123 Auto Service fix my car, I took it to fill up on gas. When I got to the gas station, the gas door hatch wouldn't open. I've never had this problem before. I took it back to them the next morning and they happily fixed it for FREE in about 15 mins.

text:
I took my VW here based on a recommendation from a friend and after reading the other reviews on the site. The symptom was a noticeable "wobble" in the steering wheel - at low speeds the wheel traveled left to right and at high speeds it dampened out to a wheel vibration. The car tracked straight while on the road.

Steve diagnosed a worn tie rod, bad control arm bushings, and an unevenly worn front left tire. He replaced the tie rod, two control arms, put my full-sized spare on the left front, and the worn tire in the trunk, rotated the right side tires, did an alignment, and charged $600. I have no problems with any of this. He also told me I needed new tires as all four were very worn. I'd checked the day before and all four tires passed the penny test, so I told him to leave the tires on. He also showed me the bad parts.

When I got the car back I took the worn tire in the trunk and rolled it across some pavement. It rolled straight - no sign of uneven wear. I put it on the car's left rear wheel, then went to move the rear tire to the front to replace the spare but discovered 123 Auto had badly over-torqued all the lugs on the spare. Three of the five required penetrating oil to coax off, one came off with no lube but lots of extra persuasion, and I stripped the locking lug trying to get it off and had to have the lug removed by a tire shop I trust. Not good for a scenario where the spare gets a leak and I can't change a flat on the side of the road. The tire shop made no comment on the wear of my tires.

My car was also due for a 100k maintenance so I took it to my regular shop two weeks later. They found that the left front CV joint boot was torn and were puzzled as to why the prior shop hadn't replaced it when they'd done the tie rod and control arm work. My shop also said my tire wear was fine and treads were even on all four tires.

So, one star, because lots of little things make me not trust these guys, and I have places I can go that don't set off these alarm bells.

Update: After I posted this review, Steve called me to apologize for the issues with the lugs and for missing the CV boot issue. He was also extremely earnest about offering to show me why the tire he'd removed was bad, and offered to compensate me in cash for the work I'd had done elsewhere. I appreciate the call back, but declined to take him up on any of his offers.

text:
l came in to have my car Mazda CX 9 to checked after the battery light came on, I assume need new alternator.
The shop took the time to properly test the system and confirmed that the alternator was still functioning correctly, even though the warning light had appeared. 
I really appreciated that they didn't rush to unnecessary conclusions.
During the diagnostic process, they also noticed a jolting issue with the engine.
This was something I was already aware of, and even the Mazda dealership had been unable to pinpoint the cause. Initially, the shop suspected the alternator might be sending a bad signal to the transmission. After replacing the alternator, the jolting issue was still present, but they didn't stop there. They went the extra mile by reflushing the transmission fluid multiple times and consulting with other shops about the symptoms. 
Eventually, they were able to identify the root cause and clearly explained my options moving forward.
The owner was extremely helpful, honest, and provided excellent customer service throughout the entire process. 
Thanks to their transparency and effort, I now feel much more confident about my car. 
I will definitely be bringing our cars here for service from now on and highly recommend this shop.

I checked around for someone new, and, lucky for me, found Kirill at KSH Auto via Yelp's service that searches for businesses in my area. I had asked for a quote, and instead of giving me one based on *my* conclusions, told me he would need to diagnose the problem. 
When I spoke to Kirill on the phone, he sounded energetic and very professional. He carefully diagnosed the problem, and called to give me a quote, which I approved. Apparently, he continued to carefully examine the issue, because when he called to let me know the car was ready to pick up, his diagnosis was updated and the price was significantly lower than what he had quoted. This was something that Brando would have done, and I was so delighted!
When I came to pick up my car, Kirill gave me some useful advice, including to drive it for awhile, and then we could talk about what to do next. He also recommended a place where I could get a smog check, and told me to bring the car by beforehand so he could make sure I would be able to pass.
I am so grateful to have found this shop and Kirill! I anticipate having KSH Automotive care for my Spyder and any future cars my family owns. Integrity, expertise and kindness are certainly something I treasure, and Kirill is a gem.

text:

Kirill looked at it, cleaned it out, used a special lubricant, and charged me a fraction of that cost. I eventually sold the Jeep but I talked to the new owner recently and 60,000 miles later it is still runing on the original transmission with no problems. Kirill will not fix things unless they are broken and will not overcharge you. 

He is one of the very few mechanics with a masters degree in engine building -- in other words this guy is far, far, far smarter and more capable than the average mechanic. 

I refer all of my friends to him and they all agree -- Kirill is simply the best.

text:
THE GOOD: I was overdue for an oil change and they were able to take me right away. The service included a free inspection, with pictures, that the customer could access online afterwards. This location is near Tj's, Target, and and plenty of other stuff to keep occupied with while waiting to pick up my car. This was all done, in a reasonable amount of time. As other reviewers have reported, the work was done competently and the pricing was transparent/consistent.

THE BAD: They called me back long before they were actually ready to let me pay my bill and go home. For most people, this would not be a problem. But I have a hidden disability which robs me of my ability to stand for more than a few minutes or sit in certain chairs (including theirs, as it turned out). No one at the desk had a spare second and interrupting would have been very awkward. I spent what turned out to be over a half hour (I checked the timestamps) thinking I was about to leave in "just a minute". A month later, I am still dealing with the resulting flare-up.

THE UGLY: The "inspection report" included a few matters "requiring urgent attention" (the most severe category), including the brake pads; which were "low" and "need to be replaced". Brought the car to my regular mechanic, who tells me the brake pads do NOT need replacing yet, and still have 40-45% left. Ditto for everything else on their list. 

YMMV, but I got hurt here bc they wanted time to compile some misinformation in an attempt to get more money out of me.

I called in on a Wednesday and made an appointment to bring in my vehicle on a Friday. I dropped off the vehicle for a diagnosis of the check engine light at 9a. I was told I would hear back by noon. 4p rolls around still nothing so I called back no answer. All good I know things get busy and hectic and car info gets lost in the shuffle sometimes. 

I hear back from someone at 430p and he tells me the issue - cool. He explains what parts I will need and I agree on the work that needs to be done. He tells me to return the vehicle on the following Wednesday to replace the part and so that their "electric guy" can re-program the vehicle. 

Wednesday I drop off the vehicle in the morning and they tell me it will be done by 12p. Great. 1p no call so I call and leave a message to get an update. Jim (the owner I assume) calls me back at 2p leaves a message saying they are still waiting for their electric guy and he will call me with an update. Not knowing if I should plan to find a ride home or if I should wait for the car to be done I called back at 430p and Jim is clearly upset that I called to get an update. After literally saying, "I'm returning your call to see if there was an update" he proceeds to be extremely rude over the phone and tells me "Did you not listen to my voicemail?" "there's no update!" What do you want me to tell you?! Are we done here? I said ok- thanks. Awkward. 

I actually was shocked that he would talk to a customer that way. Very unprofessional but hey maybe he was just having a day. I get it - but no need to raise your voice over the phone we are adults here. 

After that encounter I decided to stop calling the shop - that was on a Wednesday. 

4 days goes by - yes 4 days of not getting a call back or hearing anything from this shop so on the 5th day I decided to call. I asked for an update on the vehicle and the lady that works the front desk asked to call me back so she could "look into it." It turns out that that they were not able to fix my car and I needed to take it to the dealership. Not only was it a complete waste of time, but who knows when they would have called me about my car. The only reason I didn't rate it a one star is because they do free diagnostic and they didn't charge me for anything.

Very stressful not knowing what's going on with your vehicle, lack of consideration for customers who commute and need to make arrangements. Also after the temper tantrum it made it very uncomfortable to try to communicate with them. Seems very disorganized here, very messy shop, communication between staff members is an issue as well. 

10 total days passed by to be told they couldn't fix the issue.

Just take your car elsewhere for piece of mind and some professionalism.

text:
So I did return and to no fanfare this time. What changed!

I brought my car in with the check engine light on--time to take a smog test, so that's no good.
I called ahead and was told to drop my car off later that week--no big deal, it was still running just fine.

Took my car in...and waited...and waited. 
No word back, so I called them to check in. I was told (by a mechanic who was very polite and nice, but couldn't provide any info) that they hadn't quite narrowed down the problem yet and that they would call me back later that day. 
I did get a call back--still not ready. I was told they would call me back the next day with details.
Fine, I can be patient, I don't use my car daily anyway. I can live with this.

Get a call the next day and am told:
"it will be $300 to fix"
me :"ok, $300 to fix what?"
mechanic: "There are 3 things wrong"
me: "what 3 things?"
mech: "well I wrote them down, but I don't have the list in front of me"
me: "could you go get the list?"
mech: "well there are 3 things wrong and they'll cost about $100 each to fix, so that's $300 total"
me: " well sure, but what are the problems exactly? What are you fixing?"
mech: "We found 3 problems and we'll fix them for $300, but you know you never know how much it costs until you get in there..."
me: "I'll be by to pick my car up this afternoon"

Sorry, but I'm not just handing you $300 and hoping for the best!

I picked up my car and took it elsewhere.

Turns out there was only 1 issue: got my car fixed and it definitely didn't cost $300.

text:
Cars are not my thing. I like looking at them, admiring them, and most of all driving them. Simply put, my extent of knowledge on this subject ends there. I have a feeling the majority of the public fits this similar profile. 

When you go to a mechanic, you put your trust and faith that he will take care of your as he does his own. Unfortunately, there are others that ruin this relationship by cheating, being dishonest and that spoil it for the good guys out in the world. 

I can say with complete confidence that Emerald Repair (owned and operated by Jim) is one of the honest few that fits the former description. Jim went above and beyond to help and assist me with my problem. I had a problem with my alternator which prevented my car to start up the night before. After I called him to access the situation, he volunteered to come to my apartment and jumpstart my battery! Who does that? Jim does. That's just the kind of guy Jim is. 

We reached his shop ordered all the parts and assured me that I'd get the car in a few hours. Although the garage was filled with cars, he made it a priority to help and fix my situation first because I had to come back to work later in the day.

When I got returned to his shop, my car was back in its original condition. He even did some body work on my front bumper that I damaged some days before for free! Again, that's the kind of guy Jim is. 

His staff also exemplifies all of Jim's exemplary qualities. Kee, one of his mechanics, saw me waiting for a taxi, offered me a ride back to my apartment.

Jim is not a guy looking for short term gain or profits but a genuine, honest, blue collar guy that is always willing to help a guy out in need. You will never go wrong going to him. There's a reason why he's got 4.5 stars and this many ratings. 

Sometimes people say, "good guys finish last." Jim however doesn't. He clearly separates himself from the pack and that is why he is always successful. Honesty is the best policy!

Thank you Jim from the bottom of my heart. You have a customer for life. (well, as long as I'm in the city of San Francisco).

With a $98 an hour shop rate, I decided to look for closer shops around the area rather than venturing south and spending all my money.

text:
I first took my Toyota 4Runner to Jim when he was still at the Inner Sunset location.  My sister-in-law had borrowed my truck to take snowboarding in Mammoth. When she returned, she said she wasn't able to disengage the 4WD and had taking it to a shop at the mountain. There she paid $200+ to have the 4WD turned off and an estimate from the shop for around $500 to get it fixed. A year later when I finally saved enough dough, I took my truck to Jim for the repair on a friend's recommendation.  He called me BEFORE fixing a metal rod that the other shop had broken trying to disengage the 4WD manually and told me a switch needed to be cleaned and the repair would cost $90! I instantly fell in love with Jim and have had NO problems with my 4WD since.

Jim is honest, hard-working and extremely affordable. Because he is such an awesome mechanic, his shop is very, very busy, hence the overflow of cars and slow turnover at times.  His shop is definitely not for the impatient.  Saying this, I've had tons of work done there of late (brakes, tranny flush, tire rotation, timing belt, tune-up) and he has always managed to squeak me in at a moment's notice and give my car back within a few days.  He can be a bit scattered at times (aren't we all). Keeping in mind his time crunch and how fantastic he has been with my car AND my pocketbook, I never stress out taking my car to the shop because I know Jim will do whatever he can to save me money while fixing the actual problem.  Yay Jim Gavney!!

I've always passed by this place and have seen TONS of cars here.... never did I think I would have to come here... text:
For about a month I seemed to have to press on my brake pedal a little harder each day to get my car to stop (and stay stopped). It felt like there was a balloon under my brake pedal and as I pressed on it, the balloon would deflate, causing my car to roll forward. Occasionally the car would lurch forward even with my foot firmly on the brake. 

So after reading all the positive reviews, I faithfully took my car to Emerald and spoke with Johnny (everyone's favorite employee-and he really was quite nice). Johnny told me they were quite busy, but that I could bring my car in that afternoon and they would get to it "as soon as possible". Which they did the next day. He told me that they had flushed the lines and checked all the connections, that my brakes seemed "soft", but I had 80% of my brake pads front and back so I should be fine. I asked "did you test drive it?" and was told that someone had indeed test driven the car. I had the sense they were very busy and not really willing to spend any more time and effort on my brakes. So, I paid $37 for the time they spent looking over the car and drove it off the lot. 

The problem persisted over the next month and got even worse, so I called Midas. The guy at the Geary street location (Jim) suggested that the car may have an issue with the master cylinder or power booster, but said I absolutely should not drive it, as it was very dangerous to do so. I said "I have been driving it like this for over a month". 

At the Midas shop the guys could not believe I had been driving the "death trap" for that long without an incident. They replaced all the lines, and replaced the master cylinder, they have to replace a seal in order for the car to be completely safe, and I have to wait to do that work because I am now broke, but at least the car stops now. 

So, bottom line is, although the guys may be nice, the shop is busy and they may or may not give your car the care and attention it (and you) needs.

text:
Looking at the number of stars some people give this shop, i find it SHOCKING.

I took my car here over a year ago for a simple oil change. The brakes were working well, and I had just had them checked out several months before by another shop that I had been using for many years. I came to pick up the car after the oil change, and one of the 2 owners said "by the way, your brakes are not working well...have you noticed that before?...no? well, i don't have time today but i'll look at it another time." I proceeded to drive the car away from the shop, and the brakes barely worked enough to stop the car. Thank you, Emerald Auto, for almost allowing me to drive off into a fatal car accident.

The shop then tried to repair the brakes and said that AFTER taking the whole car apart, they realized I had unusual molding on the brake lines and they couldn't find a part to replace them. This required the transfer of the car to the dealer, which wanted to charge me $2000 for fixing the brakes that were fine when I brought the car in for a change. Perhaps Emerald Auto needs to use a lighter foot when handling our cars, so as not to pound our brakes into the ground.

As an additional plus, it is fabulous that they have no space for anyone to put their car when they drop it off. Just an added bonus. Thank you Emerald Auto, as I am now the proud owner of a new Honda civic, which I will keep FAR from your shop when it needs a repair.

This place is golden. 

The garage is cramped and unassuming. I've lived 2 blocks from it for years and walked by on a daily basis, as it is right next to the 12th & Judah N stop.

Big mistake. I don't even want to calculate right now how much money I've wasted over the years at another garage (see other reviews for more deets). 

I was referred to Emerald by a friend, called to make an appt and then couldn't take my car in due to my scheduling issues. So, I waited. And wondered. And hoped the car, which had a lit "Check Engine" light, would keep on keepin' on. I don't drive often these days, but being a kid from the suburbs, can't give up my car (it represents Freedom, even to this day, after years of car payments in lean times and living in a major metro city).

Then, last Friday, as I was walking out the door to head to the hospital to visit someone in a real emergency, the battery died. Nada, zilch, nothing. Coded.

I called my insurance company's roadside assistance program. Shortest estimate to get a truck out to jump it- 45 minutes. Called Emerald, apologized for not even being one of their customers yet and told them I needed a jump in an emergency. Jim told me no problem, he'd be over in 5 minutes.

**Let me reiterate- at this point, I was not even a regular customer. And Jim dropped what he was doing to come help me out.**

And that's all it took. He came immediately, jumped my car and wouldn't even let me pay him. Saved my ass in a time of real need. 

A few days later I took the car in for a new battery and some other much-needed, long delayed repairs- I dropped by without even scheduling with them- and they had my car in and out in just 2 days and the cost was AMAZINGLY low. 

My car is now running better than it has in YEARS.

Support this garage. If you believe showing support for small business, throw your hard earned bucks this way. This garage is honest and does great work. I have never trusted a mechanic- at least until now.

text:
I brought my car into Stress-Free Auto Care for a routine oil change and tire rotation. Instead, I was told I had an oil leak and that my front lower control arm bushings were torn and needed replacement. My car only had 37,000 miles on it, so I couldn't shake the feeling that I was being taken for a ride.

The inspection report flagged the bushing issue in red, which pressured me into agreeing to the repair. I ended up spending a staggering $2,580. This was my first time visiting this shop--I usually go to the Subaru dealership--and I deeply regret the decision.

Their claim of an oil leak was never confirmed. After some inspection, they said they'd need to remove more parts to investigate further. I declined. Then the receptionist acted like she was doing me a favor by charging me only half the inspection labor fee because they couldn't find the root cause. That felt manipulative.

A few months later, my car started having battery issues, so I took it to my dealership. I brought along the paperwork from Stress-Free for reference. The dealership replaced my battery and, upon inspecting the supposed oil leak, said it looked more like someone had splashed oil on the engine rather than an actual leak. When I asked about the bushing replacement, they said it was unusual for a car with only 37k miles to need that repair--though city driving could cause wear, it was hard to say definitively.

I also spoke with several male friends who are knowledgeable about cars. They all agreed that bushings typically don't need replacement until around 100k miles. That confirmed my suspicion: this shop may be taking advantage of customers, especially women, by recommending unnecessary repairs.

I'm angry and disappointed. I'll never take my car anywhere but the dealership again. What stings the most is that I told them I was looking for a neighborhood shop to build a long-term relationship with. Clearly, they didn't care. It was anything but "Stress-Free." Avoid this shop at all costs.

text: Let's start off with what car I have, 2016 Honda Civic 1.5L Turbo. For the past four years or so I used an online mechanic that would come to your location, home or work. I made the an appointment online which offered a $10 discount for first time customers. Which I didn't get. No biggie. Well any ways I made an appointment for a Saturday morning appointment. We then proceeded to the office so he can finish checking me in. As he was typing stuff into the computer, he then asked agin why change my oil. I told him I have a turbo engine and I want it to last longer so I change the oils more often. He then toils me he also has a car with a turbo and he domestically change oil that often. He then told me next time he was NOT LET ME CHANGE MY OIL AT 50%. He said he follows the manufacturer service guide...or something like that. I thought to myself, they don't want my business?? I felt kind of offended, how can you tell a customer not to bring your car in for service. This is not his car. This is "My Car" and if I wanted to change oil every month that is my business not his or the auto service company's. Overall with the attitude I was treated like a moron that likes to waste money. I will not be bringing my car to get serviced here since they don't want my business. I will be looking for a new mechanic the next time my daughter comes home.

This should have been a slam dunk five star rating. 

Great: My car died and was long overdue for a general check up including replacing the battery. Called around and Emerald was the only shop able to see me within a 48 hour period. Jim was able to get the car in mid-day that day and turn it around first thing in the morning next day. Really happy with the speed. A lot of people are concerned about the ethics of a mechanic - didn't get that vibe from Emerald at all. More of a "You want to come to us? Fine. You don't? Fine." The charges were reasonable and itemized.

Meh: Not much of a talker and handled my request while also handling another customer and the phone at the same time but as long as he gets the job done, that's all that counts.

Disappointing: Jim and team went 95% of the way (I hope) in doing the check up and replacing the battery. But the last 5% is where it was just simply sloppy. In the morning, I was dropped off at my finished car and the Emerald team had left the lights on all night - already significantly draining the brand new battery they had just installed in the car! Got in the car and the maintenance light was still on. I think they did do the work but didn't take the 30 seconds to reset the light. Similarly, the stereo panel was locked and required the "code" which is a fairly easy thing to punch in in any standard Honda. It did make me wonder about anything else that may have been hastily done. I called Jim to let him know about the things that were 95% there but missed out on the last 5% due to a lack of attention as I believe its much better to give direct feedback (I'd certainly prefer that in the business I run). I left a message but never got a call back. 

Overall, I would come to Jim again in a pinch but probably feel like I have to micromanage exactly what I wanted done and check it thoroughly to feel really comfortable.

text:
I pondered for quite a while whether this should be a 2-star review, but I could not agree with myself that Emerald Auto Repair deserves more than 1-star. This review has been posted after my first, and last ever, visit.

Wife took it upon herself to get an oil change (2013 Mazda 3) based on location and Yelp reviews, which led her to this place. Maybe that was my mistake for letting her do anything involving the maintenance of our automobile, but it's only an oil change, what could possibly go wrong? So I let her be and sent her with a note with the only instructions that she would need, which was to get 0W-20 oil, or 5W-20 if 0W-20 was too expensive. (Mazda owners manual kind of recommends either)

What the owners manual DOESN'T recommend is the oil that Emerald saw fit to offer and administer to the engine of our car. Apparently, wife was recommended a "blend", and not knowing what that is, she accepted that recommendation (because it was from someone who allegedly knows more about cars than we do). When she got home and gave me the invoice, I immediately knew that she didn't get what she was supposed to. The invoice says that she received a "blend" of "5W-30/10W-30/10W-40/20W-50." WTF is that?! 

Even the large text on the oil cap on my engine, which clearly says "SAE 0W-20", should have been a fairly major red flag to not continue with their 'recommendation.' 

This obviously seemed questionable, so I called as soon as I saw it, yet Jim, the guy who mans the phone and the front desk, insisted that we got 0W-20 and it was a perhaps a computer mishap. Well, there are numerous other things that tell me that was not a computer error: (1) the price that she paid did not reflect what a 0W-20 oil change would cost just about anywhere; (2) the decal placed inside the car window had a handwritten mileage for next oil change as +3,000 miles (Mazda recommended oil changes for these newer car engines is 5,000-7,500).

It was during this phone conversation that I learned that she had to bring the car back on Monday (it was Friday and they are not open on weekends) to get a part installed that they didn't do because it was not in stock. I didn't even think to ask what this was for, assuming it was connected with the oil change. I was already going to bring the car back on Monday and have them drain their garbage "blend" and put the proper oil in. 

On Monday morning, when I pressed, Jim admitted that we didn't get the oil that this car is supposed to receive, and so he got me in fairly quickly, and I left with my new (correct) oil and no additional charge. Before I left, though, I was asked to come back again for they still had the wrong part, which turned out to be an air filter. Not thinking about why am I getting a new air filter, I left. Unable to go back later in the day, the wife did... and came home with an additional $52 invoice. WHAT?! 

While I don't mind paying for the proper oil, this unnecessary air filter cost almost half of this new invoice. (I could have bought my own air filter online for half of what they charged me!)

I looked in the owners manual and I placed a call again. It recommends changing the air filter every 37,500 miles, of which my car has 15,000 miles less than that. Jim told me that the air filter was "dirty" and, probably seeing where I was going with my tone, said that they don't "upsell for things that aren't necessary". I am quite confident that my "dirty" air filter would have been good enough to last until its recommended time for change. I was offered my air filter back because "the trash wasn't picked up yet" but I declined the offer, because it's not like they are going refund this new one that we've already driven on (despite not many miles). 

Quite simply, this was a lot of hassle over one oil change... one oil change that should have been done correctly in one visit with zero additional phone calls. I would rather pay more at the over-priced dealership than go back to Emerald Auto Repair.

text:
Bar none the BEST mechanic shop in all the Bay Area. text:
I have been going to Jim for about four years now. I have one of those cars that the mechanic cringes when I pull up as it is a difficult car to work on. Jim always takes amazing care of my vehicle. His staff is friendly and knowledgeable, and they are honest. They will show you a part that will need repairs, tell you when you can expect to fix something or they will tell you to hold off to avoid double repairs. Instead of making a quick dollar by putting a band-aid on a situation, they show you and address how long you can wait or if this is a bigger fix. They will also take the time, if you ask, to show you the broken parts they have taken off your cars and what exactly they repaired or replaced.
Jim and his team go the extra mile as well. I had to get my water pump replaced this week. I needed my car last night, but when I showed up, it still had another twenty minutes to go. I was on a very, very tight schedule. Instead of making me wait and be late to a work event, the team drove me to my house to walk my dogs and pack my bag for work that night. They swung back around exactly twenty minutes later, as agreed, and took me back to my car. They stopped everything, right in the evening when there are massive pick ups at the shop, to ensure I wasn't late. That extra care and attention have made me a customer for life. 
Emerald Auto is always busy, but that tells me I am not the only one to have discovered this gem in the heart of the city. They are honest and extremely exact on repairs. As a single woman in this city, I am always a bit guarded with mechanics, but I know Emerald Auto and the team are people who are there to fix cars and not take advantage of you. I HIGHLY recommend them.

text:
This is a review I really never wanted to have to write.

In the past, I've sworn by Jim and his shop. I've referred other people to him. I've raved about him

That was then, this is now.

I don't know what changed; maybe it's because so many earlier satisfied customers, like myself, referred so much business that they got overwhelmed. I really don't know what happened here. But after today's experience, I'm finding another mechanic.

First off, I'm handicapped. I have multiple sclerosis. My car is 95% of how I get around; without it, I'm basically dead in the water.

I brought my 20-year-old Infiniti in because, increasingly, I was hearing a loud ominous squeaking that accelerated when the engine revs accelerated. I dropped the car off with a request to see what was causing it - being handicapped, I can't afford to be stranded somewhere - and also to please check the front brakes.

Verdict was a bad rear bushing. I said okay, fix that. He said I'd been right about the front brake pads needing to be replaced. Cool, do those too.

I was able to pick up the car a day later than he'd told me it would be done, with not one but THREE new bushings, and the new front brake pads we'd agreed on The bill was $750.

Right. Not happy, but I paid it. 

Guess what? Squeak was STILL THERE. In the interim, the driver's side door latch suddenly stopped working from the outside. I went back to Jim and said look, I can open this fine by leaning across the passenger seat but it would be nice to have access to my car without having to risk triggering the MS by long painful stretches, and oh by the way did you guys DRIVE this car before you said it was the bushings? Because the squeak is still there.

That was yesterday (Thursday), early. I let them know that I needed the car by this morning, since I had a noon appointment for medical stuff in Daly City. Last thing I heard was "I'll call you within the hour".

Five hours and two calls from me later, I was finally told "needs a new latch, about $237 out the door for the part, plus labor."

Upshot is, can't do it. Just blew $750 on three bushings for my still-squeaking 20 year old car. OK, he said, I'll put the door back on. You can get it tomorrow (Friday) morning.

Long story short: the car door now no longer opens from EITHER side. And managing to crawl across the front and start it, the air bag light came on and started flickering.

Oh, and turns out "I FINALLY drove the car and heard the squeak, it's a bad fan belt tensioner." Why not have driven it BEFORE we did five hundred plus bucks worth of bushings? 

When I asked him to please put the car door back the way it was when I drove it in so that I could actually use my car in the interim, I got first shouted out and then he turned his back and walked away.

It's a shame about this place. A year ago, I would have rated them as high as you can get. After today, time for a new mechanic. I wish them the best, Jim's a good guy, but I'm out of there.

I get my car regularly maintenanced by the same mechanic my parents have had for 30 years, so I knew that that wasn't really the case. Not to mention, I was bullied into thinking that nowhere else in the City would I find a cheaper, "honest" service. He even went so far to point out that I don't drive a Honda Civic (I must have driven away in a Subaru by mistake, the last time I was at the grocery store).

I was frustrated by the quality of service, but almost resigned to the cost of the fix. I jumped on Yelp, and found Emerald, which was three blocks from each my house and my office. Not expecting much, I called them, just to get a comparative quote, and spoke with Jim. He gave me the "conservative" quote, which was still hundreds of dollars less than what the other garage had quoted. He also reassured me that he could do it for less, probably. As much as it was the surprising cost difference, it was probably more the way Jim treated me. He gave me honest answers, helped me with a tow service to fetch it from the other garage, and made sure that I didn't possibly need anything out of the car. He treated me with respect during every interaction, and I really felt I was being taken care of. Real customer service.

While it took two days to have my car fixed, I know that Jim took real care to make sure it was resolved. His mechanic did a whole one over of the car, and made sure I knew of any minor issues to keep an eye on, rather than fix unnecessarily. When I got into the car, it felt brand new! 

Definitely going to be using Jim for all of my car fixes in the future!

text:

How many shops will do that?
They saved me $250 in labor cost as well as a mark up since I bought my starter at Kragen.

I highly recommend taking your car to Emerald for your car repairs. They are the only shop with mechanics that are able to diagnose your car on the spot and they do an excellent job.
Their lot is packed with cars for a reason.
They are honest and affordable mechanics!

text: BE CAREFUL with this place. They seem nice and trustworthy mostly b/c of the reviews on here... but they are not. I went there once b/c of a clicking sound in my car. The next day the car was making the same sound and they said that one of the axles was "defective" and needed to be replaced again... Later, I had different problems and STUPID ME I decided to go there again b/c I figured it must be a one in a million chance that the parts they use are defective. He told me my transmission was out and needed to be replaced with a used one. Said it would take a week. A couple weeks went by and he hardly updated me on progress, always said he'd call back whenever I called, never called back. Finally he told me the car was ready. I spent $2,000 and drove my car off the lot - and it did the VERY same thing - couldn't switch gears! I didn't even get around the block and came right back to the shop. What's worse... when I went to pick up the car - he charged me more than he quoted on the phone. When I asked him about the price quote, he said " I don't know where you got that number from?" These guys seem nice, but they aren't. They take a much longer time than anyone else does although, granted, they are very busy. I'm not sure how they got a reputation for being so "honest." Either (1) I lucked out and had two conincidentally totally bad experiences with the parts they use within a few months of going to them or (2) the mechanics themselves are writing the reviews on yelp. I think it's a bit of a scam.

text:
I'd never heard of Emerald Auto & Brake until I came across it on Yelp. With a high 4.5/5 rating based on almost 50 reviews, that seemed like a good enough indication to me that I'd get some good service for my car. And behold, I did.

Not only were the prices quite good, but when I came back to pick up my car, Jim was quite friendly and test drove my car with me to verify the work done, and he discussed what was changed and answered all the questions I had. It was clear to me that these guys do good work at good prices, and treat you like a customer, not just a revenue source.

I took my car in for a brake job - front brakes were squealing, so I figured it was time to get them replaced. I got their early in the morning, and within a couple hours we talked by phone and he told me that it's possible my front axels might be bad, but he'd look at it once he got the brake assemblies off. At the end of the day, Jim told me that the axels looked fine - no need to replace them, they still had life on them - and they took care of my squealing brakes. 

A dealer or other mechanic might have tried to ram new axels down my throat, but Jim was on the level with me and said they were good enough and safe to use. I really appreciated that honesty. Total bill came in at a very reasonable $238. For all parts and labor, that's a good deal. I've had minor dental work that costs more. Hell, I've bought electronics that cost more than that - the work they did means I can drive my car safely and not... oh, what's the word... die. Yeah, that's the word I was after. What a great deal! I'd easily expected to walk out with a $500+ bill, but the actual bill came in less than HALF of that.

Their shop is tiny, dirty and crowded. But who cares. They do good, solid work at a good price. No jerking me around, no attitude, no blow-offs. I'm not a car guy, and I'm naturally suspicious of mechanics, but from this experience, Emerald and Jim did me right, and I'm very pleased with their work. I will definitely return there for my next automotive adventure. I happily recommend Emerald to anybody.

My one concern: they weren't as proactive about calling me with updates as I would have preferred. Jim said he'd call me with an update, and when he didn't, I ended up having to call them every 2-3 hours to get an update. In the end I got the information I wanted, and he probably forgot to call because he was busy (they must get a lot of business), but still, as a customer I shouldn't have to do that legwork when I'm paying the bill. So to those reading this, I suggest you be ready to pick up the phone and call them if they don't call you back within 1-2 hours after they say they will. If they fix this faux paus, I'd have nothing to complain about. Despite this minor thing, I still recommend them. :)

text:
Don't go here.

My left side brakes were grinding, no doubt they'll have to resurface the rotor. Checked Yelp, called Emerald, "Bring it in tomorrow morning."

Got there at 8:30/:45, said it would be $150 if it was just the pads. He said he'd call in two hours and let me know what it would be. Around noon I called to see what was up, "Can I call you back in 20 minutes?"... I called again "You're gonna need new rotors, so it'll be just over $300" "Both rotors?" "Yeah, they're under spec" "What time?" "Should be done by 4" 

At 4:30 I called again "Yeah it's ready, uh, hold on ... No it's not ready yet, can I call you back?" (are you starting to see a patter here?) 
At 5 I started to walk the distance from Willard street to the garage, all closed up with one guy just about to leave. "Hi..here for the Honda" He looked at me guiltily "Did he call you back?" "No, I just wanted to get here before you closed" He looks on a small board for my key and grabs the phone "The guy is here for the Honda, here talk to him"
"Hello? We close at 5:30 and you're car won't be ready until the morning" "I was told it would be done today and I need it tonight" "OK, do you have a spare key?" "??11 uh, yeah" "OK, go home and get it, your car's over on 9th, you can come over and pay in the morning." ...and hung up.

His buddy was looking mighty worried, still looking for my key. I raised an eyebrow, "Uh, that guy's mighty rude." He explained they were actually two different businesses, and that I should ask for some money off for my time and inconvenience. I took the N home, grabbed my key and took the N back. Drove home. He actually -did- change the rotors.

Don't go here.

text:
THIS IS LONG, BUT YOU'LL BE A BELIEVER IF YOU READ IT:

*****************

My car, Dodgy, has more than 100K miles on him, is ten years old, has lived in several cities from coast to coast, and has been cursed with one accident (only once with me in it) at least every 18 months since the first WEEK that I brought him home (... within Dodgy's first 1000 miles, his front bumper had been sheared off by a NYC cab and stuffed into the back seat by my ex-boyfriend). 

Needless to say, Dodgy has had a rough life and has been handled (and MIShandled) by many a body shop and mechanic. During my first three years in San Francisco, I took my car to several different places (too many to name) and received friendly, expensive and unnecessary repair service. 

One day, Dodgy and I went to see a movie at Century 20 in Daly City and parked in the free garage adjacent to the Todai building. Dodgy's rusty muffler lost its will to live and hung onto the car with a small brace and screw. Until Dodgy tried to go over a speedbump and the muffler ripped loose, through my rear BUMPER and fell off right in front of this hot guy in a nice car behind me. It was really an AWESOME experience because I was already feeling great that day from a break up with a long-time boyfriend and the termination of a temporary job. It was truly my lucky day.

I put Dodgy in park, opened my car door and trunk, strutted over to my muffler and thanked the guy behind me for honking saying, "thanks! yeah ... I think I might need my muffler", and waved when I got back in my car.

Since I wasn't working, I drove my car to four different places to get estimates on the body damage to my bumped and to replace my muffler. Each place had an outrageously high estimate for the work I went in for AND told me that I had other issues with my car that they noticed needed immediate fixing (* please note that I never received the same diagnosis from more than one place, leading me to believe they were all scammers). 

Frustrated, I sent an email out to friends asking for suggestions, receiving a list of highly ranked shops from one of them. Emerald was ranked tops in every category from Customer Service to Work Quality to Hourly Rates to Recommendation level.

Took Dodgy to Emerald, didn't tell Gary about my visits with other shops and waited to hear what he had to say. He eyeballed my car and said something like "looks like you need a new muffler and some attention to your bumper" and drove me around the Inner Sunset for a while to see if there were any other sounds he heard that might indicate a problem. He told me my car was in fine condition and seemed to only need the muffler. I asked if he was sure. He said yes, is there something else that is wrong that I don't know about? I then listed off four or five other issues that had been brought to my attention by the other people. He said he had no reason to believe that those were an issue and would I mind popping the hood and he'd be happy to check. I did. He did. And he said ... nope, your insides look clean and pretty good like they'll last you a while. If you want me to do your muffler, I can look underneath without a problem. I said sure and asked how much. He told me. It was about half the price of the other people. I asked how much of the charge was parts so I could determine the labor. He told me. I asked if he was flexible about the labor rate since I had lost my job and was pretty sure I'd be going to him from now on (since I had determined he was fair and honest), and he dropped it even lower (not a ton, but I appreciated the gesture). 

They fixed my car and when I went back to pick it up and pay, the price was even less than the reduced quote he gave me.... he said it didn't take too long and was pretty easy since the muffler had already fallen off. Bahahaha!

Anyway... I'm a devotee of this place now. It's like taking my car to the doctor for checkups when I go here. I know that there are a few problems that will need attention in the next few months, but I also know that nothing is urgent or life-threatening AND I've been told what signs/sounds to look out for in case I want to know when I absolutely MUST bring it in.

Just got my brakepads and rotors replaced yesterday. I got caught up with my day and missed the calls that Gary made to tell me my car was ready. Shop closes at 5.30, but he called me every hour after that until I called back (at 7.30) so I would get my car back last night(I had told him that I really needed it and would like it back ASAP).

Love this place. LOVE IT!

P.S. - Who is that guy in the photo? I've never seen him before either...

I picked up my last night and was more than pleasantly surprised to find they waived the labor costs on the third and final repair and I drove my car home last night.

JR

text:
Subject: Formal Complaint Against Stress-Free Auto Care
Address: 2941 Geary Blvd, San Francisco, CA 94118

To Whom It May Concern,
I am writing to formally express my serious concerns about my experiences with Stress-Free Auto Care located at 2941 Geary Blvd, San Francisco, CA 94118- Phone: (415) 751-7860. Based on my multiple visits for repairs on two different vehicles, I feel compelled to warn other potential customers about the untrustworthy practices multiple misdiagnosis , and inflated charges at this establishment . 
Top Reasons to Avoid Stress-Free Auto Care:
1. Untrustworthy and Misleading Practices: I have experienced poor workmanship, misleading diagnoses, bogus additional fees and inspections having had the same issues addressed multiple times--specifically, vibration, leak, grinding noises, rough rotation, and shaky wheels when turning. Despite being told that these issues stemmed from the steering rack which they replaced , I am still facing the same problems after so many visits , which indicates either a lack of skill or intentional misdiagnosis to inflate charges. 
2. Alarming Payment Requests  Questionable Billing Practices 
One alarming aspect of my experience was the way I was treated when asked to pay a staggering amount of $7,651.01 in cash or cashier check!  It's unreasonable to expect customers to pay such a large sum in cash or by cashier's check, especially when all my credit card payments had been approved through the year. This request feels suspicious, suggesting they were aware that their previous repairs were inadequate. The ongoing issues--vibration, grinding noise, rough rotation, and shaky wheels--indicate that the problems were not resolved, and this pattern of misdiagnosis raises serious concerns about their shady business, expertise and integrity.
3. Inflated Fees and Bogus Charges: The shop has charged me excessively for repairs and introduced unjustified fees, including a "storage fee" of $175, which I was neither informed about nor signed for. This charge is not only unethical but potentially illegal.
4. Repeated Misdiagnoses and Concealed Issues: I brought my vehicle in for oil leak issues and a transmission inspection, only to be charged double fees for additional and unjustified inspections (over $900) for what should have been a straightforward assessment. They failed to inform me of the actual leak until I came to pay, after having the vehicle for ten days. Concealing this, despite the high inspection fees, is unethical and unacceptable.
5. A Disturbing Pattern: Multiple Visits, Numerous Bills, and Persistent Issues at the Repair Shop

*             Mon, Dec 11, 2023, 11:05 AM: Same leak inspection & repair -- $2,349.38
*             Appointment: May 25, 2024, 9:00 AM/ Leak never fixed right
*             Invoice Date: May 30, 2024, 3:47 PM -- $1,420.17/ Leak never fixed right

*             October 29, 2024: $7,651.01/ Leak never fixed right-still leaking as they acknowledged 
6. Poor Customer Service and Lack of Resolution: When I sought to resolve these issues, manager Mr. Loren Winfrey refused to compromise or reach an amicable solution, I tried over and over but he shut the door in my face each time . My attempts to escalate the matter to his boss Mr. Yinon Weiss were met with indifference! 
I have documented all my interactions, including receipts and invoices, to support my claims. Given the pattern of behavior exhibited by Stress-Free Auto Care, I intend to file a complaint in court to protect other consumers from being subjected to similar experiences.
I reserve the right to pursue legal action if necessary. It is imperative that potential customers are made aware of these shady practices , bogus and inflated charges to avoid being misled and overcharged.

text:
I brought my car to Stress-Free auto a few weeks ago. I created a Yelp account just to warn other potential customers about my bad experience here.

The staff is very friendly, and based on the other reviews, it seems like they do a great job when things go well, but I'd like to share my experience when things *don't* go well.

I brought my car in for some maintenance. Though they fixed the issue I brought the car in for, when I picked it up, it was making a loud screeching noise that wasn't there previously. I immediately turned around to show it to the mechanic, who drove around the block with me and confirmed there was a problem.

They weren't able to service my car then, so I brought it back a few days later. They called me later that day, saying they had fixed the issue.

It was immediately obvious as soon as I started the car that they had not fixed the issue. Because it was a loud screeching noise, it's impossible to miss; they knew they hadn't fixed the issue and just wanted me to go away.

I gave up, because they had clearly lied to me. I made a formal complaint via email, which they never responded to.

Again, I do think my experience may not have been representative. But, know that if something goes wrong with your car, they will be friendly and maybe even really try to fix the car. But, if they don't know how to fix it, they may react how they did with me - they were comofrtable lying to my face then ghosting me.

Just be careful when going here is all.

text:
I had the best experience. Out of nowhere at 8am during a storm, I started having issues with my brakes. I called and Trina answered and told me to bring it in. They let me know the work on my brakes (and belts I had been putting off) may not be done by the end of the day. Since I was in SF for work but live in the east bay, Trina said she would hold their loaner car for me just in case so I could get home that evening. They also ordered me a courtesy Lyft to work. I did end up keeping the loaner overnight free of charge and the work was done the following evening. My transmission fluid was completely dry but it was too late in the evening to do anything. She was concerned for me so she called SEVERAL places near my house to confirm the fluid was in stock and showed me where to top it off myself when I got home (after making sure I was comfortable with this of course). Their text communication and photos of work so you can see what they are recommending and why, made my experience beyond stress-free. text:
Found this STAR Smog Checker on Yelp. If your car is older than year 2000, just heads up that you'll have to make an appointment with them. However, it was easy to make one for next day at the time I wanted (they seemed very open to any time). 

I showed up the next day at 9am, and there were several cars already parked in the driveway. I managed to get the last spot in their driveway. There was some employee working on the car in front of me, didn't bother to say hello. So I went to the front desk, and while waiting for 4 mins before someone showed up, I noticed the HUGE MESS in the lobby, the desk in the lobby, the garage itself, etc. etc. It was so disgusting. It seemed like their whole garage hadn't been cleaned or organized in about 15-20 years. Random junk, papers, loose items, random small items on the floor like it needed to be vacuumed. It was quite appalling. The guy ended up showing up and was very friendly though, told me to fill out a quick form. Then he disappeared again, and I had to wait another 4 mins. When he returned, he said it'd be roughly an hour wait, which I anticipated for my old car. 

I was killing time at Fifty Fifty coffee shop down the block. He ended up calling me 1.5 hours later. I wasn't too bugged by it since I wasn't too strapped on time, but I can see how that can be frustrating for some, especially if I had an appointment. The final bill came out to $60, pretty reasonable. 

Pros:
-Easy to make appointments
-Friendly service
-Fair price for smog check
-Fifty fifty coffee shop is 2 short blocks down, great for killing time with wifi

Cons:
-Super dirty interior of carshop in lobby where you wait
-Went overtime by 30 mins, may be big deal to some
-They seem understaffed, and could use someone in the lobby at all times to help get things going for customers. 

Overall I'm happy with the service and would return. You just need to level set your expectations here.

text:
Cannot recommend this place. I called ahead to ask for the cost of smogging a 1996 vehicle and was quoted $50. However, once I got there, the price had become $80, reduced to $70 when I complained. A far cry from $50. Rationale had something to do with the type of machine required to smog such an ancient car. As I mentioned age of car when making initial inquiry, and again the previous Friday when I brought it there in the late afternoon and was told to come back Monday, I couldn't help feeling that the shop had pulled a bait and switch.

Moreover, once the car was finished, somebody from the shop took off with it, without even stopping to check whether I (the owner) was on the premises to pick it up (I was waiting in dingy cold office) and the car disappeared. Jim made several attempts to reach employee by phone to no avail. 15 minutes after I had paid bill, the car and driver were finally located. It had been parked several blocks away, far from any shop supervision. In fact, next to the tree area of USF on Anza where vehicles are highly vulnerable to smash and grab threats as there is little traffic on that street.

It would not have taken much for the person in the office processing my bill to inform the employee charged with moving my car out that I was there waiting for it. Instead of circulating around, using MY gas and wasting both his and my time, he could have simply handed it off to me in the driveway of the shop and all would have been copacetic.

Only reason I came to Emerald was because original quote was dramatically lower than that of most other smog shops in the area. That should have been my tip off. Clearly a case of penny wise pound foolish. Learned my lesson.

In the end, not much cheaper than other places where cars remain under shop supervision and are returned expediently to customers. 

My suggestion: get smogged somewhere else.

text: This is really a zero star review, but we all know that Yelp makes us give one star. I was recently in San Francisco, and had car trouble on the drive down. Due to my experience with a different mechanic we were 95% sure that one of the camshaft sensors needed to be replaced. Based on yelp reviews and availability I decided to bring my car to Emerald auto repair. We gave them the information that we had about the camshaft sensor. They ended up spending multiple hours diagnosing the issue and replaced the crank shaft sensor and charged almost $400. On my six hour mountainous drive home alone with two children, the car was behaving in the same ways it had been before we took it to Emerald. The problem was not fixed, and we luckily made it home before the car died. I took my car to my highly competent mechanic whom I have been using for well over a decade. He replaced the camshaft sensor, and the problem was solved. When I called Emerald to tell them that they had replaced the wrong part after I told them what was probably happening they told me they would get back to me and never did. After multiple calls where no one picked up and multiple messages that no one returned, I finally got through to somebody. They told me to call the warranty place, but when I called the warranty place they said they didn't cover issues that the mechanic didn't take care of, only issues that the mechanic did take care of. If you want to spend a lot of money and a lot of time waiting for your car only to get it back and still have the same issues that you started with you should definitely go to Emerald.

text:
This review is long overdue. I have lived down the street in this neighborhood since 2010 and that first year I went to every auto shop in the area for everything from smog checks to oil changes to major repairs (there are a lot). I figured I had options so I may as well figure out which one I like best. Of the 3 or 4 I've found no better than Jim at Emerald, and after that first year or so I've always gone to him.

Sure his shop is a little rough around the edges, but he has always made sure I'm well taken care of. Last year my car had an issue with the clutch losing pressure and there was an expensive fix that was guaranteed to work (very expensive) or an affordable fix that had a decent chance of working. He understood my car was not worth that much so we decided on the cheap fix and it worked for a few days and then started to break again... Ultimately we did the fix that involved taking apart my transmission. He called me to make sure I was okay with the cost, and ever since my car has worked great. He was trying to keep my costs under control, but neither of us could have predicted that the expensive fix was inevitable. If I recall correctly he only charged me for the second fix, and threw in the labor/parts from the first attempt since it didn't work.

Recently I went on a road trip and I was worried about the car since it had that major breakdown a year back. I stopped by and their shop was totally slammed, but he fit in a quick check for me and told me all it needed was an oil change sometime in the next few hundred miles, but nothing urgent.

Whenever friends have car troubles I always tell them to swing by. He's great.

text:
This is indeed my first ever Yelp review but every time I leave Emerald Auto I have a huge urge to review so finally I have gotten around to it (only about 20 minutes after leaving their shop)... They deserve 5 stars any day. I have been taking my little old 2004 Toyota Corolla (122,000 miles) to them for a few years now and am seriously impressed every time. 

I am the epitome of a stereotypical gal who knows literally nothing about cars... seriously, its pathetic... When I first moved here I tried a few different auto shops in the city who all charged me WAY too much, had me "fix" things that didn't need fixing and were inconvenient, sloppy and rushed. I got to a point where I would make my friend take my car in for me so they wouldn't scam me. Until I happened upon Emerald/Jim and Crew and all its glory!!

Their prices are reasonable (I mean hey, its SF, nothing is going to be super cheap), the attention to detail is excellent, and the clear knowledge and genuinely nice and honest group that works there deserve praise. As I am such a noob for car related issues, I run everything by my friend who is a car guru before getting any work done (he even has the same car as me so I trust him more), he too is incredibly impressed with what he has heard about Emerald and is always shocked by their prices and their HONEST way of business. 

Seriously... Emerald Auto never ceases to impress me, in particular the owner Jim is beyond fantastic. He is patient, friendly, kind, does not take advantage of a lady who seriously knows nothing and the most importantly, he is totally honest. Any time I have brought my car in for weird sounds, oil changes or just to give it a quick scan/check up, I am beyond satisfied with the work ethic, in-depth inspections and the minor adjustments (brake pads, things I didn't ask for) Jim and his crew will throw in for free. Jim has never even slightly seemed like a guy in it only for the money and he has been so straight forward and upfront every time I go in. 

Few examples? Example 1: "I think I need my tires rotated?", answer, Jim looked and told me they were totally fine and it save the money until next oil change, he also made minor adjustments on my brakes to keep them in tact for free, told me it was a simple tightening and clearly he wasn't going to charge me. Example 2: Jim warned me my clutch was on its way out, again as I know nothing I asked him repeatedly if I should just get it fixed then or wait, he told me how expensive clutches were and to save up until it gets really bad and fails. Example 3: I am heading on a road trip and was concerned on my clutch which has become progressively worse (as expected) than months ago (thanks SF..), Jim was completely upfront with me, gave me all the options and knocked 2 hours of labor off my final price. Example 4: They are not greedy dudes who will charge you $100+ to look at your car, you pay for what needs to be done and if its nothing then its nothing. 

I seriously could go on an on. Needless to say, I really adore these guys and I would recommend them to anyone. I have and will continue to suggest their service to any and all people. Those I have converted to these guys (after many a stories and "I seriously think I have the best mechanic in SF") have only spoke their praises as well. 

Finding a good, honest, fair and truly genuine mechanic (esp in SF) is incredibly difficult and always a crapshoot. I am thrilled to have come across these guys a few years ago and will continue to claim continuously about how I probably have one of the best mechanics in the city. 

Thanks a million to Jim and the crew. You guys rock.

text:
I just got my car back and couldn't wait to "yelp" about Tom and his team. This is my first experience writing a review for anything or anyone, but the awesome care and service I received from Metric Motors totally warrants it.

I had just bought a used BMW "as is" - didn't pass smog due to bad cats. So I started looking for mechanics on Yelp and noticed that Metric Motors had 39 five-star rated reviews. I called them up and talked to Tom, immediately it felt like I was talking to an old friend. I told him about the issues with the car and my concerns that I might have bought a "lemon" so he told me to bring it in and he'd do a PPI or pre-purchase inspection, except in my case, a post-purchase inspection. (I strongly encourage all used car buyers to make sure they do a PPI before they buy). 

I brought the car in the next morning and received a call from Tom a couple of hours later giving me a very thorough review of the car, defining, in user-friendly speak, the various items found in the inspection. He confirmed the cats were bad and would need replacing in order to pass smog. I told him that since the registration expires in a couple of days that I'd pay for an extension and bring the car back the following week to get it fixed, but Tom said "don't get the extension, we can probably get the cats done today and get it smogged and registered tomorrow." Well, Tom and his team followed through - fixed the cats, smog tested AND washed the car - I was able to register my car the following day. Furthermore, the cost was comparatively less then the quotes I received from other shops. When I picked the car up Tom showed me the parts he had replaced and gave me a list of recommendations with timelines to keep the car running efficiently.

I highly recommend Metric Motors, Tom and his team define excellent workmanship, customer service and satisfaction. I not only drove away with peace of mind, but educated and encouraged. I'm a client for life!

text:
Lifesaver. That's what Tom was for me. The story:

On Dec. 23--just one day before my planned holiday roadtrip--the dreaded check engine light blinks on. (Stay calm.) First thing the next morning--Christmas Eve--I start calling around, hoping to find a shop in the city with some time to investigate, like, now. A couple of the well-regarded specialty shops turn me away ("we're all booked until next week"), and at this point I begin to freak out.

Then, as luck would have it, I get ahold of Tom at Metric Motors. His eagerness to help is immediately apparent, even over the phone. After a few minutes asking questions and troubleshooting what could possibly be wrong with my car, he invites me to bring it in.

Although not officially a BMW "specialist," he seemed to know my E46 inside and out. Not only that, he's very open to sharing his knowledge with the inquiring customer: everything from the esoteric ("the final stage resistor could cause your battery to drain") to the very basic ("you should only use BMW-brand coolant--the blue stuff"). A true professional.

He had my car checked out, topped off, and on its way with a clean bill of health in about the time it would have taken to ride the bus home. Tom's passion for auto service impressed me, big time. He sweats the details, and isn't happy until his customer is. 

After dealing with the folks at Metric, there's no question where I'll be bringing my car from now on.

text:

Tom apparently is the new owner and I began to tell him my story on why I hadn't been back. He was sympathetic and he told me his story about leaving corporate life and how he bought the shop from the old owner and the things he's done to change the business to become better at serving his customers. He locked up my car and then drove me home! At that point, I did believe the reviews I read. 

I'm just getting back from picking up my car. Turns out a cooling hose burst and needed to be replaced. They fixed my car, washed it, got it back to me in less than a day and bill was 66 bucks! I was really worried and thought it might be hundreds of dollars, but was pleasantly surprised and thoroughly pleased with the service I received. 

Way to go Tom! Thank so much for making the extra effort to take care me. You've certainly made some great changes and I'm glad to say you've got me back as a loyal customer.
