text:
Our Audi A3 overheated, and our normal mechanic said the engine was ruined, head gaskets were melted, told us to just trade it in, I didn't have $60k laying around for a new car, so I just parked it back in my garage. A few months later I called around to a few garages but no one would touch it, they all said the same thing, trade it in and get rid of it. 

Then I called Jose at Metric, he's the only mechanic who said "Bring it down, I'll take a look at it". When I went down to his garage he literally stopped working on the car he had in the bay, took a flashlight to my engine, told me it was only the water pump in about 30 seconds, and gave me a reasonable ballpark repair quote on the spot. I was kind of dumbfounded thinking it can't be this simple, but a day later he started working on the car, sent me video text updates with the work he was doing on it, and low and behold he fixed it, cleaned out the valves, checked all the fluids, did a nice oil change at my request, and, I can't believe it, but my car now runs like a top, no kidding, like a brand new car, oh my god I can't tell you how happy this has made my family. 

Metric Motors is a great shop, I don't even want to talk about them because then they'll be swamped, but wow they really did a great job on my car and it's running perfectly now, I can even go on road trips with it, I'm so impressed I can't even begin to tell you.

Thank you Jose, Angelita at the front desk, and there was another mechanic there as well, thank you guys so much for the great work you did for us, we are so happy we found you!

text:
I can't say enough good things about Joel and his team. He really went out of his way to save my ass. If you're in the SF area and need a honest and trustworthy shop, Metric Motors is the place for you.

Epic essay below.

I was driving my 1999 Lexus LS400 from Los Angeles to San Francisco and about 15 miles away from SF, my car broke down while driving on the 580. The engine died and then threw a CEL. I got stuck on the freeway and had to be towed off. The car was then parked on the street, close to my Airbnb. The next morning, I come out to find that someone had smashed in my passenger window...great, more shit to deal with.

So now...not only did I have the CEL, I had glass everywhere. I had one service call left from AAA, I thought..."how am I going to get back to LA?" First thought was...okay, get the car towed as far back as possible (200 miles) to a Toyota/Lexus speciality shop. The issue there was, well...it would likely take awhile to get 200 miles south of SF and by the time I got to whatever shop, it would be too late for them to diagnose any issues.

Step in Joel and his crew at Metric Motors. I had sent a mass Yelp blast to all the shops in the SF area, seeing if anyone might be able to help me out. Joel was one of the first to reply and instantly I knew that MM might be the best option for me. He offered to see my car as an emergency service and quoted me $100 to diagnose the issue. At that point my dilemma was...do I use my last tow to go 8 miles to MM or 200 miles south to whatever awaits me. After a brief conversation with Joel, I decided to go with MM and hope they'd be able to help me out.

Okay, so the tow truck drops me and my car off at the shop. Joel says they'll get started and that it should take a few hours. I go about my business, now trying to enjoy the extended time I have in SF. A few hours pass and Joel calls me back, he reports that they ran several tests, but the CEL that I had previously seen wasn't reappearing. Okay, good news? So after explaining what MM had tested, Joel and I both came to the conclusion that due to my extended journey from LA to SF, my ECU might have just overheated and thrown the CEL, but after sitting for an extended period of time all was well again. He advised me to drive the car back to LA, but make more frequent stops. Joel was also kind enough to vacuum up most of the glass that was all over my seats and carpet.

This is the real kicker though, when I was pulling out my money...ready and happy to pay, he stopped me and said, "don't worry about it, we really didn't do anything and I was the one who convinced you to come here in the first place." Wow, seriously...when does that ever happen? What a standup guy, running a top notch operation.

I could go on for another few paragraphs, but I think I've made my point.

Metric Motors...yeah, they're pretty great.

text:
I got great quality service and clear explanations for years from Tom and team on my Volkswagen, I must have used him 40-50 times in total. But the real reason I'd advise anyone to go to Tom is that you can trust him when things don't go well.

Long story short, on one service occasion I had a battery replacement done at the shop. When I picked up the car, check engine lights were on. I had to bring the car back for a diagnostic ($), and then had to purchase a part the car supposedly needed for ~$800, which I bought from a wholesaler directly (cheaper than Tom could offer, and since it was OEM he agreed to let me).

When I brought the car in to do the work, the team discovered the error codes were not due to a faulty part, but wires from the battery replacement they hadn't re-connected properly. They made a mistake, whatever, we all do sometimes.

They easily could have re-attached the wires, changed out the part, and charged me for the labor. I never would have known. But these guys have integrity. They called me immediately and let me know their error, and Tom got in touch later to let me know he was going not only to refund my money for the diagnostic, but also willing to cut me a check for the part I bought.

You cannot ask for more in a field where the professional (the auto-mechanic) typically knows 1000x more about your car than you do. When you know you can absolutely trust them to always do the right thing for you, there's no reason to go anywhere else.

I only wish Tom worked on domestic vehicles, since my new ride isn't German-made.

text:
This incident took place in 6/2016. I didn't follow up on Yelp at the time, but recently thought, "I use Yelp, so I should contribute information."

I had brought our BMW 325xi to Metric a couple times prior, once limping in with a bent belt pulley, another for LOF and brake fluid flush. The first visit was very satisfactory and avoided serious damage. The second visit went OK, but they forgot to reset the CBS (condition) codes; I noticed all the warnings from before the service were still on before I left, so brought their tech back out to reset them; a minor annoyance.

I stopped going to Metric after I brought the car back for newly-balky power windows and door locks. It turned out the battery was shot, so we scheduled a replacement. They performed the work, I picked up the car & paid, and went for a drive to Half Moon Bay. On the way, the dash display started throwing messages about faults in the AWD, while the car alternately surged and lagged at ~60mph. I pulled into a parking lot at the earliest opportunity, where I proceeded to wait 3 hours for a tow truck, as the car refused to start once turned off. I called back Metric to let them know of this new severe failure. AAA towed the car back to Metric, where I learned the next day the technician had failed to secure all connections to the battery terminals! I wasted 3 hours and risked severe damage to the car because Metric failed to install a battery properly, one of the simplest maintenance tasks on a car. The car has shown none of these symptoms since this was resolved.

To their credit, Metric took my call, paid my ride home and back to pick up the car, and refunded the full cost of the invoice. They're nice guys, pleasant to work and talk cars with, but that should never lead to such gross inattention to detail. Seeing the recent good reviews, perhaps they've upped their game since.

text:
Tom and Joel at Metric Motors are awesome! Having recently moved to the city for a new job, I knew that I would one day need to find a mechanic when something in my BMW breaks down. That day finally came when I noticed an insane amount of coolant leaking out of my car, and I looked on Yelp for a mechanic. I messaged Metric Motors to get a quote and an initial diagnostics, and they were extremely helpful in pinpointing what the issue could be just based on my description of the problem. After speaking with Joel on the phone, he informed me that I could bring the car in and they would work on it immediately. Joel called me about two hours after I dropped the car off at the shop telling me that they found the issue, and sent pictures of the cracked radiator indicating where the leak was coming from. He suggested that they replace the radiator and promised that it would be done before end of day. Sure enough, I got a call a few hours later and the car was ready and the total came in just a bit under the quoted price. Talk about efficient service!

Unfortunately, the coolant started leaking again and I immediately called the shop and talked to Tom, the owner, who suggested that I bring the car in and they would take a look to see where the leak could be coming from. When I got to the shop, Tom immediately dropped what he was doing and popped the hood of the car to try and pinpoint the problem. Tom had my car up on the lift within fifteen minutes of me walking into the shop, and did a pressure test trying to pinpoint the leak. Within minutes, Tom and his mechanics were able to find the leak and Tom informed me that they would take care of it free of charge and would let me know once the problem was fixed. Not even two hours later, Tom gives me a call and tells me they were able to fix the problem and the car is ready to be picked up! Turns out it was a faulty part on the radiator, and Tom went to the BMW dealership to pick up the part immediately after I left so he could repair the leak. Tom and his mechanics at Metric Motors really do stand by their work, and I would not hesitate to bring my car to them in the future. Highly recommended!

text:
All these five-star reviews are well deserved.

Having moved to the city not long ago, I was dreading the process of trying to find a decent mechanic, who wouldn't rip me off, for my 1997 BMW 328iC. As far as I was aware nothing major needed doing, but the old girl definitely needed some love, an oil change etc. Based on the plethora of glowing reviews on Yelp for this business, I made an appointment. 

They were able to squeeze me in for the next day, which apparently is unusual as business is booming, since they are building a great reputation and probably get a lot of customers courtesy of Yelp.

As others have mentioned, Tom, the owner, is a great guy. Honest, down-to-earth, no BS and will tell you like it is. He genuinely seems more interested in making sure customers are satisfied than in making a quick buck or nickle-and-diming clients, like so many mechanics tend to do. He gave me some great advice for the HVAC control unit in my car, and with his help plus google, I was able to repair the unit, turning what would have been a $700 repair into a $2 purchase at Radio Shack! 

I also like that Tom is "with it" technologically and responds promptly to emails, which is my preferred form of communication since I'm a computer geek. 

Metric Motors did a full inspection of my car, oil change plus all the other stuff that goes with it, for a very reasonable price. 

This is one of those old-school family businesses that everyone should be supporting. A smiling professional who knows his trade and is out to make a fair wage for doing a good job. As he points it, Tom used to be standing on the other side of the counter so he knows what it feels like to get handed a bill for $1000 for work you barely understand and didn't expect. Now he's on the shopkeeper side of the counter and I'm glad of it!

Mechanic Heros

I can't find my old review here, so this is a re-do. I first found Metric Motors through a co-worker. My 6-year old Audi was being held hostage by the dealer across the street. Royal Motors was claiming I needed a new engine-- even though I only had 50k mi on the odometer. I had just bought the car scarcely 1 year earlier. I had absolutely spoiled it rotten, rarely driving it and washing it only by hand (@Touchless Carwash). So I was a bit ... disbelieving -- when hit-up for a brand new engine. Estimate: $9,000 minimum. My co-worker found me weeping in my office & immediately picked up the phone to call John (former owner) of Metric Motors. John said to bring the car right over, so we picked up the car & drove it across the street. An hour later, John called to let me know one of the valves was loose, something about the pistons & cylinders, but he fixed it, & it would cost $90. That was my total bill. One one-hundredth of the estimate the dealer had given me. I had that $9k estimate printed out in case no one believed me. But in any event, it was the reason I started having my car serviced at Metric Motors. I have never been sorry. Never felt ripped off or short-changed. I am so glad that there are still honest car shops out there. And thanks to Yelp for making consumers aware of the good AND the bad ones out there.

text:
So guess what, Tom's still around and he's still the best in the business. Unfortunately he's not in the shop as much, but he's gone above and beyond to catch up with me and help me out.

I've never made a 180 degree turn around like this, but Tom and Rob reached out and implored me to accept their help. They've been super busy with the shop filling up and trying to expand the business, but didn't use that as an excuse. They slipped up on what is usually phenomenal service, but went above and beyond to make things right.

Here's why Tom, Rob and Metric Motors rock:

1) Communication. This is the best part. Tom spends A TON of extra time making sure you know what's going on with your car. Doctors don't tell you this much about surgeries they're about to perform. Tom first gave me the rundown on the phone of everything it could be and how it works. Then once they had my car and had done the analysis, another call from Tom to let me know everything that was going on, and all of my options. Then, the part that was always my favorite. When you pick up your car, Tom grabs the busted parts from a box and shows them to you. Explains how they're supposed to work. Explains how they're broken. Explains how it happens. Explains how they fixed it. Shows you on your car where they fixed it and what it was. Explains what you can do to keep your car in top shape. You get the idea... For those of us who don't know cars so well, it really really helps to have someone explain it to us so that we understand where our money is going.

2) Honest and Integrity. When you're working with Tom, you can't help but trust him. He gives you all of the information and makes it clear what you can do, what you should do and what you need to do. He's very conscious that these things cost money, and is very good and letting you know what can wait and what can't. There's no better feeling then realizing you can actual trust your mechanic. I trust Tom.

3) Empathy. These guys understand and feel for your needs. For brevity's sake I'll spare a few details here, but Tom understands that it doesn't always make sense to fix everything that's broken. He'll make sure you know about it, but he spends a ton of time laying out your options. There are things that need to be fixed right away, don't leave the shop, but Tom also gives you the breakdown. In all fairness, the staff was very friendly and efficient - they were able to get parts and replace the clutch and flywheel on my Boxster in only 2 days.

HOWEVER...

I bought my car under unusual circumstances (the previous owner had brought it into the shop before deciding to sell). When I bought the car, I was told that the clutch would need to be removed and disassembled in order to determine what was wrong with it. I was also was warned that the flywheel (which is $1200 for the part alone) could possibly also need replacement but that we would only know once the clutch was removed. No problem. The shop tech, Andy, even advised me that we could install a solid or lightweight flywheel instead of the expensive and problematic OEM Porsche DMFW for a significant cost savings. Sounds like they were looking out for my best interests!

But then I got the call from Rob, the shop manager, who told me that both the clutch and flywheel were bad (as well as a few assorted other items) and needed replacement to the tune of an additional $1400. I told Rob what Andy had told me about installing an alternative flywheel, and Rob insisted that he was wrong and that I had no options but to install the $1200 flywheel from Porsche. Out of curiosity, I checked online and found that the part lists for $700-800 on average. I even called another Porsche-specialized shop down the street from Metric, and they quoted me $900 (including their markup!). Now, I understand that mark-ups are how shops stay in business, and I am all for paying talented people to do good work, but $500 in pure profit on ONE part? After bringing up these concerns Metric was only willing to knock $50 off the "list" price they planned on charging me. 

Feeling backed into a corner and knowing I would have to re-pay another shop for the labor to re-do the job with the cheaper part, I reluctantly allowed them to finish. $3100 for a clutch rebuild and new flywheel... OUCH.

On top of all this, the previous owner of my car told me that Metric Motors has serviced it since the day its factory warranty expired. I asked Rob for a list of recent services that had been performed and he told me that this was the first time that this car had been in their shop. After the service was complete, I went home and dug through the paperwork the previous owner had given me...and found 20+ service records from Metric! First time in the shop...Seriously?

I wouldn't exactly say Metric had my back as other Yelpers have experienced.

text:
This is the best auto shop I've ever been to and will be the only shop I visit from now on. The highlights of my experience are:

(1) The shop's owner Tom is incredibly friendly, knowledgeable, outgoing, and helpful. He gave me practical tips for checking my brake rotor thickness and my pads and spent time answering all my questions. 

(2) The rest of the staff, including Rob and the technicians are also just as friendly, knowledgeable, professional and approachable as Tom. 

(3) Without asking, the shop held onto the motor mounts they replaced on my Passat so they could show me why they needed to be replaced. (They do this will all their clients and its such a pleasure, too many times I've had a VW dealership call me up after I've dropped a car off and tell me about all the things they found that needed to be replaced far ahead of schedule and then, even after asking to have them hold onto the old parts, they throw them out.)

(4) The work on my car was done for less than the estimated amount. (Even if the work had been done at the estimated cost, the rate still would have been reasonable and more than competitive as compared to going to a "stealership".)

(5) In addition to the service work performed, my car was thoroughly inspected and I got a plan of what items will need to be serviced in the future and approximately when they expect they will need servicing. 

(6) The shop was outstandingly clean and exuded professionalism.

(7) The oil change that was part of the service was half the cost of what I've spent at quick lube shops for a full synthetic change. 

(8) My car was ready ahead of schedule.

(9) They washed my car, including my difficult to clean wheels, for no extra charge. 

(10) They were gracious when I called to tell them I was running late for my appointment and told me to take my time. 

I have never been to a better mechanic. How often do you get to leave the mechanic and feel great about the experience?

text:
The short story: The 5 stars on their Yelp page here really says it all. Absolutely outstanding customer service.

The longer story: I've been getting most of my services done on my 2005 VW Jetta at the dealership and am frankly fed up. Way too expensive and impersonal. I also really wanted an independent mechanic that I trust and can build a relationship with. A work colleague recommended Metric Motors. I called them up at the last minute hoping to get my car in for a service before leaving on a road trip. I spoke with Tom, telling him I knew it was unlikely that he could take my car the same day but he said he'd get back to me by 9:00 a.m. and let me know one way or another. He called me at 8:59 to tell me he had a client postpone and said he could take my car. I was thrilled. Tom also checked me in when I showed up. He was incredibly personable and helpful. He even showed me how to visually spot-check my brakes to gauge how much life the brake pads had left. 

When the car was done I got a call from Rob, who was equally as personable and helpful. He talked me through the whole diagnostic on my car, told me what service they gave it, what we need to keep an eye on in the future and then said it would be ready for pick-up as soon as they gave it a washing and inside clean-up. (A happy & unexpected surprise!) All in all, he said it was in great shape, which I was relieved to hear.

I think (read: know) I've found my new mechanic!

text:
Atech Auto Repair gets an A- to B+ in my book. I took my boyfriend's 2013 Subaru Crosstrek here some 4 months ago for an oil change. Though the oil change was reasonably priced and the gents running the shop were polite and fast with working on the car, the Crosstrek started acting funny in the months to come... we had a couple of instances where the car at idle would add throttle on its own, or would slow down on the freeway mid drive (even if you were flooring the gas pedal).

We looked around the engine bay to see if there was a leak or anything amiss, but there was nothing obvious.

Fast forward to this past weekend: on the way back from Sacramento, the check oil light came on. We ended up going to an express oil change along the way back (I'll be writing a review for them shortly after this one in case you happen to be in the Vacaville area).

It turns out the car was low on oil and was burning it at an extremely high rate (there was less than a quart circulating in the block). The tech said he didn't see any leaks near the drain plug, but he did notice that the oil filter was a bit loose, which might be the reason why we were burning oil like a kitchen fire.

I'll give Atech another shot in the future since I think they're an honest establishment, but because of the potential flub with the filter, I have to hold on to a star from this review.

P.S. The torque spec for the oil filter on a 2013 Subaru Crosstrek is 32ft-lbs. It's theoretically hand tight, but use a proper torque wrench just in case.

Seeking a second opinion, I randomly called several auto repair shops and fortunately found Hayes Auto Repair. From the moment I spoke with Joe, he was incredibly helpful. He patiently explained the issues with my Prius, guided me through the repair procedures with an illustration, and clearly understood my concerns about the repair cost. He provided a transparent quotation before any work began.

Approximately an hour after I dropped off my car, Joe called to inform me he had identified the problem: a motor attached to the grill shutter. The very next day, my car was fully repaired without needing to replace the entire grill shutter. Hayes Auto Repair fixed my car for less than a quarter of the price quoted by San Francisco Toyota.

I truly felt that Joe treated me with sincerity and professionalism. I am absolutely positive that I will return to Hayes Auto Repair for any future car service needs.

text:
Ladies, if you are looking for an honest and reliable place to get your car worked on, Hayes Auto Repair is it.

All I can say is WOW, WOW, WOW....and add 10 stars more!

Due to covid we decided to go down to one car, which is a 1999 Mazda Miata...or Mazdarati to us. Now that this was to be our primary mode of transport, we decided to address the nonfunctioning driver's side electric window and the worn brakes. It also has some creaks and noises that we never had investigated. We drove it when absolutely necessary, and kept the AAA card handy, just in case. 

I called around to several shops to learn what their process was to diagnose the problems. ALL the other shops I called wanted + $150 just to tell me what was wrong with it. 

Hayes was the only shop that said the diagnostic fee would be put towards the repair. Had it been only mechanical, there would be no fee. Of the 4 phone calls that I made to Hayes in advance of bringing my car in, I was always treated with kindness and patience. 

When I dropped the car off, I let the owner know that I wasn't employed at the moment, and would be happy to go with used parts if that would save us money. We just needed to be sure the car was safe and functional for a year. Joe searched and found the part for half of what a new one would cost. He also explained everything in great detail and even sent photos of everything they found. 

When he called with the full diagnostics and prices, we weren't sure what to get fixed. Joe said "If it was my car, this is what I would get done and why." I felt like my brother was advising me. What a great feeling!

When we went to pick up the car, it was cleaned from top to bottom, including removing the rust from the tire rims. I didn't even recognize my own car! There were many other kind gestures and considerations, but my review is already long enough. I have never been so pleased and relieved. 

Thanks again Joe - we will be back and will tell everyone about your great establishment.

text:
I've known Joe for a very long time...maybe 10 years or so by now, but never on a personal level until recently.

I knew Joe from when he owned Franklin Auto Body in Oakland off of Int'l Blvd because I had always taken my cars to him each time I got into an accident...which seemed to be more often back in my younger years.

He's always done great work so when my brother-in-law needed his Mercedes repaired, I knew exactly who to call. I called Joe on his cellphone and told him I was heading over with the car to get an estimate, and I drove over to his Oakland location just to find out he had sold it.

By this time it was 6 PM (which is when he closes his shop) on a Friday evening so traffic into SF from Oakland was horrendous, but Joe told me that he would wait for me until I arrived. Still the same sweet guy I remember from years back when he was willing to drive me around in his 740 so I can go shopping while my 2005 Pilot was in his shop.

After getting the estimate, my BIL agreed to have Joe do the repair on his car. Joe's place also handles mechanical repairs as well so I asked him to check what the "check engine" light on the Mercedes meant. He checked the code and told me it needed a replacement 2nd air pump something along that line, which he says his guys can't do so he recommended us to a place that does.

The body repair was done very well. I wouldn't even be able to tell that the car was ever damaged. He replaced the right tail light and the back bumper. Painted the driver side of the car as well because someone had keyed the driver door. My BIL wanted to paint just the door, but Joe insisted that if he were to paint just the door, the colors won't be an exact match and it'll just look cheap so he might as well just leave it as is...which I totally agree. Why drive an expensive car just to have one door that doesn't match with the rest of it? So, Joe gave me a great deal and my BIL decided to have the driver side completely repainted. Smart move because it looks great now.

I love the fact that Joe is such an honest guy. He's friendly and easy-going as well.

I also came to find out that he is also my buddy's (Peter P.) neighbor so he asked me to come over to hang out at their houses with them once in a while. LOL

What are the odds that all the best guys I've known from 10 years ago, whom I consider as my close friends know each other? Talk about a small world...

text:
I tried Hayes Auto for an insurance repair after reading the reviews on Yelp. I couldn't have been more pleased with the experience. 

Ask for Joseph. He is a real pro and will work with you during the insurance process to make things go smoothly. He is also really polite, smiles, and shakes your hand -qualities that seem to be phasing out of auto mechanic shops these days. 

There were mostly new imports in the shop - everything from luxury to minivans. 

Joseph gave me a time-line of 7-10 business days to complete the work. Considering that an insurance adjuster wouldn't be out for a few days and 1/2 of the car needed paint, the time-line seemed optimistic. He called me 5 business days later, to tell me that the car was ready. They did a great job. 

My insurance company wanted to replace my fenders, hood, etc. with aftermarket and/or used parts. It's a pretty standard practice, as it can reduce their costs substantially. Still, Hayes worked out the pricing to install new OEM parts at no additional cost. They also fixed some nagging issues while they had the car taken apart. 

I've done a fair amount of work on cars, and dealt with plenty of auto body shops. I can't stress enough the value of the work these guys did. Really above and beyond.

text:
My transmission went out on me when I parked my car on a hill in SF. It would not go in reverse. I was parallel parked and did not know if the car could move forward due to the car in front of me - there was no room to get out without backing up, which I could not do. I called a friend who recommended Hayes Auto Repair. Now I'm recommending them to you.

I called them at once and talked to someone who said that, depending on the repair needed, they might have to send it out to someone else to have it rebuilt. I brought the car in and the owner, Joseph, helped me out. He gave me a verbal estimate - a ball park figure of $2,000 for a used transmission and $2,500 to rebuild mine. He did not recommend a new transmission because my car was only worth about $3,000 in good condition, which it obviously wasn't in. I told him that I might just give the car to charity and he suggested selling it first on Craigslist for maybe $500. He said he would waive the storage fee for a few days until I could figure out what I wanted to do. He said he would work on getting the estimate the next day while I thought about selling it. I decided I would try to sell it rather than pay for the repairs.

I put an ad on Craigslist and had three callers within 5 minutes. I settled on a buyer and decided to meet the buyer at the garage that day at 1 o'clock (the day after my car broke down). Joseph was so cool about it. He wasn't put out about me not repairing the vehicle. He let me use his office to handle the transaction - filling out the DMV change of ownership certificate and Joe even made copies of everything for me. The buyer needed to break a hundred dollar bill and Joseph asked his employees if they had change!! Joe even reminded me to get a copy of the buyer' license. It was like he was a friend that went along with me to make sure everything was cool.

Also, Joseph hooked me up with Hertz for a $25/ day rental car ( a Toyota Corolla) with unlimited mileage.

If this is how they treat non-customers, you can be sure they are going to treat paying customers well. That's what my friend has always experienced with Hayes Auto Repair. I highly recommend them!

text:
I was referred to Hayes Auto Repair by a family member who gave them high marks for their service. I had this horrendous sound coming from my engine and I was fearing the worst that something was wrong with my transmission or something else that would cost a lot of money to repair. So, I brought in my SUV on a Monday morning...Alan, the owner and the mechanic, Terry checked it out and they determined that it was an idler pulley that needed replacing. Terry even brought this stethoscope type instrument and listened to the car (these guys are serious about their stuff)!! Alan went on ahead and ordered the part (of course the place they use didn't have this part in stock). So, instead he had to order the part through another resource. I have to give him credit that he made the effort to get me the less expensive costing part vs. the more expensive part. 

The situation with my SUV was serious enough that he highly recommended that I don't drive my vehicle until the part comes in the shop and I bring it in for repairs (I'd risk the fan belt breaking) and that would cost much more money for those repairs. I really appreciated this fact; and they could have had me drive my car until it broke, have it towed to their shop and then I could have paid 10 times the amount! So, I was out of a car for 3 days but very thankful that I wouldn't have been surprised and stranded with a broken fan belt god knows where.

Alan gives me an estimate of $250 or so in repair costs (I was so relieved to hear this amount). Fast-forward to Friday...I drop off my truck at 8am, I receive a call at 11:30 that my SUV is ready for pick up. Now, in my history of auto repairs (w/dealerships and the like) I wasn't expecting to pick up my vehicle until after 4pm (especially on a Friday). To have it ready before Noon was very impressive. Now, I don't know if installing an idler pulley is as easy as changing oil but I was glad to know that I'd be able to enjoy my weekend. What made this visit to this repair shop even more impressive was the actual cost; it was $150 ($100 less than I'd been quoted). That doesn't happen at all...esp. for me when it comes to repairs. 

I started my vehicle and to my delight it sounded so smooth...I think it even purrs now!

Hayes Auto repair...you will have a return customer, DEFINITELY!!!

[{'id': 'D0C34Ihmbl0YghEbz8g37A', 'text': 'For many years our family business has been known for its high quality service and having our customers' best interest in mind. Unfortunately, there was a misunderstanding in this case.

When we inspected the wiper motor it became clear that copious amounts of leaves had fallen into the drainage areas and had flooded the windshield motor. If the drainage area is poorly maintained then the motor will eventually burn out. Being that this part had to be replaced, our shop looked up the cost from the dealer, which came out to be around $500. Realizing that this was an exorbitant amount, we explained to our customer that she might be able to find the part cheaper online. We allowed her to keep her car in our shop till she found the part herself, even at our own expense of time. Generally the price of leaving your car in our shop is $85 daily, but we were trying to give this customer a hand and let her keep her car in our shop charge free. We feel we tried to do our customer a good deed.

As the owner of Hayes Auto Repair, I am not into selling parts, although selling parts has become the standard of marketing in the automotive industry for many shops. We tell our customers the options available to them and let them decide which path they would be willing to take. Whether it is buying a part online or purchasing it from the dealer directly - which is inherently more reliable - we let our customers make that decision.

In this situation it is important to understand this analogy. You can buy a steak at a restaurant for $5 or you could buy a steak at another restaurant for $15. Are they the same? Of course not. We try to give our customers the best quality service along with access to the best parts available, but we still allow the option of installing a part of lesser quality if so desired. 

In regard to the 8" cracks the customer claims to have come from our work, it is clear to us that she did not fully understand the extent of our work when making this accusation. The work involving the wiper motor has nothing to do with the windshield glass at all. You do not even touch the window for this job. 

Hayes Auto Repair has been a family business for over 50 years, giving honest and high quality work to the community. Our business is known for keeping our customers best interest in mind and going out of our way to help, which has given us our good reputation throughout the Bay Area. We extend our hands out to our customers guiding them through the confusing process of automobile maintenance and reparation - helping them and their cars for the future.', 'author': {'id': '-5nErriWQCpzHq6QuKp_0Q', 'url': 'https://www.yelp.com/user_details?userid=-5nErriWQCpzHq6QuKp_0Q', 'name': 'Alan Y.', 'photo': 'https://s3-media0.fl.yelpcdn.com/buphoto/uYQjruWM4OeM94QSMKoojA/90s.jpg'}, 'timestamp': '2011-09-29 21:54:56'}]

my car is a standing target. park it and someone will try to ram into him. three times in the past four months alone.

mark at hayes went to bat for me and this is how it turned out:

- talked the insurance company into replacing the bumper instead of just painting it
- excellent body work and paint job
- guaranteed that he would negotiate with my insurance to keep me from paying anything other than my deductible
- spot painted a place where a friend had scratched off some paint with a pair of ski's
- recommended that i skip the hood work, since it was a small dent and would incur a whole separate deductible payment

full service, extra perks and great recommendations. 

lucky for them i get hit all the time (heading in again next week, passenger door and rear-view mirror this time). the excellent customer service will surely be paying off in loyalty and recommendations for years to come.

text:
YOU GUYS. YOU GUYS. SERIOUSLY YOU GUYS.

This place ROCKS. I am not a person who is quick to get excited about auto repair. But Hayes Auto is the best.

For starters, they are always honest and helpful. If there is something wrong with your car, you can roll in, they'll take a look at it and give you your options. If you're looking for a cheap fix they'll tell you that too--they don't just give you the $$$ treatment. If it's something quick and easy to fix, don't be surprised if they fix it on the spot and wave you away with a smile. Another test of honesty: I've asked whether a big repair was worth it to do on my car, and they've told me straight up that it wasn't worth it. Are you sure your mechanic would turn down a $2k job if you dangled it in front of his nose?

Second, they do excellent work. Every time. Enough said.

Third, they are friendly. They remember you. They smile at you. None of that gruff stuff here. It's a family owned shop. This stuff matters! Maybe it matters more if you're a girl, I don't know. But it matters a lot to me.

They can do pretty much anything--mechanical work, body work, painting, everything. (Yes, they can fix your Prius!)

I never thought I'd be writing this much on an auto shop review. Just goes to show how good they are--they've inspired me! :-)

Take your car there!

text:
*Please see pictures I have uploaded from Toyota for work that they completed after Masonic Smog wasn't able to complete the work. 

I came to Masonic Smog and Repair for an ABS brake pump and actuator replacement for my Toyota Prius. They had the cheapest quote at $450 to replace the whole Brake pump actuator assembly which was significantly less than what the Toyota dealership quoted. I decided to go with Masonic because of their glowing 4.9 star reviews. They were ok with me bringing in brand new/unopened purchased parts from Toyota. 
On the morning of the appointment, I dropped off all car and parts and was told the job should take 4-5 hours. I get a call later in the afternoon from Masonic saying that they installed the actuator and pump but was having trouble bleeding the brakes. They were only able to bleed the brakes up to 80% and could not bleed the rest... First sign something was not right. So my husband and I go down to Masonic to see what the problem was, the 2 young mechanics tell us they didn't know what was wrong as they have never encountered this issue before while installing brake pump actuator parts. They tells us they want to keep the car overnight and try again in the morning. I was fine with that as long as they completed the job. The next day they said the car was finished but they were only able to install the brake actuator and not the pump. They "suspected" that the pump was defective and told us to go back to Toyota to claim warranty. Something didn't sit right with this so we brought it back to Toyota dealership and they said the only way they can test to see if it's defective is if we paid them to install it. So we had no choice but to fork over the $1250 that Toyota wanted to "test the brake pump". And guess what.. Toyota was able to install the pump and the pump had no defects that Masonic Smog said it did. 
We were fuming now because Masonic Smog was incompetent and blamed the part for being defective when in fact the part was perfectly fine and Toyota had no problem installing it. So we go back to Masonic to confront them about this and the 2 brothers were the most unprofessional mechanics I have ever encountered. They flat out laughed at us and said that Toyota probably gave us a new part. Why would Toyota give us a new part without telling us? That would cost them extra and it definitely would be billed back to Toyota corporation so there would be paperwork. At the end of back and forth arguing, they refused to refund our money saying they completed their job even though I paid them to install the whole assembly not half. These 2 young kids/ mechanics lack integrity and humility. They obviously don't have a lot of experience working with Hybrids or any life experience and customer service skills. Their response to my confrontation showed me that they are untrustworthy and excuses were that of someone that was guilty and deflecting blame on the parts instead of their incompetence. In the end, I had to pay twice to get the job that Masonic Smog couldn't do. They are the worst mechanics both professionally and mechanically!! Stay away from this place if you have real electrical/mechanic work that needs to done because they will deny deny deny any wrong doing even if they are incompetent!!! I've learned my lesson and will try to find a mechanic that has experience, integrity, and trustworthiness. Everything this place ain't...

*Update, the response from Masonic Smog and Repair to my review just proves my case. They flat out LIE and have no ethics! As you can see on my invoice, Toyota only charged for labor, not parts!! Masonic please learn to be honest and take accountability, you'll keep more returning customers that way. During the last confrontation, the 2 brothers did not even bother reading the service invoice while we went to confront them as they already made up their mind that they weren't going to give us a refund for their incompetence!!

text:
After a disappointing experience with a larger local auto shop that seemed more focused on profit than service, I decided to switch mechanics on the recommendation of my barber and tried Eddy's shop.

Eddy's operates a smaller, more personalized garage where he and another mechanic, both skilled in European cars among others, work directly on the vehicles. I took my Mercedes C350 to Eddy for a thorough inspection to ensure its reliability for long road trips. He conducted diagnostics and maintenance, holding the car for two days, and while he pointed out some additional issues that needed attention, he assured me it was road-trip ready.

Recently, when my car displayed warnings for the ABS system and check engine light, Eddy promptly addressed these. One issue was the intake manifold, which he had previously mentioned might need replacing. Throughout the repair process, Eddy was communicative, providing updates and a clear quote. He took extra time with the car to guarantee its safety before returning it.

I'm now completely satisfied with the condition of my car and with Eddy's honest, thorough, and friendly service. It's refreshing to find a mechanic who truly cares about the quality of his work and his customers' safety, rather than just the bottom line. I fully trust Eddy with my car and won't consider going anywhere else.

Thank you, Eddy, for your exceptional service!

text:
I've been to a lot of mechanics in a 5+ cities with as many different cars. Out of all of them, K&C is far and away the best.

Drop off your car and a short while later, the owner will call with a full rundown of each and every issue, its exact impact on the function of the vehicle, exactly which issues need to be fixed vs. what you can get away with not fixing, and the pricing for each potential repair. text:
My entire reason for coming here is quite comical, so I will tell you that and then RAVE RAVE RAVE about the wonderful customer service and helpful employees! 

It's a Thursday and I am oh so excited to finally be out of my crappy house in the Sunset. I finish packing my car and run in to drive away. I started off, drove a few blocks and realized... oh no, I know this feeling... but I know that I have not hit any curbs recently!!!!!! So I pull over on Moraga st and 37th. I get out of my car and what do I see?!?!?!? OH MY MOTHA EFFING, someone has stolen my tire, but nicely enough replaced it with their donought, a broken donought. Not sure if that's really nice, but I guess better than no tire???? So some nice police stop to help me... we are all laughing by now... and I realize I'm going to Vegas tomorrow... screw it ill come back.

So I get back from Vegas and look online for a good tire store (I have had 3 tires replaced since living in SF, I hit a lot of curbs I guess) and who came up with great reviews?? DUH Sunset 76! Plus I realized that it was not far. I found out that my insurance would not cover buying a new tire but would pay for a tow. Screw that!!! Waiting and then having to talk to some creepy guy while he takes my car away (happened last time and then gave me a recipt on the back of a business card so insurance never refunded me). So I call Sunset 76 and say... 

"Honestly, I know nothing about cars ... (explain my situation)... Can I drive on this broken spare 10 blocks?? It's not my tire so I don't care"

He says Yes, so I hop in my car praying that it makes it up the hill 10 blocks. 

I arrive, laughing about the horrible noise the way up and the fact that no one tried to stop me and let me know my tire was flat... hahah.

I explain my situation and he of course laughs. So I let him know that I'm broke and can not really afford to buy a new tire. Then he lets me know that I also have to buy a rim too.... OOH MAN!!!!! 

But they are so nice that they went out and found me a used rim and tire. Then I told my dad about how great it was and that I was getting a used tire. He says... NONONO, that is not safe, you must have a new one!

So I again call and ask, if they had gone through a lot of trouble finding me a used tire because after speaking with my father, it was clearly not the one he wanted. (it is his car, I guess) They said no problem and it was finished that night.

These guys are super nice and helpful. I highly recommend you to them, and take if from a girl that has gone to most tire shops in the hood and they are for sure the best!

Thanks guys, it runs like a champ!!!!!! And you did not break my bank!!!!!

text:
I wonder if all these posts are real or doctored. My experience is totally reverse to what others say. What I am telling down are facts which I can support with receipts.

I got two jobs done at this shop on my MB 300E. They advertised 107 dollars for transmission oil change, I thought of getting it done. They charged me 193 dollars (mileage 104,620). O.K. no problem so far as MB parts may be costlier, I thought. Within 15 days or 375 miles of driving the transmission oil started leaking. Ultimately the leak became a drip and I took the car back to them mileage 105, 014). The owner flatly refused to Honor the guarantee taking the plea that it was a Saturday and as I wanted the job to be done the same day, he could not get the proper parts. The owner was foul mouthed and was giving ridiculous explanations such as I was looking at the car from a distance and the mechanic was nervous, I insisted to get the job done on a Saturday hence no original parts etc. etc. After a lot of haggling and looking at the way the oil was dripping (I think he realized that even the worst part wouldn't drip like that if job was done properly.) he agreed to do the job on the condition if I paid for the parts. He did the job and I paid for the parts. Same parts, I repeat same parts which he had put in the first instance, but the job done with care, hence no leakage at least so far!!! The worst was yet to come. A few days later, the transmission started behaving erratically and I had to get it examined. The transmission oil level was too high. I wrote an e-mail to them asking as to why they charged me twice for the same parts. To date no reply!!!

Earlier in May last year, with the mileage at 102,876, I got a check engine light and I went to this shop. They found that the O2 sensor was bad and needed to be replaced. I gave the go ahead, they did the job and I paid $ 273. Fine. Last week, at 108,1xx there was again the same problem. The O2 sensor didn't survive even for 6,000 guaranteed miles ( I have the receipt). I preferred not to take the car to them and got the job done somewhere else, knowing fully well by now that they will never agree to their fault of not doing the job properly. Instead of facing an arrogant owner I preferred to spend my hard earned money.

The problems that cause the need for a mechanic aside, Louis & crew are the best.

I had developed a small oil leak and needed to figure out where it was coming from. It could have been simple or maybe more complex and would need a bit of time to fix. I live on the other side of town, and called to explain my situation and if it was possible to make an appointment to first figure out what was going on, and if they needed the car for a while I would make another appointment and come back after making arrangements with friend to follow and get me back and forth while they worked on car. We looked at schedules and we agreed on 10 am the next day.

Got there exactly at 10, and the fellow who was checking me in made it seem like I had just showed up out of hand. I explained that I had appointment for 10 and we were just going to do a quick look to see what was up. The guy was pretty much completely ignoring me and asked me to fill out sheet, with name and number. Again I told him I was there for a 10am appointment. He asked for keys and instead of pulling into open bay he parked my car with a bunch of others, and then told me they would call me an hour or two. I explained that no, I specifically made an appointment so that this would not be the case. I wish I could do a better job of explaining at how he clearly did not give a damn about what I was saying. I guess I could have been calmed down with an explanation of a communication error, or he could have called over Lou, who is the guy I spoke to and tried to reschedule. BUT his attitude was totally unacceptable. I left in a huff and will not return.

So if you live close or your schedule works out I can't attest to their current level of competency or pricing etc. But whoever that guy is, my guess the manager of some kind, has the kind of attitude that I choose not to do business with, and hope you have better luck than I did.

text:

After taking a look at each tire they told me it wasn't necessary yet to replace the other three and, when the time comes, they can sell me three new ones. 
I decided to just get the flat replaced, and they said it would be about an hour. I went to a nearby coffee shop to get some work done and got the call that it was ready just over an hour later. When I got there the car was out front, ready to go, and they had even reassembled the mess of housing and storage compartments around the spare after they returned it to its spot. Professional and friendly service (and price) earned them my tire biz going forward.

text:
I've been trying to hold back on this review as I was trying to give Lou the benefit of the doubt. Called him and left him a message about a week ago and the guy never returned my call, so here we are.

Dropped off my 2004 Volvo(17 year old car) here around 3/6 and stated on the form that there were 3 possible problems with my car: Speed wouldn't surpass 20mph uphill, idling rpm, and brake issues. He gave me a call and said I needed a new electro throttle unit, which would cost about ~350$ plus labor. I said that's fine, just get it done. A couple days later he calls me and says the part he ordered didn't fit and he needed to get one from the dealership which would cost ~600$-700$(1st red flag). I responded saying that is fine again, just get it done asap cause I need the car. Pick up the car and paid the man ~970$. I grab my car just to find an empty coffee cup that was left in my car (2nd red flag) and proceeded to run errands. As I am driving I find that the RMP is still idling and that the problems wasn't fixed, I go back the same day and drop my car off for another 3 days. While I am there I see Lou disputing with another customer about him installing the wrong set of tires (Stuart's review, 3rd red flag)

He calls me and tells me that it would be another 3 hours of labor to fix the idling RPM as I have a vacuum leak on my car. Frustrated and angry, I still tell him to fix it for me. I pick up the car a couple days later and he did me a favor charging me only for 2 hours labor, which was ~350$.

I drove the car for 5 days afterwards and the timing belt snaps and the engine is completely destroyed. My question here for Lou is why wasn't the timing belt brought up when you did you diagnosis, as you are the expert, not me. If he had told me that I would need all that work done I would have just junked the car and bought a new one. Why haven't you returned my cars in the last two weeks? This is too many coincidences for this to be an accident and I am speculating that this owner is praying on unsuspecting victims because of the high cost of living in SF. If anyone else has had similar issues like mine, feel free to send me a message and I would be glad to report this to the BAR or BBB.

text:
ROBBED BY A TECH

I came here for an oil change based on the overwhelmingly positive reviews here on yelp. I am a delivery driver and receive a fair amount of direct tips in cash. This cash often finds it's way into my center console during a shift, and sometimes gets left overnight. 

The day I had my oil changed here I'd had around 80-100 dollars in my center console, including a crispy 50$ and even a 2$ bill. Having sort of forgotten about it, I didn't think anything of it until the next day when I was going to clean out the center console after my shift. The money was gone.

Having dealt with theft repeatedly since moving to SF I was beside myself. I couldn't believe this had happened again. My cars have been broken into several times and one was even stolen in the last year from in front of my house. This, however, did not have the feel of a break-in. text:
[UPDATE 6/26]: It looks like they really do care about their customers and they really are pleasant people (like I said below). Louis (who I believe is the owner) messaged me right away to make things right. My intent was to merely write down my experiences and to not actually try to get something out of all of this. In fact, I already had an appointment with another nearby place. But he offered to take me today and get my car serviced. He tells me that the person I've been talking to isn't a mechanic and is new. I usually do my own oil changes but didn't want to mess with it this time so I'm going in today to get my car serviced and I'll update on how that goes later today. But so far, Thanks, Louis for trying to make it right. I love supporting small business owners and my faith in humanity has been restored. 

---------------------------
I came here a little bit over a week ago to get gas. I asked them how much an oil change and a tire rotation would be. They quoted me "around $75" so that was great! I asked if they could take me right then at that moment. They said no because they were busy already so I said can I make an appointment and they said "of course" and that they actually have an online scheduling system. 

So I go home, make an appointment for that Tuesday at 3:30. No response. No confirmation. Tuesday came and went so I went back online and made another appointment for 3:30 on Thursday. No response. No confirmation. 

I give them the benefit of the doubt and I actually go in myself on Friday to make an appointment. I tell the guy how about 3:30 next Tuesday. He says 'ok'. I ask him to invite me to the google calendar appointment and then he says 'ok'. I get home only to find that the invite was made for 3:30pm for Monday. 

I call in today (Monday) to ask them if they can correct the appointment to the correct day. They say, it's already booked up. Then this conversation happens: 

Me: "Alright, then I guess I can just try to come in today. You said that the oil change and the tire rotation would only take 30 minutes anyway."
Mechanic: "We're busy today."
Me: "Right. I have an appointment though. But since I'm trying to make this work I might be 5 minutes late."
Mechanic: "We close at 4:30."
Me: "So if I come there by 3:35 and the servicing only takes half an hour that should be enough time." 
Mechanic: "But we're busy and we close at 4:30."
Me: "You're 'busy' because I have an appointment with you. I'm one of the reasons you're booked up today." 
Mechanic: "Ok. but we close at 4:30."
Me: ...
Mechanic: "So.....yeah..."
Me: "...Nevermind. We're just talking in circles here. I'll just go somewhere else."

So, needless to say, I won't be going here ever again. Which is a shame because it's only a couple of blocks from me. My in-person interactions with everyone here has been pleasant. They all seem very nice. BUT there just has to be a better way of handling customers. I don't get how he thought it was even confusing. I guess I'm just glad that he's not working on my car anymore.

text:
A good friend of mine recommended this place. So I made an appointment online for Saturday morning. I came in yesterday, parked my car and soon I was being helped. This was my very first time here. The guy at the front counter asked to sign a paperwork upfront for the job that will be fine; oil change & vehicle inspection. I told him I forgot to print out the discount coupon for new customer. He said that he had no idea there was such coupon and told me to talk to AJ. I did and AJ was great! He was kind and friendly; he printed out the coupon for me right there when I told him that I forgot to print out the coupon. AJ said; "ah, don't worry, I'll print it out for you." Thank you so much, AJ! You're awesome! 
However when the service was done, and the guy at the counter (his name is Greg) called me to pay; I handed him the coupon. He said the bill was $78, the coupon printed out from their website was $31.78 for oil change, filter change and vehicle inspection. When I handed Greg the coupon, without even bother reading the coupon, he said; oh no, with your vehicle (Audi), there's no discount. 
Then I told him and point out that the discount coupon is for "new customer", and he said, oh, OK. So finally let me paid the amount said in the coupon. I feel like Greg is a bit dishonest and bit rude. He told me to go to a cafe and come back. No, I'll wait. He then told to wait on the front then. Ok. But why? Why would he told me that when he allowed three other customers (Asian guys) waited for their car when the technician was working on theirs? Greg himself is Asian, he said nothing to those guys. When I sat on the front as Greg told me to, I couldn't help but hearing everything that was going on when customers come and paid. One lady customer who came previously to pay; I overheard Greg told her that her bill was $97. She had a coupon, too and Greg was super friendly with her (she's Caucasian) and told her that her bill was only $25. Wow! I don't know what service she had. She came back from the same cafe that Greg was telling me earlier. Greg wasn't even made a fuss about the coupon she has. He seemed to know her well since he's super friendly. That's pretty steep discount, I must say, and yet, he made a fuss with my $31.78 coupon that his colleague AJ printed for me. Oh well. Greg is ok, just seems a bit dishonest to me. And he's happy when I paid cash. Of course.
Five stars for AJ all the way! 3 stars for Greg. 4 stars overall. Could have been solid 5 stars -- not so good first impression by Greg's attitude. I still recommend this place. Just be cautious dealing with Greg. That's the negative side. Will I come back? Maybe.

Don't risk your life or your that of your family's. Go somewhere reputable or get a referral from friend/co-worker. Whatever you do, DO NOT let these people near your car.

text:
Louie, the owner, has been my car mechanic for years, and I have nothing but praise for him. He is the most honest and trustworthy mechanic I've ever used. 

Because I had serious problems with my car overheating while driving down the freeway on the Peninsula, I had my car towed to a mechanic at the nearest freeway exit. After the mechanic looked at it over and over, ultimately, charging me thousands -- yes, thousands, you read that right-- for a variety of additional problems he said I had with my car, this other mechanic never fixed the original issue, which was that it was overheating. 

I ended up taking my car to Louie for him to look at it. Granted, he found the problem with the cooling system difficult to pinpoint, and it took him a few days to figure it out, but he ended up fixing it for a modest charge and it has been running great ever since, with the temperature gauge right where it should be.

The only reason I didn't have it towed to Louie initially was that I didn't want to pay the extra towing charge to bring it all the way back to San Francisco. However, I should have done it, because my car would have gotten fixed way sooner and for way less money than I ended up shelling out to that (unscrupulous?) mechanic on the Peninsula.

text:
I bought a set of new tires and needed a place to mount them. After looking through all the reviews on Yelp, I decided to give this shop a try. Making an appointment was a piece of cake. I scheduled the appointment on their website and received a confirmation email the next morning. I picked early weekday morning just to avoid rush and people tend to be nicer in the morning. I'd never schedule an appointment right before they close. Always put your feet into their shoes.

On the day of the appointment, I got there at exactly at 9am and had no clue of where to go. I asked a staff for direction and he pointed me to the office to fill out paperwork. After that, I gave them my key and was told it would take approx. 1 to 1.5 hour. They even mentioned the price beforehand. After roaming on the street for almost an hour, I went back there to check it out. My car was still up in the air and they were working on the 4th tire. 10 minutes later, I was on my way home. 

The bill came out to be $100 ($25 per tire), including disposal and balancing. I expected it would take them 3-4 hours to do it and turned out to be just an hour. Boy, that was quick. I give them 5-star for tire service. 

Pros:
Friendly staff
Fair price
No hard selling
Fast service

Cons:
No waiting room (at least I didn't see it)
Poor directional signage

text:
This place rubbed me the wrong way. Maybe it was just my experience. I brought my car in for a oil change and saw that they had good reviews and the appointment making process seemed easy. I can pretty much get next day appointments. I had a check engine light also so I wanted them to take a look at it for my second visit. So in total I probably made about 3 visits. 

My first oil change went smoothly without a hitch. The total was like $39 bucks which made me super excited to go back to them because normally I pay about $70 since my car "supposedly" only takes synthetic oil. So you can only imagine how stoked I was to get a oil change for almost half the price. 

Then I came back a second time and this time I also had a check engine light on (I don't think this had to do with their oil change but just coincidental). So I decided to have them give me an oil change and to check my engine light since they do diagnostics for free. When I got my car back they said something was wrong with my electrical something something I don't really know and that I had to make a weekday appointment to get that fixed so I was like okay fine. I went and paid for my oil change and made a comment with the cashier lady that it's awesome that they charge so little for a synthetic oil change and she was like "you didn't get synthetic oil, it was just a regular oil change." I didn't know what to say at that moment. I was thinking don't they usually check based on your car and etc and etc to determine what type of oil to use. So then she asked a mechanic to come over to speak with me because I wasn't sure how this will affect my car since I have always been using synthetic. HE DIDN'T KNOW THE ANSWER TO MY CONCERN! I was shocked since I am used to oil change stations telling me that my car needs synthetic oil (I've been to a few such as Pep Boys, Jiffy Lube, and Sunset Service). The mechanic offer me know reassurance that the fact he put regular oil vs synthetic oil to my car would be okay. And he returned the question by asking me "oh your car takes synthetic oil?" Well I guess my fault for assuming that they would know this better than me. But stupid me already made an appointment for them to check my check engine light issue so I came back a third time. I brought it back to them the next day and they fixed it which cost me about $370. The light came back a few days later but will go off and then came back again. 

Lesson learned. I just went back to my regular mechanic and oil change station even though their hours weren't as convenient. They fixed it and I never saw the light again and I'm back to my $70 oil change. Sunset 76 you can stop emailing me reminders...

text:
I've had a really positive experience with Sunset 76 in the past but my last visit made me think a little differently. 

I've had three oil changes here total at Sunset 76 as well as oil changes at two other shops. Now, I may not know a lot about cars, but I do know about my own car, which takes 4 quarts of full synthetic oil. 

During my last visit, I came here to pick up my car after an oil change and the girl working at the front said it came out to $68, which I was a little surprised by. I tried to remember if my last oil change there was that much, but I just signed it and took my car, which was dumb on my part. If I looked at the receipt more carefully I would've noticed that they charged me for 5 quarts instead of 4. I compared the receipt to all my other receipts and every oil change I've ever gotten, I was charged for 4 quarts, even during my last two visits at Sunset 76. Not sure why there was that inconsistency. Maybe the guy who took my car saw a female car owner he thought he could hussle (which unfortunately for me he kind of did). Or maybe it was just an inexperienced mechanic who did my oil change?

Either way, $9 was not enough for me to go back to argue about. The location is also really convenient for me so I'm not sure if I will ban this place, but if I do decide to come back, I will NOT let them overcharge me again.

text:
Dear. Mr. Louis Bateh,

I've been here several times before without a problem, but this time I was really disappointed. I think the recent good yelp reviews have caused Sunset 76 repair to get busy and not need us regular customers anymore because I have to now make an appointment 1 week in the future to get repaired. How am I supposed to know when my car breaks down? Also the website is super difficult to find out how to make an appointment. I've never been able to figure it out. They won't make one for me when I'm there in person and that sucks. I can go to the Honda Service Center on 9th and Irving and either call or do it online easily so that's where I'll be going. 

First Repair: I came here about a month ago for my battery. They checked it out and told me it just had a low charge and charged me $25. I had also asked them to check the radio that wasn't working and they said it was a bad wiring and they couldn't fix that. OK. A few days later, my car battery dies again. Well, I don't have the money or time because I'm getting my Master's degree in Nursing on Monday and have a lot of finals/projects/papers to do so I've been getting around on bus and with my husband's car (luckily he works for Google and the shuttle picks him up close by). So because the problem didn't get resolved the first time, I had to come back at some point. My car has been in the garage for a few weeks until I can got a chance to take it in. That day was today.

My battery had died so my husband jumped it for me. And guess what? The radio magically worked again! Sunset 76 told me it was bad wiring so I guess they were wrong not just about the battery but also the radio. Since it doesn't restart without a jump, I needed it to get checked out since they are just a few blocks away from me and have always accommodated me and I figured just a simple repair like a new batter (I would have happily purchased the parts or called AAA to do their battery service for me. I showed up at 7:15 AM, park my car in an open space, and turn it off because I assume they've always helped me and what else would I have known to do? You don't walk away from a running car! I come up to the window and let the guy know my car needs to be checked and he tells me that he can't today because they are booked. So I ask for tomorrow and he says I need to make an appointment for next week because they are sooo busy. I asked how do I do that. He tells me to go on the website and doesn't even give me a card, I had to ask for one. I said that my car was parked on the lot and won't re-start and he starts yelling at me telling me I shouldn't have done that. How was I supposed to know? I've done that about the last half a dozen times I've been there with my 2 cars. So he tells me he can have it towed. Well, I have no choice but to take my business elsewhere at this point. So I called AAA to tow it to the Honda Center on 9th and Irving since Sunset 76 obviously doesn't need my business and doesn't care to be polite to their regular customers. I think from now on I'll just get my oil changes at the Honda Center and not have to deal with rude mechanics.

text:
This review is long overdue.

I had lived a couple of blocks away from Sunset 76 for about a year. I'd stopped there pretty often to get gas for my way-too-ancient Toyota Corolla, but I'd never really thought about them for any kind of auto service, mostly because during that time my car had never really needed anything.

But road trips to Seattle, Salt Lake, and Yosemite and a pretty grueling commute had started to take their toll on my old little car. It began to make some grinding noises and a light or two started going on inside, and, well, it just started to become time to get it checked out.

I was kinda leery about taking my car into a mechanic. I'm not from SF and I didn't really know anyone reliable and I'd heard horror stories about hugely inflated repair bills. But Sunset 76 was right around the corner so I gave them a try and waited a little nervously for them to let me know what was up. 

They did FANTASTIC work. They explained exactly what was wrong and told me what I needed to be done immediately and what could be deferred. Their price was actually a good amount lower than I had expected!

A few months later, I decided to drive this Corolla of mine to New York City, and given the age of the car, I was a little apprehensive. I took it in to these guys again. They looked it over, made a few adjustments, and Louis, the manager, took me out to the car to show me IN DETAIL what issues there were. They could have charged me a fair amount of money for this service, but they didn't. When I still had some concerns a few days later, they took it in AT NO CHARGE, looked it over, and again made some minor tweaks. It'll be good to go, they said, and a day or two later I headed east.

My 18-year old beater car ended up making it across the United States just fine thanks to Sunset 76's awesome work. I can't recommend them enough - if you're anywhere in SF, they should be the first place you go for any kind of car repair, service, or even just to fill up your tank.

text:
Sunset 76 Auto Repair has a convenient location, we are happy with the auto repair service, but because of difficulty communicating with the business we go out of our way to use other locations. 

Towed one of our vehicles over unannounced on a couple occasions, and brought it by without appointment for follow-up service. Had a positive experience. The shop made time to look over the vehicle and getting it back on the road in a reasonable time frame.

Based on the good-will I submitted email requesting quote for routine maintenance planned for our other vehicle. Did not receive a response. 

Our initial vehicle broke down again and we had no trouble coming in-person unannounced for service. Began assuming that coming in-person or calling ahead was the best way to make contact with the shop. 

After some weeks had passed decided to forgo the quote and just set appointment to bring in the vehicle. Called by phone and spoke with an associate who scheduled an appointment for the service. Due to working hours we agreed I could bring the vehicle in during the evening and they would take a look at it the following day. 

On arriving at the scheduled time to drop off the vehicle we were greeted by a gentleman who turned us away then brusquely informed us that all appointments must be submitted through email. Based on prior experience without response to email we began to feel jerked around.

We looked at other locations to service both vehicles. 

Sunset 76 is a shop I've been happy with but would like to see them focus on responding to emails within timely manner, and providing a follow-up call to the customer to modify appointment time if situations change. I'm curious what the 95% 1-day response to quotes illustrated on Yelp is based on given the difficulties we experienced communicating with the shop. 

It's possible the shop was unusually busy at that time and we had poor timing. The inconvenience made it feel like less effort to reach out and build relationship with other shops than to continue trying to schedule appointments here, thus are unlikely to return.

text:
Amazing experience at this service shop. I was glad I could quickly schedule an appointment online. During my visit, the woman at the service desk was courteous and helpful. She took my name and car key and I was ready to wander off to a coffee shop while they completed the work. It only took about forty minutes for me to receive a call from her to notify me the work was complete.

So now the moment my experience went from normal to amazing. My car had been making an awful screeching noise on startup for months. I was loath to take it into a mechanic shop for the issue, because well I hate mechanic shops and the noise would eventually cease after a few seconds of driving anyway. When I returned to pick up my car, I was informed that the technician that performed my tire rotation and balancing also fixed the screeching serpentine belt that he noticed on startup. The technician informed me that there would be no extra charge for the service and that the issue was due to the belt being a bit loose (I had it replaced several months ago elsewhere) and that it tends to happen to new belts after they stretch out a bit over the course of regular use.

AMAZING. Not only did he fix the problem, he gave me crucial information for the future! For free! I felt compelled to leave a tip. Great work, great people. Thanks, Sunset 76 on Noriega.

text:
Randomly stopped to get gas and then randomly decided to ask about a smog check. My car is an older model Acura and I was already freaking out that it wouldn't pass smog and then be given the run around about what needed to be "fixed" if I wanted to pass smog. I was assisted with less than a 3 minute wait, even though they looked really busy.

Van ran a test and gave me some instructions as he could tell that I had recently had to jump start my car. He told me to come back the next day after completing the instructions. He didn't even charge me for this test! So the next day, of course I had to call to clarify some of the instructions because I'm just not good with all this car stuff lol and he was so nice and explained it all to me again-I finished the instructions and went back in and was assisted again right away-eventhough they were very busy. Van was so helpful and he saw I had my toddler with me and told me to just take care of her and he'd complete the test. He finished in less than 5 minutes and pulled my car up to the front for me (He must've known it would be hard for me to back up out of that tiny area lol). Would definitely recommend-as Van was courteous, very knowledgeable and confident with his diagnosis and instructions. I haven't met may auto mechanics where I feel that they're not lying to me about something LOL. I've only met one other mechanic like that so Van is definitely one that gives off a good vibe and doesn't try to do mechanic talk on the customer! He patiently explained everything and I was so happy I passed smog-honestly, he saved me a lot of hassle and I'm truly grateful. 

He also gets bonus points for knowing the obscure type of music I was listening to in the car-so seriously, if your mechanic knows New Wave, he's a keeper! LOL Van, stop working so hard, and go to the concert-how often are CC Catch and Bad Boys Blue going to be here in SF?!https://www.facebook.com/events/1727097827519374/ :)

text:
PREFACE: I experienced THREE issues with the shop in the only THREE times I've used their services. I am writing this review as a member of the outer sunset community, and I am appalled that this place in my neighborhood writes on their receipts, "serving the community with integrity". Bullshit.

1. I go here to get a simple oil change on my car about a year back. They tell me there's a problem with my oil tank and it needs to be replaced, costing over $1K. That was the last time I'm going here for anything. I am super hesitant to write this review and potentially affect a small business, but the service level I have received from this place in unacceptable. The owner seemed like a really nice guy too, which makes me feel horrible about this, but the employees not fully completing a task or taking advantage of customers will hurt the business.

Lesson learned: Go outside of the city to get your car worked on.
