Quite simply, this shop's Yelp rating is misleading. These guys do sloppy work with nonexistent customer service. I would recommend going anywhere else and I will not be returning.

I went to this place two weeks ago. I opted not to goto my usual shop (San Bruno) as I felt it was convenient to try a place in the Sunset. I just needed to have a new set of tires mounted and balanced. Easy enough right?

I was told it would be an hour and a half. Two and a half hours later I picked up my car. I was told my total was $100. When asked about using their Yelp deal the cashier coldly stated, "...uh... You could... But... Uh... We don't make much money on the tire jobs. Your total is $100," WTF? 

ON TO THEIR SLOPPY WORK: Later that night I had an odd feeling something was off. I checked my tire pressure and found the following:

Tire 1: 40.9
Tire 2: 40.0
Tire 3: 39.0
Tire 4: 34.0 (the guy also did not put the valve cover back on either, THANKS!)

Yes, I checked these values two more times with another gauge and received the same results. What the hell happened?

Mind you, these are stock OEM wheels which are recommended to have a pressure of 30.0 to 32.0 psi give or take one a psi. Overinflation makes your tires more prone to a flat or an accident, causes a rough ride, and at the very least can lead to expedited wear on your tires.

This shop either had no idea what they were doing, were in a rush, simply didn't care, or all of the above. It's inexcusable. I would be terrified to let these guys touch my car again and would recommend against letting these guys touch your engine.

[{'id': 'xqqeTYLbuhp98dkdZB_dSQ', 'text': 'I think i may have found my new car maintenance home sweet home. Everything reviewers said about this place was true. They're very professional but at the same time treat you like a friend, explaining everything to you (and they're super reasonable priced to boot)! I never write reviews, but i really enjoyed how easy this was that it really warrants a review. 

I originally made an appointment to have a smog check ($40ish!) and an oil change ($30ish). Additionally I had asked about having the throttle body cleaned. I had grabbed the yelp deal before coming over ($60 credit for $50) and dropping it off. Came back in an hr and a half to the car smogged and oil changed. They mentioned that they didn't do the throttle body clean because it's an electronic throttle body (and they only do the mechanical ones).

Now 1st off, i want to say up front that i know that the throttle body can be not that difficult to clean...even with what people say, most forums and such just say to move the butterfly valve manually with something softish and clean it as best you can on your own. But i've also heard various ways in which you can also cause yourself problems (assuming you're doing this without removing the actual throttle body). That being said there's several reasons why i appreciated this experience.

1) Ease of appointment and drop off - took me 5 min to make an appointment, 5 min to call them the day after for confirmation (turned out that was my fault since the confirmation got filtered into my spam email), and 5 min to drop off the car.

2) Price - for the city, $60 out the door for a smog check is considered good. $40 is pretty much unheard of even for the suburbs! My parents live in a more suburban part of ventura county and even they pay at least $60 for a smog

3) Conservative in their Work - This is a personal preference, though you may differ if you know cars really well. In general though, I'd rather have a conservative mechanic than one who thinks they can do something and either a) screws something up at the time or worse yet, b) slightly messes something up that will have a larger impact on the car later - i don't mind having them telling me they don't clean electronic throttle bodies...because they explained why...which leads to #4

4) Patience & Explanation (Customer Care) - This is what really made them shine for me. They didn't try to sell me anything, but they made sure to explain why they didn't clean the throttle body. One of the mechanics actually even brought over another car's electronic throttle body to show me why he can't get the butterfly to open manually and why they don't try to clean it if it's electronic (only on ones with a manual trigger). He was patient and, on the contrary to trying to sell me something, actually seemed a bit appalled when i asked how much it would cost to replace if it failed entirely. Then he explained a new part was around $1800 easily and a junk yard one was $500-800ish. He even took the time to tell me that even if it did fail, it usually can run up to 20-35 mph because of a fail safe built into most throttle bodies (aka, as he put it "you can limp to a garage or safe place at least" haha). I love that he gave extra attention and time. Not once did he try to sell me anything nor did he get impatient or act like i was bothering him with all these questions (and let me tell you, it's not like they weren't busy - there were at least 10 cars there and like 3 or 4 technicians). 

Overall, I can't stress enough that I definitely want to go back to this place and meet/work with these people again. text:
This place is legit.

I had been in dire need of an oil change. My car was telling me that I was at 5% oil life for the longest time, which I ignored. It wasn't until I was at negative oil life mileage did I really start paying attention. So now, the dilemma was this: where could I get an oil change done by 8 AM so I could make it to work on time? Enter Sunset 76.

I found Sunset 76 on Yelp, but I was saddened by their 8 AM opening time. Did I really have to come on a weekend morning? I held my breath as I emailed Louie asking if there was any way I could get an oil change earlier. Imagine my surprise when I got a reply, saying he would open a half hour early to accomodate my schedule! Now, THAT is good customer service.

I drove up to the station at 7:30 AM and was greeted by Francisco, who proclaimed, "We've been waiting for you!" like I was family or something. Oil change family, I suppose. Louie took my car and I sat in the "waiting room". I showed Francisco the $23.76 oil change coupon from their website and a moment later, Louie walks in, exclaiming, "We don't take coupons in the morning," before cracking a smile and adding, "Just messing with you". Hehe. At 7:45 AM, I was back in my car. Great people, great service.

Did I mention you can get gas here?

text:
This was the first time I needed an oil change since moving to SF where I didn't need to get anything else done on my car (not that I'm complaining), so decided to go someplace other than a dealership. When I used to get oil changes when I lived in AZ there were several places that did it for under 20 bucks so I was a little shocked to find that this was pretty much impossible to find up here (about $40 is what I found to be standard). I saw this place had a $25 coupon on yelp so I decided to give it a try.

So here's the deal. I kind of wanna give this place only three stars, but at the end of the day they were quick and with the coupon they were cheap (interestingly though the coupon I had was good until the end of the month and here I am writing this review eight days before it expires and I noticed they've pulled the coupon from yelp...weird). 

I actually called this place on a Friday and I asked if I could come in around 5 o'clock that day and they told me "no problem," but when I got there, they told me they were too backed up. I didn't complain though. I figured I'd come back the following week. I called again the following Wednesday (told them the same time, got the same "no problem" response), but when I got there I got the same "we're backed up" answer. However, before I said anything, one of the employees said he'd squeeze me in. Great. 

I was told it would be about 30-35 min., which was fine. They don't have any sort of waiting area, so I just went to a coffee shop down the street, and came back a little over 20 min later and my car was finished. I paid, and left. No problems. 

If this place had another coupon I'd come back (I'm not sure what the regular price is for an oil change), but honestly if a place close to my house did oil changes at the same price, I'd probably just go there, because I don't live all that close to the Sunset. If I did live in the Sunset, I'd have no problem coming back here though.

text:
I would give 15 stars to Sunset 76 if I could. Having a new old car after being carless for my whole adult life is ridiculously stressful. Is that rattling noise a problem? Are my brakes really ok? I'm 400 miles past where I should be for an oil change - will my engine explode? Thank goodness for Louis at Sunset 76, and thanks, Yelpers, for getting me here! 

First of all, I bring them the car right after my introductory Route 66 road trip, having been told by my dad that I should get the brakes checked out as soon as I get back to SF. I explain this to Louis, who checks them out, tells me that everything's fine, and doesn't charge me a cent. A couple of months later, the day before my next road trip, I realize that I'm way overdue for an oil change and rush, panicking, to Sunset 76 half an hour before they close. They squeeze me in without even seeming annoyed... though possibly a little amused by my level of cluelessness about this whole car ownership thing. The next week I realize that I'd never checked in about the brakes or the dire bouncing that one friend has diagnosed as a potentially expensive problem with the shocks. So I bring it back to Louis, who with amazing patience checks out both. Does he tell me that yes, I need expensive new shocks and maybe some other stuff too? No sir! He lets me know that unless I plan to be a Nascar driver I'm just fine... and there's no charge. 

I know that when there IS something actually wrong with my car, these guys are going to give me a fair estimate and a good deal... even though they could easily overcharge me and I wouldn't know any better. A car mechanic that I trust may be my best Yelp find ever. In the meantime, I go there for my oil changes (where they check brakes, tires, and fluids as part of their standard service) and resolve, every time, to bake those guys some cookies.

text:
This review is long overdue...Tony was referred to me by a friend who highly recommended him for his personal, honest service and unusually accommodating protocol of picking up and delivering customers' cars. I was not disappointed. Tony carried me through the last 2 years of life with my 96 BMW with the sense that I could rely on him for affordable repairs and honest advice that served me as opposed to brought him business. This is a tall order as far as I'm concerned, and, as a struggling single mom and teacher, I needed a mechanic I could truly count on. Tony was this and more! After the first repair and assessment, Tony presented me with a long, detailed list of all the things in need of repair in order of priority, and, unlikely as it sounds, advised me to do as little as possible given the make and age of my car and my financial situation. When my car's cooling system began to fail, Tony implored me to buy a new car and practically refused to fix it since he thought it would be a waste. Yes, Tony is that kind of guy. He'd rather turn business away than rip you off. Luckily, for me, I was given the chance to buy a new vehicle, and Tony saw me through this process with emergency weekend text messages advising me on how not to get ripped off at a dealership, etc. He also helped me price my BMW when I wanted to sell it and offered helpful advise at a moment's notice when someone wanted to manipulate me into selling it below market value. 

Tony is the kind of mechanic who is always a phone call or text message away and who can be relied on for solid, honest service. I think he's too busy these days for door-to-door pick up and delivery, and that's a good thing: hardworking, honest guys like Tony deserve to busy! Highly recommended.

text:
I definitely feel like a slacker for writing this review so late because I have this saved draft from almost 2 years ago. 

First Choice Auto Repair lives up to its name! The owners are two hard working brothers who seem very honest with their customers. 

The first time I took my car here was when smoke was coming under the hood. I just finished my doctor's visit and decided to go to a nearby shop b/c it would be too dangerous to drive far. First Choice Auto Repair was less than a mile from where I was and has stellar reviews, so I took a leap of faith and came here. 

I called the shop first and described the problem to the gentleman on the phone. He was very friendly and calm and said I could bring my car in right away for a free diagnostic. It didn't take long for them to find out what went wrong with my car and provide me with a reasonable quote. The best part was that I could pick up my car by the end of the day. 

Since then I've taken my car back quite a few times to replace battery, fix leaks, etc. I have an old car (2003 to be exact), so it needs a lot of work. What I like most about this business is that they are super fast and responsive. I could always get my car back within a day or two. And they do quality work.

text:
Wondering why this place is for Auto Repair & Brakes, when the mechanic told me they do not fix brakes at their location. I also asked to replace my taillight headlights (provided the bulbs to them) which they did free of charge.

I took the day off of work so I could get my brakes on my 2000 BMW 328i repaired. I asked if I could schedule a time and he said to come in at 9:30. I did and he said he would call me once he takes a look at my car. Before handing over my car, I asked for a time estimate. He kind of brushed me off and walked away and said "a couple hours." I waited at a coffee shop nearby and waited a few hours for him to call me. I walked pass the repair shop before I left the coffee shop and saw that my car still hadn't been serviced. Hours passed until it was almost 4pm and he still hadn't called me, so I headed back to the shop. When he saw me, he said "Oh I meant to call you but now you showed up." Then let me know that my brake line had a leak due to rust and either needed to be replaced or cut. However, he said that I needed to take it somewhere else since they do not repair them at their location. 

I could understand if they can't fix it since it's a German car, but it would have at least been nice to get a call from them so they could let me know that they couldn't fix it, and I would have had the time to take it somewhere else instead of wasting my entire day. Now I have to wait yet another day just for my brakes to be serviced at a new location since most places are getting ready to close.

text:
I had never had my car (07 Corolla) worked on beyond just basic oil changes etc. This was fine for me until one day last week when my A/C completely died. I looked around on Yelp and this was the highest rated repair shop. I'm not particularly keen on placing total faith in reviews and I tend to pay attention to bad ones more than good ones when evaluating a restaurant or other business. My experience wasn't flawless, but they're getting my 5 stars because of integrity.

Prab and his team are fast and stand by their work. It's a lot more important to me to know there's a mechanic I can rely on in the area than anything else. My car was ready in less than 24 hours with a new A/C fan, blower motor, drive belt, and brake pads.

When I received the car the A/C was working fine and blowing cold, but there was a slight vibration when I hit the brakes. I called them up and they immediately told me to come back so they could take a look at it. They assured me they would work later (despite it being Friday night and they were near closing) in order to get the job done. I insisted I didn't need my car over the weekend and to take their time. I got a call at 11am this morning saying the work was done. They couldn't figure out why the rotor despite being smooth was causing the issue, but hey replaced the entire thing with a new one at their expense. This is what it means to stand by your work and your word.

I'll definitely be coming back here for any future work. I would encourage anyone in Oakland to do the same.

text:
Wow, these guys saved me tons of money! I brought my Honda Odyssey minivan into the dealer to have a tire replaced (it's a special run flat tire that only dealers have the machine to fix). While there, the Honda folks told me all four of my brakes needed to be done, I had a leaking rear shock, and a broken engine mount ! Plus it was time to replace the timing belt, which also requires replacing the water pump. The cost for all this at a dealer was: Brakes $575, rear shocks $710, timing belt $995, Engine mount $1300 = $3580. 

Thank goodness I had the sense to say I needed to shop around. 

I found First Choice on Yelp, gave them a call, asked for quote to repair all that. They got back to me in 10 minutes: their quote: $1360, minus the engine mount. (He said he couldn't estimate the engine mount without seeing which one was broken). I truly thought he had forgotten to include one of the repairs, or was quoting only the parts or something, because it was just unbelievably less than the dealer and other shops I had called. 

So I bought the car in to First Choice, and no, it is not some fancy place with free popcorn and cafe lattes in the lounge (like the Honda dealership!) but who the heck cares. They were super attentive and thorough. They told me the engine mount had only the barest of cracks and really did not need to be replaced at all (the Honda guy made it sound like my engine was about to fall off) . This alone saved me over $1000 of unnecessary cost. I had all the rest of the work done, and have been driving the car around and everything feels and sounds perfect. 

My final bill was a little bit more than the initial quote, because I also had the spark plugs replaced, and the rear brakes needed to have the rotors replaced (not just the brake pads replaced). But even with these additional repairs, it was still so much less than the other quotes. Unfortunately I'll always have to have the tires replaced by the dealer, because of the special PAX tires....but for absolutely everything else, it's going to be First Choice Auto! They were just so efficient, informative, helpful, and all around nice. 

I have to say, it is SO DARN AMAZING to find someone that knows what they are doing AND is honest and inexpensive. They probably just enjoy fixing cars. They ask for a fair price, and I hope they are doing really well, because they deserve it! But this seems to be the rare business that isn't in business just to see how much they can make off of people.

Anyway, thank you First Choice Auto. And if you ever decide to go into general contracting, home repairs, plumbing, landscaping, electrical repair, housepainting or anything else, please let me know! I know I'd get a honest deal and a job well done!

As someone who doesn't know too much about cars, and being a younger female, I feel like it could be very easy to be taken advantage of when dealing with automotive issues --- BUT after today I have no qualms about going here.

I say thank you and expect to be hit with some sort of evaluation fee (which has happened many times with no service attached) --- Nope!

These guys are genuine, fair, and good at what they do. 
I'll be happy to bring my car back for future services and recommend them to friends in the area :)

text:
I recently broke my foot and have been dealing with a ton of nonsense and difficulty as a result. The last thing I needed was my car to start making a "noise" I never heard before. Still, when you hear something that doesn't sound good, it's always better to be safe than sorry when you're dealing with a car. 

I had one day off to get to my car looked at, and due to other errands I did not arrive to First Choice until the afternoon; I had a feeling of dread that there was no chance they would be able to help me on the same day, especially considering how busy the shop looked. When I pulled in, after about a minute of waiting, one of First Choice's mechanics (and lifesavers), Prab, introduced himself and asked how he could help. I told him that with every rotation of my tire, I kept hearing a noise. I did not know much else, except that my brakes were redone recently. Prab stopped what he was doing to give it a once over, then volunteered to take it around the block to better hear the noise. He heard what I was talking about, and told me that he would do his best to diagnose and fix the problem sometime today. I was excited by his declaration, but still kept my hopes down thinking I would get a call later stating he didn't have time. 

Around 530pm that day, I received a call from Prab telling me my wheel was loose, and that after he tightened it, the noise went away. I still have no idea how this happened, but if Prab did not take the time to check out my car, something very tragic could have occurred as a result. In addition, Prab could have easily made up some nonsense about labor, parts, inspections, or work done, and I would not have known the difference. If he wanted to con me, he could have charged me an extremely high price because I would not really have had an argument against it. Instead, he asked for $20. $20 measly dollars for taking the time to put it up on his lift, take off the wheel, examine everything, and drive it around again to hear how it sounded. This was all done with no appointment or knowledge of me coming. It may seem like standard service, but I can assure you that in this day and age, this is actually quite exceptional. text:

I was referred to these guys multiple times by neighbors and friends but unfortunately I was unable to get my problem solved with my car even after bringing it back in.

I have an old high mile Toyota, it has a few things wrong with it, birfield joint noises, oil leaks, dangerous low oil pressure, spark plugs etc. I got a quote and it was above what I had saved to fix my car so i left out the recommended belt replacements and the suspension work on the Birfield(CV joint) because of their recommendations and the belts looked okay and the suspension stuff was not crucial more just annoying and loud when turning left.

The engine and low oil pressure was my biggest concern, at low rpm's and after driving for 15 minutes it drops and will cut off-they found 2 oil leaks(I only knew of one), one on the head and one underneath. I paid 1k for them to drain my oil supposivley fix the leaks and change my spark plugs. after a week of getting it back the second time and them reassuring me there were no longer any leaks, which was impossible because I could see new drips on the ground. I thought hey these guys are nice why would they lie, it's probably residual oil left over from dripping down so I brought it into my garage with cardboard and now it's been 3 weeks and still drips every night-I basically just paid 1k for my spark plugs replaced and my oil drained and new 10w40oil replaced.

So I do not think these guys are bad guys? No, maybe just not the best mechanics with my type of car or they were having an off 3 weeks while dealing with my car? I do not really know because they seemed really busy and people have recommended them so they must do some work really well and have fair prices for others. I know one of the brothers was out for a bit, but I think if you have an engine issue or need to diagnostic work trouble shooting to figure out your repair it may make sense to bring it somewhere else. Still super nice guys but I keep having to tell myself it was another learning experience so I don't cry after working hard to save the money for the repair.

text:
I wanted to like these guys, because they do seem honest, and their prices are reasonable.

About a year and half ago, I had my brakes done on my 2011 Mustang. Afterward, I heard a squeal at high speed and a chirp when going over bumps. I assumed it was brake dust, but it didn't go away. I took the car back after a few months, but they said everything was fine.

I just had to replace the rear brakes, because the drivers side inner pad was almost at metal-to-metal. The new brake shop showed me that there are pins on the back of the inboard rear brake pad (the one with the wear indicator tab) that sit in the slots, and if the slot doesn't line up with the pins, the inside pad will not sit properly and WILL cause a severly uneven wear of the pad... and will likely cause one side of the steel backing plate to contact the rotor in short time.

Which is what happened. Which is what seems to have been causing the noises. Which, even with me buying the parts myself, just cost me 300 bucks.

Aligning the pins on a brake pad seems pretty basic for a brake shop. Sorry guys.

Well he had me park my car across the street, and mind you, I live a few blocks away, but I had a clear view of my car from my kitchen window. The car never moved, and was in the exact same position when I picked it up, so I'm wondering when he did the inspection... I was charged of course...The last time I had him do a repair he did my front brakes. He said I just needed pads and he did the work. The next week I took a trip up the coast and my car started making a horrible noise. I had my brakes checked and repaired before I left right, it couldn't be them. I ended up finding a random gas station and paid the guy $50 to grease them which helped with the noise a bit, but it came back. Really put a damper on the trip because we were worried the car was going to fall apart and we'd be stranded. Once I made it back I called Simon and he "didn't have time" that week, so I made an appointment for the following week. Seems like he would at least try to squeeze me in since he had just worked on my car and I had a concern about the work done. The following week he took a look and said nothing was wrong. I ended up taking my car to multiple places and finally the dealer who said I needed a new brake job and rotors. I had to pay for the diagnostic of course, and I thought they were trying to cheat me because I'd just had my brakes done and elected to not let them do any work on my car. Finally took it to another local shop to a man who has done repairs for me in the past. I should've stuck with him, but I switched to Glenview Automotive because the shop was closer. He inspected my car and immediately saw I needed rotors, and now new pads because the pads Simon put on were installed on bad rotors. My car drove perfectly after that. I'm not sure why my experience was so different than other reviews, but it's very disappointing. Maybe he just didn't like me personally, but the lack of care showed in his work. I don't need a fancy shop or a bff, just a trustworthy mechanic, especially as a woman. Despite me going to him for work multiple times, I thought it was interesting how when I would call for appointments he would say he was too busy, maybe he was hoping I'd get the hint and stop bringing my car to him. Well, the hint has finally been received.

text:
Since my first review, I had to seek out Simon's services for random events beyond my control.

On a sunny day, my windshield wipers suddenly popped up from their normal "rest position".  I thought this was odd since I hadn't touched my wiper lever. I thought it might have been a fuse suddenly going bad, but when I looked at the fuse, it was intact.  I then thought it might have something to do with my wiper motor but I hadn't engaged it ( so that probably wasn't the reason).

Took my car to Simon;  he pulled some panels off beneath the hood and found the problem.  Had to order a part from Honda but once it arrived and installed, my car was good to go. Parts and labor totaled $150 - much better than $400 for a new wiper motor!

A second problem arose when I started my car after a hike at Joaquin Miller Park.  When I turned the ignition, my car, quiet and smooth when I parked, suddenly sounded like a Harley.  Had no idea why and took it to Simon.  He knew instantly what had happened:  someone tried to steal my catalytic converter.  ( Until then, I was unaware of the rash of converter thefts nationwide;  I am very aware now).  Simon directed me to a welding shop at International and 18th, who took care of my car in minutes.

Bottom line:  Simon is a fantastic resource - I won't go elsewhere.

text:
Best auto service experience I've ever had. They were quick, efficient in their communication, and - most importantly - able to correctly diagnose a tricky issue with my battery.

Malcolm and Doyle at 1701 Auto Care helped me diagnose and fix an issue with my failing new battery. Two and a half months ago I consulted AAA and Autozone on helping me get a replacement battery for my 2007 Pontiac Grand Prix. One day after getting the replacement battery, the new battery failed and I was forced to troubleshoot the issue myself. I reinstalled the battery after cleaning up the corrosion on the battery leads, and that fixed the issue until today. I finally decided to bite the bullet and take it into 1701 Auto Care to get it checked out. It turns out there was still a problem with the connection from lead to terminal and from terminal to battery due to further lead corrosion and terminal paint inhibiting electrical contact. The 1701 Auto Care team diagnosed this issue, removed the corrosion from the leads, and sanded down the terminal paint so that proper electrical contact was established. 

Something that could have turned into an expensive unnecessary repair (alternator fix, diagnosing a parasitic drain) were all avoided because the 1701 Auto Care team diligently troubleshooted my issue. They even charged me half the quoted amount because it took them less time than they expected. Honest, great group of mechanics over at 1701 Auto Care, would highly recommend!

text:
TL;DR - Took my truck in for a general inspection and valve clearance check. Was told they didn't know how to do the valves and argued with me about what engine I have. Had general inspection done, needed a new rack and pinion. Was charged 2x the cost for the rack compared to other sources. Power steering went out immediately afterwards. Took truck back and they said they couldn't find a problem, power steering goes out again almost immediately. Never taking truck there again. Too much time wasted. 

---------------------------------------------

So far I'm not particularly impressed, though I'll give them a call tomorrow and see if they can help resolve the problems they have left me with. 

I took the vehicle to 1701 Auto Care with the intention of having my valve clearances checked, the truck being a 2000 Tacoma Prerunner (Gen1 Tacoma). It is the 2.7 liter I4 3RZ-FE engine, running shims for valve clearances. Upon getting to the shop the owner informed me that I in fact had hydraulic lifters and didn't need valve adjustments. I told him I didn't think that was true, but if he could double check I needed to get to work. I also asked him to give the truck a quick once over, since I hadn't had the time to care for it between work hours and other responsibilities. 

After confirming that I do not have hydraulic lifters, because I have a Gen1 Tacoma I called to again ask the owner to double check and then perform the valve clearance inspection. He told me he was not comfortable then said something about it making sense on Honda's but not my truck. He then said I should consider taking it to a specialty shop for this particular job, but he would still do the general once-over. I said that was fine, and went on with my day. 

Later I received a call and was informed that my rack and pinion was leaking rather badly and it was suggested I have them replace it. ***EDIT2*** Yeah I'm still a bit irritated being charged double what I could have bought the part for elsewhere. Maybe I can buy the part myself and just ship it directly to a shop next time. Hah.

When I picked up the truck the next morning I drove over to another shop, and had them check my valve clearances (all in spec). They did note however that my power steering seemed to fail at low RPM, when the engine was at idle. Given that this was not an issue before I can only guess that this is directly related to the rack and pinion being replaced. 

**EDIT** I've finally given them a call to see about having this sorted out and will drop the truck off tonight. Chatted with the owner about the misunderstanding in regards to the rack and pinion being new v. reman, and I'll hold confidence in the quality for the time being. The owner was good enough to talk through what might be causing my issue, and was very quick to want to solve the problem, while not just throwing parts at it. I appreciate that. It's still a little funny to me all the stuff in regards to not wanting to check valve clearances, but hopefully the steering will be sorted out soon. 

***EDIT2*** I took the truck in for my power steering going in and out, the owner drove it around, said he couldn't replicate the problem but told me he flushed some new fluid in anyway. He then laid on thick a story about how he used to work for a place that would scam people by convincing customers there was something wrong with their vehicles but hated it. Possibly an attempt to build trust? I picked up the vehicle and within three blocks started losing my power steering again. I'm over it, I'm never dealing with this shop again, I'd save more time and money just doing things myself.

Called 1701 and spoke to Malcolm and he was able to offer for me to drop my car after hours for him to look at the next morning (given difficulty for me to coordinate during the regular 9-5 for a drop off with a ride during work hours). I really appreciate hardworking, honest small businesses like what these two have. Malcolm took the extra time to answer all my questions about my aging car. I am so relieved to have found down-to-earth, skilled mechanics to take care of any future issues that may crop up.

Thank you 1701!

text:
My mother was always recommending this place. I asked "What did they do?" She said "I don't know, but they were very nice." They also had done something for a friend if hers. Again, no one knows what they did, but apparently they did it for free and were "very nice". I'm thinking "this doesn't help me" and her friend is so annoying I could imagine her getting helped for free just to get her out the door.
So I'd just bought a used car that suddenly needed a starter. They gave me a good price, which was a little less than what they wanted around the corner. Out of convenience I let them do it, plus an oil change. 
The starter worked 4 times and then didn't, leaving me stranded 16 miles away. I had to pay for a tow back to their parking lot in the middle of the night. The next day they said " Uh, we didn't hook up the wires right." No apology, not even a credit for the tow, which would've at least brought me back for something else. and given them a chance to display that "legendary niceness" that I'd heard so much about. 
As far as the oil change, they put on a filter which didn't have the seal attached. When I replaced it again, their seal stayed on the block and made a seal sandwich. The seal sandwich blew out and if it wasn't for the gauge reading and the streak of oil it made I never would've known what was happening. Any decent filter would have the seal firmly attached.
Get your oil changed elsewhere or do it yourself, get a name-brand filter and don't let 1701 do anything.

text:
I work in an industry where fixing one thing can sometimes cause other stuff to start acting weird, so let me preface this with: I totally get it. I do not blame 1701 for an old car doing weird stuff. I've also taken my car to 1701 in the past and they did quality work, so I didn't hesitate to bring it back this time. I brought my car in for a general "check-up" since I was getting back on the road after SIP for client visits. There wasn't anything going wrong, I just wanted to be sure everything was safe since my car had basically been sitting unused for months. Turned out I needed some new tires and a couple of belts. Awesome. Paid for it, picked up the car, and on my way home a bunch of stuff was off. The car was pulling heavily, the steering wheel was no longer aligned straight, and when I drove at speed it shuddered.

I brought the car back and asked them to fix it because it did not feel safe to drive. To get everything fully repaired and working properly/safely again it took three trips back to 1701 and each time it felt like they were just getting more and more annoyed with me. Call me crazy, but when you are going 65mph on 880 and your steering wheel is shaking so bad it makes your teeth chatter; or when you're driving down Grand and pulling your wheel hard to the left just to keep a straight line... I think it's a justified concern. This wasn't minor, inconsequential stuff I was nitpicking over. I understand that changing one thing leads to others and it's frustrating that it all needs to be corrected, but that isn't my fault.

Here is the credit they absolutely deserve: they got the work done and ultimately made it right. They fit me in when I brought the car back. They didn't fabricate new expenses or excuses. I sincerely appreciate that and thank them for doing an honest job.

From a customer perspective, here is what was frustrating: You can't blame your customers for expecting you to finish a job. The entire point of bringing a car to a mechanic is for it to come out better than you leave it, and in this instance, my car came back worse than I left it. I've been driving my car for over 11 years. I've had tires replaced many times, I've had belts replaced before. I know what it's supposed to feel like when it's normal. The things that were happening as a result of the work were not normal. Getting annoyed and rolling your eyes like I'm overreacting and brushing off legitimate safety concerns as "something that just happens" is patronizing, dismissive, and dangerous. Is it frustrating to have to keep redirecting attention back to work you've already done? Yes. I often have to do it in my own work. It's part of the job. Don't deflect that frustration onto your customer and behave as though I'm some massive inconvenience to you. I would have been perfectly pleased if you had done a more thorough job the first time and I didn't have to come back. These were obvious problems that could have been easily observed by simply driving the car. Giving me an attitude when I'm asking for you to correct these errors is unacceptable. I wasn't just coming back over and over because I thought it would be fun to bug you guys, I was justified in returning until it was fixed.

replies:
[{'id': 'QqpfA5pP21gVPFLP-p9evg', 'text': 'Hi Mary,

Thanks for your review and concern about your Honda Odyssey's previous repairs. In terms of your vehicle's spark plugs, the first time we replaced them was on 04-03-2017 at 101,742 miles and the second time on 05-06-2019 on 133,703 miles. Spark plugs do usually last longer than 31,961 miles, though at the same time there are many factors that cause premature wear and tear on ignition systems.

The reason why your spark plugs were recommended the second time around, and two years later was due to the spark plugs being fouled; upon inspection we found the tips of the spark plugs were covered in lots of black carbon deposits. Generally speaking carbon deposits form due to dirty engine internals, often times extra amounts of carbon will end up inside of the engine from aging EGR systems (exhaust gas recirculation systems), aging PCV systems (positive crankcase ventilation systems), aging piston rings and/or valve stem seals, or even poor quality fuel.

When carbon deposits form on the tips of the spark plugs, the spark plugs can not produce what we would call a "clean spark" to ignite the air/fuel mixture. Which in turn will often times cause lower fuel economy or in worse cases an engine misfire, which would prematurely wear out very expensive components called catalytic converters.

In terms of your vehicle's vibration the initial concern was a vibration upon braking at higher speeds which was due to warped front brake rotors; the replacement of the front brake pads and rotors took care of that particular concern. On top of the first vibration concern we had already repaired, your vehicle does have other worn out components that are causing additional vibrations. These other vibrations are due to wearing out suspension components. From what we have found so far your vehicle's front lower control arms and front and rear struts are starting to wear out, which in turn is causing a wheel alignment concern and the other vibrations.

If you have any questions or would like to schedule an appointment we will offer you a second inspection free of charge of the additional vibration concerns to ensure what we have found are the main culprits. At the same time we can prepare price quotes for the additional recommendations so you'd have a better idea of what to expect if you'd like to repair the issues.

Thanks again,

[{'id': '7Ec6qyYtY6OgPZq3cqWjUw', 'text': 'Hi Denise,

Thanks for the feedback. I appreciate you taking the time to let us know what we can work on in terms of our communication, etc. I fully understand your frustration with us and this scenario; and have already spoken to my employees about not having multiple employees conversing with a customer to explain what is going on with their vehicle.

The strange thing about this scenario is that I have confirmed that I indeed called you back and left a message (I checked my call log), I admit it was later than it should have been; though I did call you (your vehicle left on a Friday, I called back on Thursday for a duration of 4 minutes).

The voicemail explained that we could potentially get away with replacement of only the intake manifold actuator, since I found an aftermarket company that manufactures a replacement kit with a new upgraded metal bracket. The only reason the whole intake manifold would need to be replaced was if upon removal of the actuator we found the flapper door within the intake manifold assembly itself was seized.

Price quotes for the repairs are below:

1) Intake manifold actuator replacement (if intake manifold flapper doors "are not" seized)
-Price quote: $502.29 + Tax

2) Intake manifold assembly replacement (if intake manifold flapper doors "are" seized)
-Price quote: $1,241.90 + Tax

With this being noted, I'm not exactly sure how the other automotive repair shop was able to charge $2,000.00.

The part of your review I am not able to accept is the fact that you're lightly accusing us of doing something to your vehicle, causing the intake manifold actuator to break along with the check engine light to become illuminated (whether your writing is in the context of it being an accident or intentional I'm not sure, since it's difficult to "read" context).

The service we performed on your Mercedes Benz was a Service B which includes replacement of the following:
Engine oil and filter
Engine air filter
Cabin air filter

This service doesn't entail removing any components near the intake manifold actuators. If you're at all wondering about how frequently the actuators break, I would recommend performing a Google search to see the numerous posts on Mercedes Benz enthusiast forums having to do with the same issue.

I have been in the automotive industry for 12 years and I take huge pride in being an honest and very reasonably priced shop for the area. I do apologize for this long spiel, though this is the main reason as to why I feel obligated to write what was written above.

The two additional fault codes present on your vehicle are fuel trim malfunction codes for the bank 1 and bank 2. These codes are something I recommend taking back to the shop that performed the intake manifold assembly replacement. Mainly because the one code that was present after we performed the Service B was specifically for a faulty intake manifold actuator, not fuel trim codes.

Thanks and sincerely,
Brett Hayashida (Owner)

EDIT (02-13-2019): Hi Denise,

In terms of my voicemail I do apologize if you never received it. I did my part in terms of trying to find the best economical options for the issue your vehicle was experiencing, though I should have done better at following up a few times with you to ensure you received my message and had the information.

As for what the other shop was mentioning about one clip missing off of the engine air filter housing, I'm really not sure what clip they're speaking of. Mainly because the design of your vehicle's engine air filter housing does not have clips that you have to remove in order to replace the engine air filters; you simple detach the two cloth/plastic tubes coming from the front of the engine bay, pull up on the rear of the engine air filter housing, flip over the housing, unbolt a bunch of bolts, and remove and replace the two engine air filters.

Even if the whole engine air filter housing was removed and the vehicle was started, the vehicle would run perfectly fine since a component called the mass air flow sensor is located after the engine air filter housing and right before the entrance of the intake manifold. The mass air flow sensor is a component that measures the amount of air flowing into the intake manifold, in which sends the measurement to the computer, which adjusts the amount of fuel injected into the engine accordingly. The mass air flow sensor, at least with your vehicle's design does not take into consideration of what is occuring before the intake manifold, being the engine air filter housing.

The most likely reason why your vehicle felt different upon pickup from our shop was due to the broken intake manifold actuator and/or the possibly internally seized intake manifold flapper doors.

Anyway, I appreciate your feedback and I do apologize that we were not able to make things right with you. I will be bringing up a few notes from these reviews with my employees during my next shop meeting.

text:
I recently took my wife's car to Car Care Service and spoke with Wayne, the owner of the business. I requested the following basic work:

Change engine oil and filter
Change gear box oil
Change spark plugs
Change engine air filter
Change cabin air filter
Flush and refill engine coolant

The problems began after my wife picked the car up. When I took a quick look at the final bill and the car, I noticed that a) I was charged more than the original estimate and b) the car was missing a front wheel cover.

The following morning I drove back to Car Care Service to ask Wayne a) why the bill was higher and b) where the wheel cover might be. As I was talking to him his mechanic came walking out of the shop with the missing wheel cover. Wayne then explained that the bill was higher due to his supply house providing an expensive carbon activated cabin filter that cost $61.50, rather than the original estimate of about $30.00. 

When I got home from work that night I began a more thorough inspection of the work and the following day I contacted other local repair shops to assess what they would charge for similar work.

First, the work inspection: 

1) I pulled off the cover of the cabin filter (which filters the air before it blows through your air vents) and was shocked in two ways: First, I found the compartment absolutely full of leaves and dirt! While everyone knows that the cabin filter compartment should be cleaned out and wiped down when replacing the filter, the mechanic at Car Care Service chose to simply pull out the old filter and slap in a new one amidst all of the leaves and dirt that had been blown in there. My second shock was when I found it was not a carbon activated filter, as Wayne had told me, but cheaper micro-fiber paper filter.

2) Soon after, an engine warning light came on indicating that the engine coolant that mechanic had changed was low. I had to then pick up engine coolant and top off the reservoir to the minimum level required.

Second, the cost of parts and service:

1) The cabin filter: Car Care Service acquired the cabin filter from a wholesale supplier named WorldPac. While $61.50 may be the "list" price of the WorldPac part, I asked another local repair shop to contact WorldPac and request a price for the same part. After calling WorldPac they told me that that exact same filter would cost them about $18.00 wholesale and they would typically mark it up about 30% or so to a retail price for the customer. A 30% increase over $18 is just under $24. With these numbers in mind, Car Care Service chose to mark up the cheaper paper filter well over 300%!

Relative to being overcharged for the filter, I then decided to obtain estimates for the entire list of maintenance service items that I set forth above. What I found from my research is that it looks like I was charged overall about $200 more by Car Care Service than I would have paid at another repair shop in Alameda.

Note that I didn't just write this review before presenting my concerns to Wayne. I initiated my contact with him via email. In one of his emails he finally admitted that in installed a "microfiber filter" (aka cheaper paper filter).

When I expressed to Wayne, via email, my concerns regarding the sloppy, unacceptable work and being overcharged for the cabin filter, among other things, his response was:

"I am not responding to this e-mail. Call me personally if you would like to discuss this.
Wayne"

So I called him. I left a message with someone else in the shop and she told me he would call me back within a few days (I also asked her if I could speak with the mechanic who worked on my wife's car directly and she said it was their policy not to let their mechanics speak to customers). After a few days, when I hadn't heard from Wayne, I called him again. This time I got him on the phone.

The essence of what he told me was:

a) He had talked to the mechanic about his sloppy work.
b) All of the prices he charged me are fair.
c) Since I make a decent income (his assumption without knowing my income or expenses) I shouldn't be complaining, as he is just trying to make a living.

Not once during the conversation did I hear him offer an apology for his mechanic's sloppy work and the extra time I had to spend to fix things. Nor did I hear him offer to make it up to me in some way. He simply defended everything.

In the end, soon after my disappointment and frustration with Car Care Service I found another garage in Alameda where I consider the service to be excellent and at a fair price. It's called Alameda Auto Care, on Eagle Avenue, near the corner of Park St. (just a few blocks down from Car Care Service), run by Andy and David.

The end result, I'm sorry to say, is that I will never again take my cars to Car Care Service. I cannot recommend them. I'm taking my cars to Alameda Auto Care.

I just wanted to write a public thank you to the guys at Car Care Service. I picked up a new-to-me 1967 Porsche 912 this morning and while filling up on gas the battery went out completely. I called AAA but apparently my membership had failed automatic renewal (no one notified me) and the guy I purchased the car from had just loaned his truck to a friend of his for the day.

I set off towards a close by auto parts store to buy a new battery to get home, as I still had 80 miles to drive. While walking past Car Care's open garage I stopped to ask if they had a portable jumper cable system. The guys dropped what they were working on to accommodate me and sent David and I along to try to get the car back on the road. text:
Thank God for Car Care! I can't imagine taking my car anywhere else after finding this place! I tell people from all out of town to bring their cars here. These guys are friendly, thorough, and the real deal!

Looong story short, my car had been leaking oil for a few years--had diagnostic done and work completed early on, but it continued to leak. I eventually took it to Pep Boys in the Central Valley while out of town one weekend (yeah, I know *eye roll*) because I never had time during the week. You know the story here, yes? I thought Pep Boys would be sucky con artists who would try to quote me for work that didn't actually need to be done because they'd think I knew nothing about my car (which they would be terribly wrong to ASSume). They proved they were sucky con artists who also sucked at doing the most routine of jobs--the only one I allowed them to do (I won't bore you with the entire story here, but do look out for my review of them in the future). Car still leaked oil. Came to Yelp, found Car Care and my experience was great from start to finish! After dropping my car off, I nervously awaited Brett's phone call explaining the work that need to be done and...dun, dun, dun, the quote! *Gulp* After hearing that the leak was located and the other work I needed as a result of the oil leak (none of which was proposed by Pep Boys, but all of which made complete and total sense considering other issues I was experiencing with my car) and reassurance that it would no longer leak following their work, I held my breath as I prepared to for a sky high quote. *quote given* Say whaaaat?! Pep Boys' quote for what they claim needed to be done (none of which was suggested by the CC team) was astronomical! They completed the jobs, including one thing they did at no cost. THEN, on top of that Brett and company informed me that Pep Boys didn't correctly seal my valve cover because it was still leaking oil. They cleaned it up and told me to bring it back the next day just to be sure, and if it still leaked, to take it back to Pep Boys and let them know. Well, I did, it did, so I did--this time to a local Pep Boys because they threw in, and charged me for, the warranty (look out for my future review of them as well, if you're still interested lol). Well, this local PB did just what I knew they would, pretended to be nice and caring, then tried to pull the okey doke on me and trick me into getting work done that I didn't need. I nicely informed them that if anything else need to be done, I was taking it back to "my regular mechanic" (mind you, I had only been here once at the time). Welp, they didn't fix their company's mistake, nor did they say another word to me after I refused to let them do the work. Never again! It sucks when you can't trust businesses to not rip you off! Ugh!

OK, so, if you're still here, you've probably concluded that this story isn't as short as I promised, but I've said all of this to say: you owe it to yourself to give these guys a try! I even went back for a basic oil change! I'm sticking with these guys as long as they keep up the good work!

text:
I have put off car service for far too long because I've had such negative experiences in the past with other garages... being ripped off/lied to/problems not fixed/bad quotes/etc. and couldn't find a place I trusted. To put it nicely: I'm cynical and skeptical when it comes to all things automotive. Someone recommended Car Care Service and said they were nice guys, so I decided to try them out.
Since I'd put this off for so long I was braced to face a quote of $1,500+ for all of the work my car (desperately) needed. But I was honest from the beginning and told the owner, Brett, that I was on a tight budget. Result? These guys did all of the urgent and most important stuff for well under half of what I was expecting. I'm time-bound because of my irregular work schedule, but they rearranged their appointments and mechanics so they could get me in within my time restrictions. Super HONEST, friendly, and all-around nice people. They didn't even charge me for the work they did on the first day.
When I brought the car back the next day Brett promised it would be done before I had to go to work. I was skeptical (again, I'm a cynic. My car has NEVER been done on time in the past) and much to my chagrin I got a call ~30 minutes before I was supposed to pick it up and hear that they found an additional problem with my brakes...
Not only did Brett give me a discount on the additional part I needed, he said he would waive the labor and STILL have the car done on time so I could make it to work. Sure enough I show up and the car was ready, they did all of the work he promised, and he arbitrarily waived a significant amount of labor fees (essentially paying for 1.5 of the parts I had needed) just so it would still fit within my budget. Their prices are unbelievably fair and reasonable to begin with. I almost cried.
There are not enough words of praise I can lavish upon this place. They have earned each and every one of these rave reviews. If you need any car work done, ever, GO HERE. This is truly what 5-star service looks like. I am never going anywhere else.

text:
This is a review that went from 5 stars to 1 star in a matter of ten long, abusive minutes. PLEASE NOTE!!!

I took my car to Xiao at Car Care Service in July. He was fantastic! He worked with me to find cheaper parts and did excellent work on my car in a timely manner. He even topped off my fluids free of charge. Really, I thought I'd finally found my car repair guy. 

At the time of that first visit in July our Sienna (2000) was making a very loud noise every time we ran the AC. Xiao diagnosed the problem as being the auxiliary fan. When I picked up the car he mentioned that there might be some initial rubbing noise, but that it would wear off. No problem. Well, fast forward to October and the car still makes the exact same sound when I run the AC. I finally took it in today to ask him about it. 

I had no intention of asking for free work nor did I feel as though he had misdiagnosed the car initially. Our car is super old and has multiple problems. I expected back in July that there would probably be more than one problem going on. Nevertheless, the sound was the exact same and still needed to be addressed. I figured he could help me out again. 

At the very mention that we were still hearing the same sound -- literally it was close to the first sentence I spoke to the man -- he began hollering at me in a very defensive tone. [{'id': 'Hw_iWdE--MqTZSlYYCpM8g', 'text': 'RE: VW TDI/DIESEL SERVICE AND FORMER OWNER WAYNE ROBBINS:
Last year my wife and I brought our car in for a timing belt & water pump replacement, a fairly standard procedure. As AAA members, we thought that this AAA-certified shop would be qualified to do the work--were we wrong! The owner Wayne Robbins claimed that his shop was experienced with TDIs, including timing belt jobs. Can you say "false advertising?"

At the time of pick-up, we were told that another part would also need to be replaced. However, Wayne thought it was safe to use the car and return later to have the part installed. As I drove, the car produced white exhaust, usually sign of a mistimed engine. The next day the car would not start at all, and after a few more days, the car was supposedly fixed.

Because Wayne never offered any explanations, I asked another TDI mechanic to examine CCS' work. He found that:
1. The engine timing was far outside of spec.
2. A new tensioner pulley (replaced by CCS along with the timing belt) had a badly damaged tab. 
3. Engine mount bolts were not replaced per VW specs.

After sorting through this, we thought everything was done. Then in Sept., the engine quit suddenly on Hwy 24, before entering the Caldecott Tunnel. My family and I were in the car at the time--can you imagine what might have happened if this had occurred inside the tunnel??!! 

Another exam revealed damaged lifters and cylinder head, and there was scoring that was consistent with a loose cam sprocket rotating about the camshaft. Since CCS had also replaced the cam seal (which required removal of the sprocket), they did not properly re-attach it; this caused timing belt slippage and a wrecked cylinder head.

In summary, the ENGINE TIMING FELL OUT OF SPEC AT LEAST THREE TIMES: while being repaired by CCS, after the repair (when the damaged pulley was discovered), and months later due to the loose sprocket. In each case, the problem can be traced back to work done by CCS, and lifters could have been damaged, even slightly, every time.

Despite these findings, Wayne refused to refund the cost of our initial repair--never mind any additional damages--and offered only to replace the engine under an installment plan (but at OUR COST) or buy our VW as-is (which means basically NOTHING). Since we were not interested in being his guinea pigs again, the car remained idle until we could afford another $3500 to have the car repaired by a truly qualified shop! AAA also was useless in this matter, and they only took our information to appease us.

Wayne's lack of proper management in this matter demonstrates negligence and a lack of ethical business practice. If there had been serious injuries to my wife, child, or me as a result of an accident in the Caldecott Tunnel, we would be having a very different kind of conversation. Considering that human lives were at risk, CCS should consider itself extremely lucky--this time.', 'rating': 1, 'language': 'en', 'timestamp': '2011-05-03 02:05:24', 'translation': None, 'recommendation': None}]

text:
I'd like to once again shout out Yen's. I recently had a scary experience in which my brakes failed when I reached the bottom of a steep hill coming home from the High Sierras. It turned out the brake pads had overheated, which had never happened before. After a 45+ minute rest, the brakes seemed to be working again, and I was able to make it home safely. I wanted to be sure there was no impending danger to pedestrians, other drivers, my passengers, and me, so I drove minimally until I was able to take my car to Yen's to check the brake pads. It was late in the afternoon, and I'm sure the service person wanted to finish up and get out of there, but he did not ask me to wait or schedule an appointment or anything like what I have experienced at so many car places. He examined my brake fluid (it was almost full), took a look at each of my tires, and let me know that the brake pads were fine and that two of the rotors were a little worn -- but nothing to be concerned about for now. I tried to give him a couple bucks for his help, and he would not accept.

I wish more businesses (especially when it comes to cars) were like Yen's -- what a gem in this day and age.

The second day, after the purge valve part arrives, the mechanics spent 30-min lifting my car up and performed random actions under my car. But the purge valve replacement should be very straightforward and does not require doing anything from the bottom of the car. text:
I came to Nayarit because another mechanic at a different shop said my transmission on my 2015 Nissan Rogue was damaged and they don't deal with replacing transmissions. A quick perusal of Reddit revealed that Nissan Rogues from this time period were notorious for major problems with the CVT transmissions and there was no fix apart from replacement. I am always a bit terrified of dealing with mechanics because I realize how vulnerable I am to having to trust the expertise of a complete stranger and I have no real independent way of verifying that I am not being taken for a ride. I was fully expecting having to shell out $7000 or more. 

So, when I rolled up into Nayarit, I was greeted my Marcos. He was friendly and welcoming, and fully explained the history of problems with Nissan Rogue transmissions and why they generally have to be replaced. But he said he wouldn't know for sure until he did a full diagnostic. So, I left my vehicle with him, fully expecting the worse.

So, I was quite surprised when Marcos called me and said that perhaps my problem was not my transmission, but instead the transfer case that is attached to the transmission. The transfer case, well, transfers power, between the front and rear axles for all wheel drive. Marcos explained that replacing the transfer case, which is a third of the cost of replacing the transmission, might fix the problem. But he warned me that, sometimes, after replacing the transfer case, they realize the transmission still needs to be replaced. I was cautiously hopeful, but still prepared for the worst.

In just two days, Marcos replaced the transfer case, did a full tune-up of the existing transmission, as well as some other severely needed maintenance, and turned my vehicle over to me working perfectly. No need for a new transmission! What??!!? 

Marcos could have told me I needed a new transmission, and I would have believed him. It is extremely evident that Marcos is extraordinarily trustworthy - he will do a careful diagnostic review of your vehicle, carefully explain exactly what is wrong based on his expertise and experience, and will only repair or replace what is necessary.

The cost of his work is very fairly priced. He works fast. He takes great pride in the high quality of his work. He has integrity. What more could you possibly hope for?

Thank you, Marcos. You are awesome!

text: Marcos is a very honest and straightforward business owner. I had some issues with the delivery of my clutch online, which put our appointment previously made in jeopardy. He worked with me on the timing of getting my clutch and flywheel in, and worked me into his schedule with ease. I was initially concerned since he stated that he hadn't worked on a 10th Gen Civic before, but I was willing to give him the opportunity to broaden his "transmission portfolio". The car was completed in the timeframe he first estimated, and he did a great job! My 2019 Civic Si was slipping due to several modifications to the HP/TQ that the stock clutch just couldn't hold down. This issue is no more! For those of you on the fence for your modified Civic Si/Type R, just do it! Please note: the 500 mile recommended break-in period for a new clutch/flywheel should be followed, no exceptions, with no aggressive full throttle shifts, nor compression braking. Needless to say, I now have an official "Transmission Guy..." and that, along with the new clutch, feels great!

After my car was broken into and my laptop was stolen, I was already morosely counting in my head the hundreds of dollars it would cost me to make my car's driver side window whole again (not to mention the cost of replacing my $450 earphones that were also in the bag. Fortunately the laptop was a work laptop that was replaced the next day).

text:
I decided to make a yelp account just for this guy.
I normally hate going to auto mechanics.  What could be worse than being in a situation where you have a huge expensive machine that needs fixing that you rely on for your daily life, and then trusting a stranger who knows everything about it while you know nothing. 
A hit and run made a huge dent in the back of my car and insurance wouldn't cover it so I would have to pay out of pocket.  A friend recommended M&M to me, so I tried it out.  
I came in expecting to pay about 5-600 to replace the bumper.  He quoted me at 500, 300 for the part, 200 for labor.  Then he said he could try to just remove the dent for me for 150.  I told him I didn't know because I was worried the paint scratches would still look terrible.  He said he would fix the dent and if I didn't like how it looked, he would give me a 150 credit towards replacing the bumper.  That was perfect for me, and he did it right away.  When I came back, you couldn't even tell it had been hit in the first place.
Great guy, I'd recommend M&M to anyone.

text:
I had my driver side door replaced a few years back by this shop after getting t-boned. So when I found a replacement door (and hood, which only requires 4 screws to replace since the hinges stay intact) which matched my car's color, I excitedly called them back to see if they could do a swap for me again. I ended up having to call 3 times until I was able to speak with the owner Vahe (sp? ; I'm not sure if he's related to Raj, the previous owner apparently) who refused to give me an estimate over the phone and said he had to 'plug it into my estimate software.' After some additional quibbling, he finally told me that it would probably cost around $600-700 dollars. This amount of money for a simple door and hood swap is ridiculous! It's something I could do on my own time but I just don't live in a place that allows for mechanic work (apartment complex) or access to all the tools. I recall Raj was way nicer and professional about it rather than trying to sound like a used car salesman and sleaze their way into bringing my car to the shop (I would have to ask a friend to bring the spare parts to be swapped since they don't fit in my car, at which point would be difficult to decline the job).
Really, really disappointed and I don't think I can recommend this place again.

*Update* Very interesting that the owner chose to respond so quickly upon my updated review. Their claim was factually false, as reasons to bring in my car were never discussed over the phone and he repeatedly just stated that he would be plugging in and quoting me whatever his estimate software produced. In fact, they have a button where you can request an estimate right on their Yelp page which makes it even more unbelievable. Would re-iterate to avoid this place like the plague since the new owners obviously did not carryover the honest work from the previous ones.

I am pleasantly shocked that there are still honest people left in the car business! 

I had an unfortunate incident where someone hit my car while it was parked on the street and they left without leaving a note/number. Looking at their great review on yelp, I went to M&M before deciding what I wanted to do. 

I went in and explained my issue. They came out looked at my car and literally physically pulled the grill out, opened/closed the hood and showed me how there is no problem with the car other than the minor dents. All other body shops told me that I would definitely have to replace the grill and how the hood will most likely not close. Essentially, they fixed my car for literally no money and it took 5 minutes! I would highly recommend them!!

text:

text:
I registered a yelp account just for posting this review. I hope my experience with M&M will help for people who needs to find a body shop. In summary, Raj and Akbra are great professionals. They are honest business man, and they do beautiful work! This store gets 100% recommendation from me. (If you have limited time, please skip the details below :) )
My car was involved in a minor accident and the rear bumper was damaged. I went to few autoshop stores and they quoted me ~$3000 to fix it after I explained my situation. I feel, in my situation (a 10 years old car, regardless how much I love my car), it is unnecessary to spend so much money to make my rear bummer like new. I did some online search work and found M&M store with endless great reviews, and I decided to give a shot. To see whether I will get different quote, this time I didn't tell that my car was damaged in accident(Raj didn't ask neither). He carefully inspected the damage, and quote me ~$1700 for getting everything back like new. When I asked him whether it would be cheaper if I have to pay myself with cash, he told me that this is the minimum charge that he can offer. This is the honest shop we are looking for, period.
Something great other than honest about them? Yes, of cause! Later on, I told Akbra that I don't think it is necessary for me to get a completely new rear bumper. He listened to what I think I need, and told me that he could just do some major adjustment and repair the cosmetic damage. He quoted me a very fair and reasonable price to get my problem fixed. This is the shop that listens and works with customer according to their need and budget, period.
I would think that is already a fortune for me. but wrong when I saw the work Akbra finished. He explained what he did to me as promised, and he also pointed out some detail works he did for me that were not mentioned in our previous conversation. Marvelous job! 
Thank you for your great service, Raj and Akbra!

text:
Matt and AIA have taken care of my 2006 Honda CRV for all 160,000 miles with more to come. His service and professionalism are the absolute best and greatly appreciated. His pricing is always fair and he never does any service that isn't essential. I tried to get him to change my brakes many times because I had never heard of a car with 160,000 miles on it's brakes. Each time I asked, he took them apart, measured them and assured me I still had plenty of life in them. He never charged me for doing it either. Now what other shop would repeatedly turn down a brake job? 

When I mentioned that I did not have enough leg room, he made a custom bracket allowing me several inches of extra leg room. He later found a firm which pre-manufactures brackets and installed one in my wife's car as well. 

When the headlight lenses clouded over, rather than replacing them he brought in someone to "renew" them. They are clear as can be and that was 3 or 4 years ago. I haven't found anything he won't do including getting the car smoked and alignments.

When I needed my last set of tires replaced, he found that the original spec'd ones were no longer made and researched a very good alternative for me and my driving style (winters in the mountains). This set has already outlasted the manufacturer's recommended ones and still has 10,000 miles left on them!

As I debate getting a new car, Matt is always letting me know what things "may" go wrong in the future based on his experience with other CRV's. This helps me assess how much longer before I get into major issues. But for now with great service available and a fair price from Matt, I guess I will hold on for another few years.

I like his new Oakland location as it is much closer to us on the east end of Alameda and the freeway access is fantastic. When his lease was not renewed at the old Navy base, he bought an older building in Oakland, really fixed it up nice and provides wifi and other amenities for customers convenience.

I hope all this sounds like he is a great mechanic that cares about his customers because he is and he does. 

Thanks Matt!

text:
Okay, so based on most the previous reviews, I thought this place seemed better than most shops in the area. I was a little skeptical though as I read several other reviewers that said these guys didn't know what they were doing and were just okay mechanics at figuring problems out. Trust me when I say you will want to read this review on how I wasn't helped by them at all. 

So yesterday I was driving my VW Passat and I was going about 40 mph and my car just shut off while driving. It was so quiet that I didn't even know it shut off and it was coasting to a stop. I turned the key and it started right back up. I'm not a mechanic but this tells me a lot of key information on how to figure out what is wrong with it. First off, it coasting the way it did, instead of jerking to a stop, would seem more electrical or possibly spark plugs and not like any fuel or fuel pump problem. The same goes with it starting right up, as it wouldn't have a perfect start if it were sucking fuel back up first. I have mechanic buddies and this is first day stuff.

But I called Alameda Import Automotive and explained all of this and right afterward, do you know what their mechanic told me? "I will have to take it home with me and drive it around for a while until it shuts off to figure out how it is acting and what it is doing."

I said, "I just explained exactly what it was doing so what would you need to do that for? How would you seeing it do exactly what I just explained happened help any more besides just wasting a bunch of time?" 

I had to explain what happened again and he said, "sounds like a fun one," meaning it seemed like it would be a hard thing for him to figure out, if ever. Are you kidding me? This is easy for a good mechanic to figure out. Check the spark plugs, check any electrical that could possibly effect the whole car, do some work which you would be paid to do. One of my friend mechanics who lives out of state told me many great steps he would take to figure it out very quickly, without ever needing to see it shut off while driving it. He had a wealth of knowledge, whereas the mechanic I spoke to here didn't give any idea as to what he thought was going on, and didn't seem to have a clue, but instead he said it seemed like a fun one and said he would have to take it home with him to figure it out. If you want a mechanic that will actually listen to you on what went wrong with your car when something went wrong, this is not the place. At least the guy I spoke with. Pathetic. 

So they can read this review and apologize and try to explain themselves like they do toward every negative review, but that simply doesn't change the fact that their mechanic was clueless and didn't seem to care at all. Maybe the owner/manager is better and actually tries, that's why he responds to every negative post. But check your staff pal. I just told the facts, what else is there to know?

I had a friend come give my car a jump. Great! It works! As I was driving to the store, my car suddenly died on me. I panicked and thankfully I wasn't driving on the freeway. I sat there in my car and wondered if it was my battery + alternator that was the issue. I frantically looked on Yelp for a mechanic around me. 

I came across Alameda Import Automotive. Not going to lie, I was a little 'sus' with the high rating reviews. Is this place truly worth the five stars and +200 reviews? I read through the reviews and a lot of people mentioned the same things: personable, reliable, transparent, and trustworthy. 

Before I towed my car to AIA, I messaged the owner Matt on Yelp regarding my situation. He suggested that I bring it into the shop to get a diagnosis and see from there. So I decided to shoot my shot and get my car towed here. 

Before I towed my car to the shop, I gave Matt a text informing I was going to bring my car to the shop to get a look at. By inspecting my car, he was able to point out a few minor things and luckily he let me know my alternator was still in good shape and it's probably just the battery that needs a really good recharge. Not going to lie, that was a relief to hear because I was expecting to pay a decent amount for it to be replaced. 

Matt let me know the things he was going to fix/replace and gave me receipt summary of how much everything was going to cost. He also let me know how long it would take to fix everything. A day later, he gave me call letting me know that there were a few bulbs and mounts that needed to be replaced (I knew this was a problem before hand but decided to ignore it, lol). Since my car was already at the mechanic, I said "why not?" and proceed to let him fix it. I really appreciate that he called me to let me know before doing something without my consent.

After picking up my car, I truly thought I was going to pay a lot more than I was going to. This place deserves the five stars and I plan to be a forever customer when it comes to car problems. :-)
