I went here to take care of a small oil leak in an 8 yr. old VW Sportwagen, with parts & labor it turned to a $1400 fix. When I picked up the car I was told it also needed a whole list of things which culminated to a total of more than the car's value (wow a free inspection..hmm ).
I was somewhat skeptical considering my vehicle had less than 75,000 miles on it and not used much but as a typical gal, I don't know much about mechanical stuff so I decided to listen to them and start with the struts/shocks off their list of things (their 1st priority need and most expensive). After their installation of the new struts/shocks my car became a noisy bouncy house on wheels! It's so bouncy and squeaks like crazy - it feels like I'm in a rollercoaster ride.
Did it really need those new struts? it rode so smoothly and quietly prior to bringing it here. It's soooo horrible riding in it now and I'm sooo regretful for listening to their UNSOLICITED recommendations from that free EXPENSIVE inspection!

Since then, 2 different mechanics have checked the squeaking and told me they did not lubricate it well, and another one said it was a poor install job and recommended I take it back to them so they can fix it. And I did, but but of course, they did not acknowledge that it was their work causing the squeaking and bouncing, instead I was told it's because it needs additional parts. B******T! Then why did the old struts not cause squeaking and bouncing?

When I took the car back to them to get the squeaking checked out they charged me another $180 to inspect an issue they caused! Really, I'm not kidding I have receipts and all.
As, a single parent of 2 ..it's not easy coming up with extra money and do my best to avoid unneeded costs, like this one. Easy to go broke by putting trust in the wrong hands.

Sadly, I'm still bouncing and squeaking my way around town because I refuse to spend another cent on a place that takes advantage of situations like these and don't believe the issue is due to the need of additional parts.

I should have listened to Dad's advice... if it ain't broke don't fix it!

text:
On 9/24/13, I arrived into Alameda from Sacramento, and was quite fearful for my car's future. Along the trip to Alameda, my car began sputtering and the RPM's would rev up to 3000 RPM's uncontrollably. No check engine light, and no obvious problems under the hood, I decided to take my car to this shop per suggestion by my uncle.

Ian greeted me and remembered my call when I met him in person. He informed me that he would have it checked, and take care of it. I gave him the keys and awaited his call.

I received that call the next morning saying that my car was ready to be picked up. No major problems, no codes popped up when tested, and the problem could not be replicated. The only thing, was that my transmission fluid was almost empty ( No leaks which he checked for ) and he filled it for me himself.

When I arrived to pick the car at 5pm, Ian professionally greeted me again and went over my car and told me what his thoughts were on my Mazda 6.

Here's what really made my day.

I was originally quoted $90 the prior day for having my car to be looked at. Though I was told that a problem could no be found, nor replicated, he returned me my keys FREE OF CHARGE.

I've never seen such honesty in a mechanic shop before, and I was compelled to write about it and share my experience. If this shop were in my hometown of Sacramento, I wouldn't take my car anywhere else.

Ian at Alameda Import Automotive LLC, you sir, rock.

text:
Ok- this review for Alameda Import Automotive is long overdue.

I've moved from Alameda so I sadly no longer go to this shop. I just had a bad experience with a shop down here in soCal, and I was reminiscing of all the awesome service I've had w/ Alameda Import Automotive and decided it's finally time to write a review.

I discovered this shop in mid-2010, when they only had about 7-8 Yelp reviews (all five stars, of course). It's been awhile since I've been to Matt at AIA, but I remember my experiences very clearly. I'll outline them below and let my stories speak for themselves.

1) '98 Toyota Camry Engine Rattle

My old 98 Camry had this strange rattling noise coming from the engine for about a year that I finally wanted checked out. I bring the car to Matt, and he says he'll take a look and give me a call. A few hours later, he calls me and explains that he put the car up on the lift, inspected this and that and that and this, and tells me the noise is probably coming from inside something something, (it's been awhile so I forget the details). He would need to start taking apart the engine to get to the root of the noise, but given the age of the car, he's confident it's not a serious issue, that it's likely due to engine harmonics. Basically, he reassures me it's no big deal, which I'm glad to hear. I go back to the shop, we talk some more about the car, and he sends me off. I ask how much for the diagnostic. He says no charge. o_O I'm confused. Most shops will charge ~$100 for any kind of diagnostics (even if all they do is plug in an OBD scanner just to read your CEL codes). Who does that??

2) '07 Mazdaspeed3

I sold the Camry and now I have an 07 Mazdaspeed3. Fun little car. But this 3-year old car (back then) has more issues than my 12-year old Camry. My car has this random misfire/stuttering issue when I go full throttle. Because of my good past experience with Matt, I come back and explain the symptoms and repairs I had attempted. Matt says, "let's go for a test drive". Now mind you, it takes about 20 minutes of driving for the issue to start manifesting and I explained this. "No problem" says Matt. We drive around for about 15 minutes and sure enough, the car misfires. Matt tells me the likely culprits he thinks could possibly be causing the issue (bad sparks/coils, carbon build up, vacuum leak, bad gas, etc etc). Knowing I'm fairly handy with cars, Matt suggests a few simple things I can try first before bringing the car in for potentially costly diagnostics. Then he shakes my hand and lets me be. Doesn't ask for a dime, even though I just sucked up half an hour of his time. Again, Matt gets nothing from me. Who does that??

Now, mind you, this was well over a year ago. Since then, Alameda Import Automotive has gone gone from 7-8 reviews to 39 reviews. Matt was busy enough back when he was a hidden jewel on some random lot near the old naval base, I can't imagine how busy he is now. Don't go here expecting you'll get free diagnostics and advise like I did. But do come here expecting an honest, friendly guy who's not there to take your money. He's there to help you get your car fixed. If you can do it yourself, he'll let you know. If you have options, he'll explain them all to you. I've sent all my friends in the east bay here, and they all agree, there's no shop quite like AIA.

When I moved down to soCal a year ago, there were three things I knew i would miss. 1) my mechanic, 2) my friends and family, and 3) my dentist (in that order of importance). I've yet to find a comparable shop down here in sunny soCal.

Matt- please move down to OC, and let me know when you do.

text:
I was warned that the shop was difficult to find but discovered that is was only difficult because the GPS tells you to turn right on Hornet instead of left. The signs are a bit small but they are posted as soon as you drive in.

When you walk in to Matt's shop you first notice how clean and organized the shop is. Next thing you notice is how friendly, informative, and helpful Matt is. 

My undercarriage shield fell off my car a few days prior. Matt asked me to come in so he could take a look at what was needed to replace it. He looked underneath explained what was needed and ordered the parts immediately. He also fixed a lot of smaller issues around the car without charging me (i.e. rattling hood and squeaky driver's side window). He even gave me recommendations about things I could do myself. He was patient with me as well as with other customers that came in. He takes his time to make sure you understand what's wrong and what steps you can take and what your options are.

Matt not only goes the extra mile with his customers but with his employees too. As I sat there waiting for my car he offered to repair a crack on my new windshield. He brought Ryan, his employee, over who had never fixed a windshield crack before, and proceeded to teach him how. Mathew, his other employee, came over and watched too. He was patient with Ryan in guiding him through the process and answering his questions.

Matt, I believe, is an excellent business owner. He runs a clean shop, knows how to treat his customers and employees well and gives you reasonable prices while he's at it. He doesn't push or hassle and he's got a lot of useful advice.

text:
So I moved out to the bay area almost 2 years ago and completely fucked my engine on the way out. I had the engine rebuilt and the car was returned to me with some strange new behavior. I still drive my very first car...a 94 Civic hatchback. 

Now... before moving to the bay area, I had in-house mechanics. My Dad and brother have a garage out behind the house and my brother used to race hondas, so they've always taken care of my car and I, of course, never paid attention to what they were doing. In this aspect, I was spoiled for sure. I was terrified of being the "dumb girl" who gets ripped off at the auto shop so I did some research and came across Alameda Import Automotive.

I made an appointment with Matt and took my car in. When I arrived at the shop, I noticed something that made me feel assured that I was at the right place... Hondas everywhere! 

It turns out Matt also drives a civic hatchback. And so do a few members of his family. Perfect!

He adjusted a few things on my car and had it back to normal. I've also gotten oil changes here, had my instrument panel replaced (my odometer and speedometer only worked sometimes before!) and Matt also smogged my car so I could register it in California. 
I always get very detailed, clearly written receipts and the work is always affordable. I might not know much about cars, but I'm pretty good at detecting bullshit and you won't get any of that here. Matt is a honest mechanic, for sure. 

Now I'm moving away from the bay and I've already made the appointment to take my car back for one last going over before the big drive. 

Seriously, take your car here!

text:
This is a "double story..."

I was looking for a little used car for my 17 year old son when I found a great post on Craigslist. Everything about the care was looking good so the next step was to find a local mechanic to check it out before heading to see the car. 

Matt's shop came up as the #1 top rated mechanic in Alameda so I called him up. He told me that for $50 he could do a thorough pre-purchase inspection. He asked what car I was buying. When I mentioned the make, model, and year, he said: "That's my car! I'm the seller." Needless to say I was thrilled at the coincidence. Who better to buy a car from than a highly rated mechanic? 

My son and I headed to Matt's to see the car. He mentioned all the maintenance he had done to the car. The test drive was impeccable. The Carfax report was looking good too.(Matt let me check it on his computer because I hadn't had a chance to do so earlier!). We agreed on a price that included a smog check and better rims and tires. The asking price was reasonable. 

The following day we picked up the freshly smogged car and headed out of town for the weekend. When he engine light came on we called Matt who suggested we bring it back to his shop today. My son brought it to Matt who fixed the problem on the spot!

I can't thank Matt enough for his honesty and professionalism. I feel my son is in a safe and reliable car. I've rarely felt so good about buying a used car. 

So for all you would-be used-car buyers, Matt has the occasional used car for sale. Check them out.

As for his skill as a mechanic, I'm totally sold.

Keep up the good work Matt! I'm sure we'll be back for other services now.

text: I had a catalytic converter stolen from my wife's car, and these guys appeared to do a good job on it. I then took my car in as the engine light was occasionally on. I called several shops, including the dealer. They all said the first step in such repairs is detecting where the problem is using a diagnostic equipment. replies:
[{'id': 'SiZiWO_qtW_jYTGqz6FcwA', 'text': "I am sorry that you misunderstood/misinterpreted some vital pieces of information. During the free computer diagnostic I gave you for your 2007 Acura MDX, I noticed the fuel trims were high (11-17%, sensor indicated lean) and the mileage was 175k. I asked you if the O2 sensors had been replaced before, and you answered it had never been replaced. From the information I had at that point, I suggested to you that some car owners have had luck getting rid of the P0420 code by replacing the front O2 sensors, but if the same code came back up, it would definitely be the catalytic converer that needed to be replaced. I did mention to you where you might get the part from, and that it may be a good idea to get the rear sensors too if they were cheap. When you came back in with the sensors, I charged you $180 (less than the quoted price of $200) to install all four sensors even though it was more difficult than anticipated, since there were no major snags (O2 sensors tend to get physically stuck/welded to the exhaust when they are not changed at regular intervals). I then rechecked all the readings after putting the new sensors in, and the fuel trims looked normal (0-5%, well within acceptable levels).

Once, you had asked me how we could tell if the rear catalytic converter were good or not, and I replied that as the rear catalytic converter did not have an o2 sensor, there would be no way to check its condition unless we had more specialized diagnostic equipment (mainly a dynometer, gas analyser, backpressure sensors). However, I did recommend another shop with all the necessary equipment--it was the same one you called to inquire about what they would do for a P0420 code.

Again, I am sorry about the miscommunication, but I still maintain that O2 sensors should be replaced at regular intervals as O2 sensor performance does deteriorate with mileage (contamination from sulphur, etc. in gasoline) as well as age (from condensation/water). By the time you replace an O2 sensor that has already failed, you will have consumed a lot more fuel as well as shortened the life of your catalytic converter--the same thing that will happen if you don't change your spark plugs until they start failing.

text:
Was dreading getting a replacement catalytic converter, after replacing/cleaning all other tuneup/emissions gear on a 1996 Toyota 4Runner Limited with 350,000 miles. I had used my free second smog test and made improvements, but still failed, so the converter was the last thing to try. So rather than pay $300 for a diagnosis, I just took the other reviews' advice and called Mr. Yang. He listened to my drawn-out list of the repairs I had already made and agreed with me that I now either try a new cat - or give-up and scrap her or sell her out-of-state. 

I was also concerned about the ambiguity on the DMV and CA Air Resources Board websites. I knew which after market cat was right for replacing an OE California emissions unit, but nowhere do they make it clear that this is the part they want used on 49-state or 'federal' vehicles, although they make a big deal out of how picky they are on replacement parts. Mr Yang installed a Walker 81712 for me (a smog 'referee' told me by phone that this was the right one, but I was still not certain) quickly (~ 20 minutes), which was just a bonus at this point. Anyway, this new cat did the trick, I passed smog with average & (way) better than average readings, and I had been 2 or 3 times the maximum allowed before. 

Mr. Yang sells these cats for about the best price I could have gotten myself - and charged a reasonable amount of labor. I don't have a welder - or the ability to use one. If you have a similar vehicle and call around for quotes, I doubt you can beat Mr. Yang at $320 parts & labor. I know who will get all of my future exhaust business. I highly recommend this honest and skilled business man and his staff. There's great food in the area too, of course.

text:
I found Yao Auto Repair when I discovered my Honda CRV had experienced an attempted catalytic converter theft (but thankfully, hadn't succeeded in fully removing it).

I immediately called when they opened on Monday at 9 a.m. sharp. I spoke with Janice, who was extremely helpful in helping me understand my options for bringing it in to inspect the damage and get recommendations on what protection mechanisms were available for me to install to prevent a full theft from happening in the future. She was kind enough to let me drive over even though I had not scheduled an appointment in advance, and once I got there, she immediately let me drive my car into the garage so that they could take a look and give me a cost estimate for what work needed to be done and it was such a reasonable price that I decided to proceed with them given their online reputation.

The main mechanic (her dad) walked over and was surprised with how lucky I was since it was clear an amateur had attempted the theft and done it wrong, which is why they left without finishing the job. He briefly explained what damage was done and how much I would need to pay to weld the cuts and install the rebar/cables for prevention - which matched what Janice shared with me earlier as an estimate. Janice let me know I would be able to pick my car up within the day and that she would text me when it was ready. I left my car key with them and paid via Zelle (since they prefer cash/Zelle), which was convenient for me, and that way, I could stop by when it was ready to pick it up later and immediately go back to work. 

Not even 2 hours later, I got a text from Yao Auto telling me that my car was finished and ready for pickup, and when I asked if I could stop by in a few hours to pick up the car they were totally okay with it. Once I arrived at the auto shop, I saw my car parked outside, and I went over to talk with Janice and her dad to thank them. Janice took pictures of the work after it was completed to talk me through what was done - which I really appreciated! I retrieved my key and went to start my car, and so grateful to hear the familiar sound of a functioning catalytic converter that I recalled before the incident, and that confirmed for me that they were able to return my car back to its original state!

Overall, this business truly matched what the other rave reviews mentioned, and although I normally don't leave reviews, but wanted to share my positive experience with this honest and local family-run business! I'll definitely be coming back for any future auto needs since they were so pleasant and conveniently located.

text:
Yang Auto is located in a pretty low rent district of Oakland. I asked the person behind the counter about going for a walk in their neighborhood--and he discouraged me from doing it.

I took my partner's car in to have a cable welded on to make it more difficult to steal the catalytic converter from his 2010 Prius. Stealing catalytic converters is big business these days - - with the precious metals now worth more than gold. Thieves are stealing catalytic converters all over the US. We have been reading about the quick removal of catalytic converter's all over Oakland - - usually in the middle of the night. Sometimes they even remove them in a parking lot in the middle of the day. And it happens very quickly. Next thing you know--your car doesn't have a catalytic converter. It's better to protect your catalytic converter, instead of having to replace it which can be $3000 or so. 

Sandman's shop installs range from $250-$800 to protect your catalyst converter. We were able to get steel cables welded on to the our Prius for $180. It's the best price we've seen. The hope is that if someone goes to steal the catalytic converter, they will see that it's not worth their while, and they will move on to an easier job.

So, we went to Yang Auto Repair because they have the best price that we've seen to protect a catalytic converter. They were quick and responsive. I highly recommend going here--espcially if you have unprotected Prius.

[{'id': 'e017e2MwBUC4xeQomKZvrg', 'text': 'It's always been said that it's hard to find an honest car mechanic, and in my case, this saying is still true. Also, I'm really hoping that me being a female had nothing to do with the results they gave me.
Now, my knowledge in car repairs are quite limited, but I have enough common sense to know when something doesn't sound quite right with a diagnostic. I came to this shop a few days ago in hopes of help. I was heading to work when all of a sudden my engine light came on and my car wouldn't shift correctly when decelerating. I have to take the freeway to get to work and with my car acting up, I thought it better safe than sorry to risk any major incident on the freeway. I quickly looked up a repair shop on Yelp, and based on the reviews of so many people, I decided to slowly mosey on over to Almaden Auto Repair. 
When I got there, they have you fill out a form with your information, car information, and a list of what the problems are. I wrote down that my check engine light came on suddenly and that the car wasn't shifting correctly when accelerating/decelerating. I know it's easy to check what the problem is with the check engine light; all they have to do is find out the code from a reader and bam!, answer's right there. Now that part they got correct- my 3rd clutch pressure switch was the issue. What comes after figuring the issue out is what bothered me. 
I called them about 4 hours after I had dropped my car off to see if they had discovered what the issue was and they said they'll give me a call right back. A few minutes later, Thai called back, told me the issue they found with the check engine light, and that the solution was to rebuild the entire transmission and that it'll be close to $2500 to fix! WHOA, WHAT?! 
What I don't tell any mechanic is my prior history with problems, so that way there are no bias decisions made based on what I tell them; I'm paying them to find and fix the issue, not to have me tell them what I think it is and what to do. I've had this issue happen to me before to different cars- where the car wasn't shifting properly, and every time I've had it checked out, it's always been a plug or switch issue. The car was running fine without any noises coming from the engine and nothing leaking, only the shifting issue. I asked them if the car was ok to drive still and they said to drive it around 30-40 mph. With my uneasy feeling of their solution to the problem, I told them to hold off on rebuilding the transmission and that I'll pick the car up and think about it. 
Today I went and dropped off my car at another repair shop for a 2nd opinion. I didn't divulge any information about my interaction with this shop and what their diagnostic was, just to see what the 2nd shop would come up with. I told the 2nd repair shop the exact same thing as this shop, that the check engine light was on and that the car was having issues shifting when accelerating/decelerating. One hour later, they called me back and told me the same thing, that the 3rd clutch pressure switch was the issue. HOWEVER, the solution is that they only have to replace the switch itself; total cost- $380, and driving perfectly fine now. The switch itself is much cheaper if you can change it yourself, but me being car-challenged, I had the shop fix it up. The 2nd shop also checked over the entire car to see if there's anything else that needed to be done. Three hours later, done and out. 
I really hate to say it, but this shop may have tried to pull a fast one on me. Please have the decency to know that scamming will eventually come back and bite you on the behind. I would've paid 6 times more to fix something that wasn't even truly the problem to begin with. Buyers beware; do your research before saying, "Ok, go ahead and fix it" at this shop.', 'rating': 1, 'language': 'en', 'timestamp': '2015-09-05 21:43:50', 'translation': None, 'recommendation': None}]

text:
This auto shop used to be my go to, but not anymore. 

I recently went there because of a low coolant issue with some air in the system. I dropped off my vehicle and left it overnight. The following morning I received a call from Trung stating that I had a number of issues with my vehicle (rear main seal leak, replace oil pan, replace radiator, replace coolant reservoir, coolant flush, replace coolant hoses, etc.) The total cost for the job was well over $6,000.

This was a large bill that my wife and I discussed in detail. I decided to go back into the shop to get more clarification. Upon arrival, Thai, who I believe is the owner, fumbled around looking for my paperwork. He informed me that the quote that I received from Trung was for another vehicle similar to mine and that I needed a coolant flush, which was exactly what I had asked for in the first place. 

I paid for the coolant flush as well as the 75k maintenance package, which Thai recommended. The "work" was done the following day I picked up my car and drove home. 

While reviewing their paperwork at home, I noticed that I was charged for a new air and cabin filter. I recently replaced my own cabin filter so I had a hunch that they might not have done anything, so I checked their work. Lo and behold, it was the same exact filter I placed in. Also, I replaced my own air filter with a K&N recently as well. Most people know that K&N life time filters only need to be cleaned, not replaced. So being charged for service that didn't happen or need to happen is not right. 

I was not pleased about this and called them asking about the mistakes. Trung apologized and said he was going to refund me the amount for the parts. Rightfully so, I asked for the refund in labor costs as well since they did not do anything. Fortunately, I was able to obtain a refund. 

I went into the shop and talked to Thai about the the issues I had and asked for my refund. It took him some time but he eventually tallied up the numbers. I inquired and requested for a partial refund on the 75k maintenance cost and labor fees since the documents only indicated that an oil, and oil filter was changed. He stated that the technicians go through a list of tasks such as tire rotations, suspension adjustments, brake adjustments, etc. 

Again, I caught another inaccurate statement. My front driver side tire has a visible scratch, which I've been keenly aware of. I went to check my front tire and the scratch was still there in the same spot which means that the tires weren't rotated. Another example of being charged for service that didn't happen. 

This was a horrible experience. Lots of unnecessary stress and headache.

I definitely will not be going back here again. 

My advice, double check their work. Do your due diligence.

text:
They're either not knowledgeable about automotive brakes or they are gaslighters. I took my Jeep wrangler in to have the brakes serviced because my left rear wheel continued to spin when the car was in gear and the brake pedal pressed. Also, the left rear axle seal was leaking. 

They replaced my left rear axle and both axel seals. Note that I ended up purchasing and supplying the axel myself because they charged 3x the rate for the part. They also replaced both rear brake drums and shoes. 

The problem still existed, regarding the left rear wheel continuing to spin when in gear and the brake pedal pressed. I took it back to have them fix it but they insisted that they worked fine. They told me that's how brakes are supposed to work. I could not believe that they were telling me that the brake pedal is not supposed to stop the rear wheels from spinning. The tech even came out and insisted that everything was working perfectly. Nearly yelling, actually. I did all I could to explain the issue and they would not hear it. 

I then took my car to an actual brake shop. They replaced the check valve booster and thought it was fixed. I had to take it back to them too, but they rechecked the issue and agreed, of course, that both rear brakes should stop spinning when the brakes are on. In reexamining the issue, they suspected the wheel cylinder was faulty. 

I replaced the wheel cylinder myself and the brakes now work properly.

text:
**Avoid Almaden Auto Repair--dishonest, overpriced, and unprofessional.** 

I brought my car in for a suspension issue (a loud creaking sound in the front end), clearly explained the problem multiple times, and even wrote it down for their reference. I was initially told my car would be finished the day after I dropped it off. While the damaged strut I mentioned was a necessary repair, it turned out not to be the cause of the creaking noise. Despite this, they performed unnecessary repairs--including brakes and a front axle seal leak--without addressing my primary concern. Based on the lengthy two-day stay and their communication, I was under the impression that these repairs would resolve the issue I so clearly outlined to them. 

On day two, I was called to pick up my car and told everything had been fixed. Within *five minutes* of driving away, I immediately noticed the creaking was still present. I returned to the shop right away and was able to recreate the issue twice in front of the employee who handled my intake. We both witnessed the loud creaking as he drove the car into the shop but still claimed the problem wasn't apparent during their inspection. After a brief review, they told me they only needed to lubricate some parts--something that should have been done during the two days they had my vehicle. However, the noise persisted. 

Upon further questioning, they finally "diagnosed" the issue as worn control arm bushings--something that should have been caught during the initial inspection, especially since the problem was clearly suspension-related. Their excuse? They didn't hear the noise during their so-called inspection. Yet now, they want to charge nearly $2,000 for additional repairs they missed the first time. 

This shop ignores customer concerns, pushes unnecessary repairs, and overcharges for subpar service. For the money and time I wasted here, they should've at least addressed the primary issue. Instead, I'm forced to find another mechanic to fix what they neglected. Save yourself the frustration--spend your hard-earned money elsewhere.

text:
Being 500 miles away from home when your car suddenly starts making crazy grinding sounds in the middle of the night is bad enough, but add to that the stress of finding a place that won't rip you off, will do the work right, and get it done quickly enough so I can get to my grandson's 1st birthday is the kind of stuff that can break a person. 

Luckily, I found Almaden and they were only a couple of miles from my hotel and opened early on a Saturday. By the time I dropped off the car, I was resigned to the idea it was going to cost a pretty penny...all the thoughts of what could make those kinds of noises danced in my head. But you know what? They were totally upstanding when I finally got the call back about the verdict: the dust plate behind the brake rotor was bent in enough so it would rub against it. Total cost, $65. When a shop could just as easily have fed me a load of malarkey about bad bearings or axles (which I would have probably eaten at that point), it was refreshing to know there's still an honest place. 

My only regret about Almaden? I don't live close enough to give them all my business!

text:
My Lexus RX350 is approaching 50K miles. It's running perfectly with no braking issues whatsoever but I wanted to be proactive and replace all the brake pads in my maintenance quest. I requested an estimate through Yelp, Thai from Almaden Auto Repair and other shops sent me one. His shop is closer to me so I called the shop and made an appointment for the next day at 9:30am. Went there, waited for an hour but they still couldn't look at my car yet. These people don't have the concept of appointment! An older man who worked in the office saw that I was about to leave took a test drive of my car. He is not a car mechanic but Ok. He came back and made up some stuffs about my front brakes have a minor vibration so wrote me up an estimate for all pad replacement. I accepted it and left my car there. About three hours later a mechanic, Minh, called me. He told me that all my brake rotors have "cracks" and needed replacing as well. This instantly raised a red flag in my mind! My like-new car has only 50K miles since purchased new and I've been driving it gently. I would have felt any brake pulsations let alone "cracks" on all four corners. One brake rotor might have a manufacture defect and develop a crack but it's not possible all four rotors have cracks at the same time! Moreover I had personally replaced numerous brakes on my other cars so his story didn't make sense but I told them to go ahead with the job, OEM parts only as I had requested from Thai to use only Toyota/Lexus parts only and keep my old parts so I can verify them.

When I picked up the car the office guy told me they had used Akebono parts on my car even though I had verbally requested OEM parts in every conversation I had with them. I guess I didn't spell out Toyota/Lexus parts only. He showed me two front brake rotors and their pads supposedly from my car. Now the rotors he showed me were enormous discs that probably belong to a monster truck because I know my car rotors are not that big. Days before I spent an hour measuring the remaining brake pads on my car so the rotor size still ingrained in my mind. I bet they show this same disc to all unsuspecting customers in selling their story. I laughed but played along to see what else he has. He showed me some markings (not cracks) on the rotor and explained why machining wouldn't remove them. I think he didn't try yet because if he did it would be absolutely Ok. He didn't show me my old rear parts as promised however. It was late in the day. I knew that arguing about these parts would kept me there all night so I paid my inflated bill and left.

The owner has contacted me about this review and has offered to refund me the inflated amount. He seemed sincere about improving the business and promised me this issue won't happen again. I accepted it.

text:
My Prius had the "Maintenance Req'd" light on, so I made an appointment and brought it in to Almaden Auto. The tech at the front desk asked  me to write down what specific problems I needed fixed. I explained that the suspension was rough, it felt like the shocks or springs were done because you felt every little bump. I also wrote and explained that when I got up to and beyond 60 MPH, the whole front end starts shaking and had pulsating  vibrations that are quite worrisome. I was assured these would be fixed and they would call me with a quote to get authorization.

I got a call a few hours later telling me my suspension, front end, shocks and springs were all "fine" but that my tires just needed rotating and balancing. They said the "maintenance" light was on because I needed new spark plugs. Further, they wanted to "flush & replace all the fluids". The quote was $520. 

I asked how much just for spark plugs and tire rotation+balance. $228 I was told. I okay'd that and picked up my car the next morning. 

Guess who's car still has ALL the problems I wrote, was told were being fixed and maintenance light still on?

This guy. ‍

Won't be back. Sorry I blew over $200 bucks for absolutely nothing, but glad I didn't agree to the $500+ things that were allegedly "needed".

Now I just need a shop that can actually fix my problems.

text:
First of all, let me say this - if you are Yelping around for a place to get anything done on your car, close all of the other tabs you probably have open and go straight to Almaden Auto Repair. 

I despise dealing with my car (2004 Saab 2.0t). Whenever it beeps a message at me saying that something is wrong or makes an odd sound, I instantly feel sorrow and anger. This happened recently - I heard a loud metallic screeching noise every time I used my breaks. I already knew what it was (my lack of break pads/ rotors). Yes, this has happened to me before. Yes, I know I should have learned my lesson the first time. To everyone that doesn't know - replace your break pads before they get completely obliterated, otherwise you will be paying a nice extra sum to get your rotors replaced too. It is expensive and unnecessary. 

Anyways, when I started hearing these sounds, I was particularly sad because last time I needed to replace my front rotors and break pads (2) it cost me a little over $450. This time, the same thing was happening with the back pair. So, I decided to look around Yelp and see if I could find some place that could do it for a little cheaper. I decided to go to Almaden Auto Repair. I will never ever go anywhere ever again. Thai provided EXCELLENT customer service - always shook everyone's hand, remembered everyone's name, offered people water, candy, etc. He is seriously the nicest auto technician ever. A little girl who was there with her mom even picked a flower for him. Point proven.

He explained in detail how everything would be done, and quoted the job for $285. This included them going out to get the part for me. As I learned when signing for the work, this price already included taxes (a pleasant surprise). His team had also apparently done a brief inspection of my car, because they noticed that I had not changed my oil in a long time (whoops). I got this done as well.

The bottom line is that I would never expect myself to be happy after getting work done on my car. Somehow, I am. Thai is very accommodating and an absolute pleasure. Plus, now I have a shiny #1 key chain as a souvenir from the shop. I'll be back!

text:
UPDATE BELOW: I'm not sure how this business gets so many five stars. Perhaps it is for routine repairs on easy cars. My experience was poor nearly from beginning to end. I have a Audi Allroad that had a pronounced shake when accelerating. I called for an appointment and took the car in at the appointed time for diagnoses; a Wednesday. Since it is my only car I needed to rent a car until mine was done so I went down to Hertz. One of the managers at Almaden did give me a ride down there so that was nice. Then the poor service began. No word on diagnoses by Thursday afternoon about my car so I called. They said they hadn't gotten to it yet. I let them know I was renting and didn't want to go to the expense while my car was just sitting in their garage. Promises that they would get to it. Still by Friday they had not even looked at it. So I asked to pick up my car and I would take it somewhere else to have it serviced as their communication was very poor; I had to call them at every turn to find out status. They promised, promised to get to it on Saturday. Saturday comes and in the late afternoon they said it was done. They had to replace all of the control arms at an expense of over $1,000. Which, I understand, for a job of that size is a good price. BUT I was to find out later that it was penny wise and pound foolish as I will relate later in the story. I go to pick up the car but have to drop off the Hertz rental and wait for someone to come pick me up. They did send someone after 30 minutes but it was nice to have them pick me up. I paid for the work and spoke with the owner, Thai, and he was very courteous and nice. He said the shake was taken care of but there was a rattle when braking and he wasn't sure what that was about. When I got in my car it reeked of cigarette smoke and for weeks afterward the smell did not go away. Fast forward a few weeks and a pronounced thumping when I brake or go over a bump developes. Two more weeks go by and the thumping becomes worse. So while it is in for some tire and aligment work at another shop they take a look to diagnose the thumping. Turns out it is one of the very same control arms replaced by Almaden. I am told that the control arms used by Almaden are probably the cheap Chinese manuafactured ones and the bolt for this one is already worn and needs to be replaced at a cost of $500. Since I don't now trust Almaden I'm not about to have them do anymore work on my car. I'm just out. Probably have to replace the other cheap parts soon too. 
So to sum up:

1. Three days to even diagnose my car
2. Inferior parts caused a redo at an additional cost of $500 and maybe more over time
3. Car smelled like cigarette smoke for weeks after pick up.

Update 4/5 Thai has called me to try to make this situation right. He has committed to replacing the cheap parts and I am scheduled for next week. If they come through with committment I will update this post.
Update 4/15: Thai was good to his word. I left my car while on a business trip. When I returned Thai had replaced the parts that were already failing with higher quality parts. As a way to keep my business he also had the car cleaned. He worked very hard to make things right. Thank you Thai. Now I see why you are highly rated.

text:
This place is located on the intersection of Almaden Expressway and San Jose Ave. The neighborhood is almost entirely industrial, dominated by businesses and shops concerning automotive. The reasons I decided to come to Almaden Auto Repair were the five-star Yelp rating and their website advertisement of free brake inspection. (I almost went elsewhere that had a coupon advertised for discounted inspection, which would have been $50). When I pulled up, the parking lot of the business complex in which it was located was filled with vehicles, but I found parking immediately. I went into the lobby and was greeted by Thai, who paused his conversation with another customer to greet me and quickly resumed after telling me that he would return for me soon. There was already another customer seated, and I shortly waited with her; I enjoyed watching the news on the TV. When Thai returned, he had to deal with the customer who had arrived prior to me, but soon he got to me. I told him about how my brakes were squealing and probably needed brake service. He said that he would have to take a look at it first before quoting me a price. I filled out the form he handed me, and I went on my way to the nearby sandwich shop he told me about, evidently named The Bread Box and located across the street. In less time than the estimate he gave me to wait, he called me to let me know that he had completed the brake service. The brakes did not need major service yet, he informed me, and that he had performed a minor service on it instead. Since I was already there, I asked him to additionally change the engine oil and replace the coolant and returned to the sandwich shop, staying for an hour. Thai later calls me, saying that the work on my car was complete. I followed him to the lobby to pay and was astonished that see that the bill came to a rounded-up $84, including tax: I had been expecting a bill of approximately $200. Noticing the items for the coolant replacement and engine oil change, I asked him if the bill for the brake service was separate. HE SAYS THAT HE DID NOT CHARGE ME FOR IT. In my mind was "WOW," which was likely vocalized as well. He gave me a break on my brakes! I was impressed further, as I had already warmed up to him due to his consistently friendly demeanor and politeness, not to mention that he gave me a free Coke. I thanked him for the free-bee and informed him that I would return in a few months (for engine oil change and another brake inspection much later on). He sent me on my way with a shiny metal keychain shaped like a number 1 and etched with the contact information of Almaden Auto Care. 

Highlights: friendly customer service and professionalism (from Thai), prompt service wait times, very reasonable prices, and free inspections

text:
If you've given up hope of ever finding an "honest auto repair shop", stop right here! When I first found Thai's shop on yelp and read other customer reviews, I seriously thought he must pay his customers to write nice things about him. NOT SO. I could not have made a better choice for a reliable, capable auto repair shop than Almaden Auto Repair. We've lived here about a year now and have been taking our vehicles to Thai's shop the whole time. We first came to him with our older vehicle. We were preparing to sell and wanted to do so in good faith, so asked him to make all sorts of minor repairs (little plastic parts that had come loose or fallen off over the years inside the van, etc). We also addressed the one or two major repairs needed and were VERY pleased with the rates quoted and timely service executed just as promised. We had already had the van looked at by two other mechanics over the preceeding weeks/months, so we knew about what to expect in terms of cost. We were VERY pleasantly surprised by Thai's low rates for both parts and service. The total bill was much less than we anticipated, and we still corrected all the issues we intended to address before selling for top dollar. Thai even helped us discern which items we THOUGHT were important to the potential sale, but ultimately were not. He was fair & reasonable in every way - even tolerating our last-minute decision not to replace one item we'd asked him to order for us. He didn't even charge us for his inconvenience the way some places would. He just assured us that he was most interested in our long term business and it turns out that has clearly been the case. Thai is not looking to make a big profit on any one job. He's running a repair shop that services its customers fairly and in a timely manner. He provides top-notch work and has excellent knowledge of the automobile industry and mechanics of his business. 

While we were there taking care of our first order of business, we discussed our new car options and various used cars we were considering for our next purchase. Thai offered great advice and offered a very competitive price to look over any vehicle we considered buying used. He gave us a lot of good feedback on which makes, models and years were wise choices for our family in terms of long term costs. Once we did purchase two new cars, he advised us to bring them to him for routine maintenance (oil changes, tire rotations, etc) and he would always tell us if we needed to address any warranty issues with the dealership. If we'd done this with the vehicle we were selling when we met Thai, we could have saved thousands of dollars over the life of that vehicle in repairs we ended up paying for because they went un-noticed until our warranty had just expired. 

Now, we take both of our vehicle to Thai for everything. Most recently, we were headed on a weekend road trip to SLO and called for a last-minute oil change and tire rotation. Thai always knows my wife when she calls and is great about fitting us into his schedule. He got our car in and out in no time and charged about half what most major chain stores charge for JUST an oil change. Our service that day included the tire rotation AND he found a leak in one strut which he told us to follow up on with the dealership. When we did, the dealer actually chose to replace BOTH struts for FREE because they felt it was warranted, so in the long run, we would never have known if not for Almaden Auto Repair and their dedicated, expert staff.

It's a small place, but Thai is great about making his customers feel at home. He's very patient with our three kids when they are waiting for the service in his small reception area. My wife says he's extremely polite, follows through with his word and is very professional. He keep accurate records and is absolutely the best auto mechanic/shop owner we've had the pleasure of working with in the 40+ years we've been driving all over the country.

These 5-stars are well-deserved from a first-time yelper who just wants to help someone else find a trustworthy place to seek auto repair when needed. Thanks, Thai.

text:
I called AAR and spoke with Thai about a slipping clutch on my 1998 Ford F-150. He told me he could look at it today (Aug. 31 around 2pm) for free and give me an estimate. The place is pretty basic, small shop, small waiting room, decent neighborhood.

Thai took the truck out with me and did some basic analysis on the road and did an estimate. It came to about $840 for parts/labor/tax. That's around what I was expecting, so no surprises. Thai said I could have the truck back the next day (Sept 1 in the afternoon). It looked like they had a couple other cars on the lifts and some waiting so I thought his time estimate was a bit ambitious. 

Neverthemore, he sent me on my way with a working 1990 Acura Legend. The next day Thai called me and explained that the parts were a little late. It would be another day before the truck was finished (Sept 2). No worries, I was expecting it.

Sept 2 rolls around and I didn't get a phone call telling me the truck was ready or that it would be late. Not the end of the world, but it would have been nice. Sept 3 at about 1pm I call Thai and ask the status of my truck. He says it's almost done and they are testing it now to make sure everything works. He later calls me and tells me to come by and pick it up :-)

I drop off the rental, pay, take the truck, and I'm on my merry way. The truck was in good shape. No more slipping in 1st gear, reverse doesn't sound like the gears are grinding and the shifts are a bit smoother. I was happy with the results, Thai even called me the next day to see if everything felt good. He also told me to come back if anything felt funny or seemed wrong.

TL;DR
Great shop and I'll go back/recommend this shop to a friend. Time estimates to complete the work were slightly off, but still reasonable. Oh and the soda was nice :p

He eventually checked all the brake system and recommended the rotors and shoes need to be replaced because they were affected by the heat caused by the sticky brake, but not urgent. Never pushed me for the sale. That is another genuine aspect I would consider from Thai.

text:
After trying about 7 different auto repair places around Almaden Valley, I believe I found one that is really great.

After having my tie rod ends replaced at another shop on my 95 Dodge Intrepid (they were obviously needed anyway), a humming noise while driving still did not go away. The guys at that other shop said they thought it may be my differential, which could require about $2500 worth of work. They told me to drive it awhile longer and let them know if it got worse. 

After reading the yelp reviews, I stopped by Almaden Auto repair on my way to work the next day, just to check them out and ask what they thought. Thai was very nice, and immediately had someone test drive my car. At first, he thought it could be a worn tire, so he said he would rotate my tires for free to see if it helped. Thai and one of his mechanics put in on the rack and did a full inspection, listening with the mechanics stethoscope to both the front wheel bearings. They were able to determine that the noise was from the left wheel bearing, but the right wheel bearing was also loose. He gave me a good quote for both (about $200 each side), and even lent me a car for the day, which made it very convenient. All in all, it took about 45 minutes for the diagnosis (immediately, while I waited, and after I showed up without an appointment!) and I was on my way. I returned at the end of the day, and my car was ready. Noise gone, and everything is great. 

Thai even called me the next day to see if everything was fine and confirm the noise was no longer an issue. (When's the last time anyone ever followed up these days???)

Great fast service. Very good prices. Nice courteous pleasant people.

I used to work on my own car in high school and college and still do some basic quick stuff, but I'm going to take our cars here for any significant repairs.

Highly recommended!

HANDS DOWN ONE OF THE BEST SHOPS IN THE BAY AREA! My boss recommended this shop to me since he's been taking his car, his wife's car, and father's car for a few years now and he really liked his work and services. So, I came in on a Saturday right when they opened and the young gentleman greeted me and asked what service I need to be done for my car. So I told him what's been going on with my car and he had me fill out a paper with basic information and the problem or problems that my car is showing. I returned it and he had told me a quote for a diagnostic and it was a pretty cheap $70 for 4 problems/symptoms I've written down and I was pretty shocked that it was pretty darn cheap - I've been to other shops that quoted me over $100. My friend and I left the car there since they need to work on other cars from the previous day and the man said he'll give me a call in a few hours.

I actually didn't really get a call back which was fine since I was pretty busy during the day so I've just decided to stop by and see what's up with my car. Turns out I needed new spark plugs and the wires that goes with it plus some coils (ignition coils?). I met the owner, Thai in that afternoon and he had explained to me some options for what I need and then recommended the best which was get the OEM ones since it would last me longer than an aftermarket part. Thai is a very soft-spoken man and he does not talk to you in a condescending way like other mechanics I've had conversations with in the past. You can tell right off the bat that he's a very nice, genuine man and he even gave me and my friend bottled water! Talk about superb customer service! He told me to come back on Monday and the car will be ready.

Monday came so I came back but my car was not quite ready because they need to test drive it one more time to check if my car is okay to drive. Turns out that they have other vehicles to test drive so he told me to come back the next day. No worries. I didn't get to come back the next day since my friend who was supposed to come with me was swarmed with work. Today (Wednesday), I came by during my lunch time and my car was super ready to drive! Did some last minute transaction and viola! My car is alive and well :)

I really like this shop and if anyone wants reasonable priced shop, this is the one I would recommended. You won't feel ripped off and Thai gives you options on how you want to go about your car. Also, Thai will tell you what you need to watch out for to avoid super costly repairs in the future.

text:
Sent in my car for spark plug replacement and save the old spark plugs for me. I asked them to replace it with as specific spark plug make and model # (recommended in performance forums to increase fuel economy through more complete combustion). Also, I asked them to change out the differential oil. 

The result is that I noticed that the spark plugs they saved for me were in boxes other than the ones requested. I ask them about this and then the copped to the fact that they installed standard spark plugs not the ones I specified.

Also, I noticed that the oil they put in the differential was way way way over priced (by ~$50). I asked them about this and they said the oil was as per the Technical Service Bulletin (TSB) related to my car's make and model. I asked to read the TSB. After reading the TSB, it was apparent that they mis-read it and filled my differential with crazy expensive LSD oil in a non-LSD differential. 

So I figured these guys can't handle performance cars, can't perform services as per written customer directions and can't read TSBs. Maybe they can handle a standard car. Well, I was wrong.

Later, I sent them my wife's car. I asked them to replace the radiator hoses. 

When they completed the job, my wife noticed that there was a persistent whooshing sound coming from the engine. The car was in the shop an additional several hours before they discovered that they forgot to top off and bleed the coolant system (potential serious engine damage if not caught early).

Plus, shortly after, my wife's Credit Card (the one she used to pay for the work done) was being fraudulently used.

There are no minus stars I can award this shop. If there were, I would give them a -5.

text:
I seldom write reviews but I thought this review might help others in choosing an auto repair shop. It's often nerve racking taking your car to a mechanic especially if you are not really car literate, especially since there is such a stigma with not taking it to a dealership, which I believe is an unfounded stigma. Private auto repair shops sometimes are just as good and a lot less expensive. 

I recently just moved to the San Jose area from the east coast and was looking for an auto repair shop to take a look at my car as it was making a weird noise that was coming from the undercarriage of the vehicle. I waited for no longer than half an hour as the technician took my car for a spin and had it lifted for inspection. The technician was very prompt and showed me a possible reason for the noise. It was caused by an error from a prior work from a Honda Dealership, the damage was very visible. I had asked the technician if the other components of the suspension was okay, he replied honestly that the other components were okay for the time being, just the usual wear and tear but nothing needed to be replaced at the moment. I was advised to take the vehicle back to the Honda Dealership so that they can fix the prior error that they had caused. Almaden Auto Repair didn't even charge me a fee for the diagnosis, and from my first and personal experience, it doesn't seem like they would try to persuade you to fix something if they weren't sure it really needed it. I would have given a 5 star but I did not have any work done at Almaden yet, but from my first visit with them, it was a pleasant visit and they made a good impression on me.

text:
My automatic transmission felt like it was slipping and starting on 3rd gear so I decided to go on Yelp to find a transmission repair shop. I started off dropping my car to All Trans because of great reviews. Long story short after 9 hours of no communication, they finally just told me that I need a new transmission and it would cost about $3000. No analysis or process as to how they got to that conclusion. Naturally, I took my chances to find another assessment because 1) I am not a mechanic but learn about cars enough that I had a hunch that it was not that serious after self diagnosis 2) I was not ready to shell out that much especially considering my instincts.

I came across Almaden Auto Repair and went along with them as they have great reviews and are Vietnamese so I was happy to support my fellow people's business. 

Dropped off my car in the morning and they clearly communicated that they would charge an assessment fee of $95 and that I would hear from them as they discover more.

Mid day, they notified that my fluids were dirty but not low enough that it would cause any damage. Proceeded with fluid change. 

Next day, was told that I have a solenoid issue but also warned that it was only the first issue they discovered so far but there may be more. Gave me two options: Replace solenoid and see how it runs or rebuild it or replace with a lower mileage used transmission. I took the cost that would hopefully cost me less. Part had to be ordered so I'd have to wait 3 days. 

Got my car back 3 days later and they said it runs well but to try it out for a few weeks to see if it continues to run well. So far it has been over a week and it runs great! I still notice the slightest occasional slippage from 2nd to 3rd but I'm well aware that the transmission has had too long a life of over 280k miles. All 5 gears are working. 

All in all, I paid $1100 for assessment fees, transmission fluid change, oil change and solenoid replacement. I would definitely come back for these reasons:

1. Prompt communication of thorough analysis
2. Honest advice (after giving options, fixed immediate issue that will cost less but was warned that it may not be the only issue)
3. Synthetic oil changes are surprisingly inexpensive

a) Apparently they never looked at or even noticed that my engine was scrap and charged me for a damn transmission repair that was worthless.

b) It took so long to tell me the bad news

text:
My car was leaking or losing water, I didn't know why. I brought it to the shop, told them the problem, and asked them to do a thorough check. I emphasized that I needed the car to be road-ready since I was planning to take some long trips. They called within three hours, which was nice and fast, and told me I had a leak in my water pump and it needed replacing. They quoted me $350. I was like...damn. I told them to go ahead and do it. $350 is actually very cheap. The part alone costs at least $250, and it's located inside the engine. So everything has to be taken apart just to get to it. Labor alone would be around 5-6hrs. Good deal, right? I also asked them to do a transmission flush, by the way.

Two days later, I pick up my car. Pay. They tell me everything is fine now. I should bring it back soon for a hundred thousand mile check-up. Okay, fine.

I drive for about an hour and I find my car having the same problem as before. W...T...F
What did I just pay close to $500 worth of work for? I bring it back, a day later the guy calls me and says I have a bad hose. It'll cost $80 to replace. REALLY?!?! It should be free! You replaced the wrong part! One that I didn't NEED. But oh, it's okay because he was offering a 10% discount on the labor....

When I pick up the car, he gives me the receipt. It states:
1. replaced two hoses for waterpump/engine
2. pressure check for water hose and engine
3. blah blah blah

Where was that pressure check the first time? Where was it when they decided the problem was my water pump? Where was it AFTER they installed the water pump? It was such a hassle to go back and forth when this was my ONLY car. And all that money gone for no reason. I will never go back. It makes me wonder if my water pump was even ever replaced. It's not a visible part, so I will never really know.

So here is the real problem. This place is getting so much business that they have to cut corners. They're too busy to do the little things anymore.... like appreciating the customers they have!

While I realize this was not necessary as I would've likely paid for repairs had I been asked first, he went ABOVE AND BEYOND what most businesses would do. And he took care of all of this within 1 business day. Tell me another business that would've done the same thing with the same expediency, and they've got my business too.

Because of their integrity, open communication, and willingness to work with the customer, Almaden Auto Repair now has my trust for future car repairs, and I can wholeheartedly recommend Thai and his business to friends and family without any reservations. Even if you're not from Almaden, it's worth coming here knowing you can trust the customer service here.

text:
My brakes have been squealing for a while. So I did some research and some searching around for repair. I called a day early to set up an appointment, the owner Thai was courteous and asked to call again tomorrow to schedule it I ensured I would go during my lunch break and he said it was fine. I got a quote for the cost to replace my front brakes and was eager to schedule for the next day.

The next day I dropped my car off and got a ride back to my office. two hours later (most likely to wait for the brakes to cool down) Thai called my cell to ensure what I was going to have replaced, he suggested since I haven't had my brakes flushed to do that. Also asked if my oil was changed recently (all of which I haven't done for a while). I complied as it was already in the shop and I knew it needed these things. Nothing more was added as I've kept my fluid levels good and nothing else was wrong with my car (2007 Nissan Sentra). An hour and half later Thai called to report that my car was ready to be picked up. I asked if I can come near the end of day 5:30-5:45. Thai said that was fine.

I was able to get to the shop at 5:50, I walked in, Thai remembered my name as I was in there 6 hours prior and asked to give him a moment to finalize everything, I sat down and he handed me a little bottle of coke. I watched the news for a little while and drank the soda that was offered to me and he handed me the bill. 

$257 was the total charged. I was quoted: $175 brake parts/labor, $26 for oil change, $60 for brake flush. After looking over I remember what was said over the phone and the difference from what I was charged. 

After adjusting my seat I drove away pleased at the fixes made for my vehicle.

The reason for creating a yelp account: I went in on Monday (5/26/2011) to get this work done. On Tuesday evening at 7:28pm Thai gave me a call to ask how the car was driving and if everything was well with the car. I replied that everything was great and he thanked me and told me to have a nice day.

Unparalleled service, I've been living in the bay area for 2 years now and am blown away at the level of professionalism. Thank you very much!

-Grant

Edit: I noticed my tires were rotated. It would have been more beneficial to be told it was going to happen, but they were in need of being rotated. My MPG has gone since though, so I think I may need to have them rotate back.

Edit2: I was sent a birthday card when it was my birthday and I've only been here once. I am definitely taking my car back.

text:
I brought my car in to address the clunking noises coming from the front suspension. 
I usually work on fixing my car by myself to save money, but a suspension job was something I felt was too advanced a skill level to do myself and I didn't have all the tools needed to complete the tasks myself. I also am going back to school soon at the time of this writing so I didn't have enough time left to do the work myself. 

I had to leave my car there overnight. 
I provided them all the parts that I purchased ahead of time just in case, and understand that there's no warranty for providing parts. 
I was skeptical at first as to why they charge me a lot for just labor , almost $600-700 initially. That's a lot for a poor college student like me. 

But overall they communicate very well with me and the office receptionist told me on the phone what's wrong and I agree to authorize them to replace both the front struts, sway bar links, and a wheel alignment. They also discovered my brake fluid was very filthy and recommended replacing, which I also agree since I already had a brand new bottle of Honda genuine DOT 3 brake fluid stored in the trunk and told them to use that. I knew the brake fluid was dirty I checked it myself and was meaning to address that but I figured since they discovered it first I agree to have them do the brake fluid flush and replacement for me. 
I think at the end of it all their service is very good with this first time experience. 
I suppose the labor cost is fair, could have been way worse had I not provided them the parts. Could have skyrocketed to $1000+ easily if I don't have the parts. 

My only minor complaints are: 
-why can't I request to talk directly to the mechanic I'm case I had questions or just wanted to hear their opinions and experience when they were replacing parts and working on my car. Are they busy working on other people's cars? I only was provided the receptionist/ service advisor to talk to that relayed my questions to the mechanic. I found that odd. 
-I noticed that my driver side floor mat was dirtier than when I left my car. Same when I noticed dirty hand prints on the driver side door handle. I suggest they should have at least put in those disposable paper floor mats and wear gloves. 

I used the $5 check in discount for my repair bill. 

Overall very good service and reasonable turnaround time , I got my car back the very next day. Though I had to pedal my bicycle to and from there from my rental room residence in Japan town since I don't have anyone else I knew to give me a ride there. 
I may consider bringing my car back next time maybe in case I have any other mechanical concerns.

We're literally have a sign when you walk in that says grab this form fill it out drop off your keys and come back in 4-5 hours.

I've typically had my car serviced at the dealership, so I really wasn't sure what was needed for the car service. I filled out the paperwork and put oil change, tire rotation, and a multi-point inspection -- basics, I figured. I received a call about an hour after dropping off my car for suggested services: engine air filter replacement, lubing all mechanical parts and the belt, and topping off all the fluids. We received a quote for all of this, thought it was fair, and decided to proceed. My car ended up being finished earlier than expected, a plus for my husband and I.

They accept credit card payments, although I forgot which cards they accept. They have a parking lot with a reasonable amount of spaces, although the lot can surely fill up quickly (per my husband during pre-COVID times). There isn't much to do around the area, so my suggestion is to have someone go with you so you're not stuck waiting on site. 

I will be back for my future auto repair needs, and I think I've found my "go to" auto shop for the San Jose area.

My issue is with quality of work or lack there of with the Mechanics. I dropped off my car for a simple front and rear brake job. Never had any issues before so I didn't expect anything different this time. Well after I received my car the first thing i notice is there's scuff marks on the door jams and also black stains on the interior. Mind you my Lexus is about 10 yrs old but i treat it with kid gloves. I have a tan interior carpet and seats so you imagine how i felt after seeing the big mess left behind in my car. Sure I could've talked with the staff before I left the shop but to me it was common sense that if your getting into any car with oiled up boots you'd put down some sort of protective covering inside to prevent any issues but I guess common sense isn't always common. The other issue i noticed after getting on the freeway was my steering wheel was off center. I immediately called and told them about my issue to which i received a "We don't touch the suspension for a brake job" so i replied that i don't normally drive my Lexus with an off centered steering wheel that wasn't like this when I brought it in this morning. They asked to bring the car back and they would look at it but i got bad vibes from the overall experience and decided to take my care to an alignment specialty shop and got my problem fixed. The person that performed the alignment said it was grossly out of alignment but he was able to fix the problem. Although it had been some time since I've had an alignment the car was fine. text:
I brought in my 2007 Toyota Yaris (automatic) for squeaking brakes 06/23/2021. These were new brakes from just that past October (replaced at another shop. That is another, seperate story). I initially chose Almaden Auto Repair because they had a large number of pretty decent reviews on Yelp. 

I left my car at AAR while they inspected it and got a call later that day from an employee saying my transmission is producing a "grinding" sound and that they "didn't hear any squeaking from the brakes." Which is ridiculous because it is quite obvious of a sound and happens *every time* I brake. I have also never heard any suspicious sounds from my transmission and have had no Check Engine lights appear for any reason. I go in to hear what they are talking about and while my car is idling, I do hear a sound, though I would never describe it as grinding, it was more of a rattling sound. They claimed it was my "transmission axle bearing" which just doesn't really make sense as a description. They said that my transmission needs to be replaced and estimated me at $3600 and said it would take 2 weeks to repair. I said "No thank you", paid the diagnostic fee, and left. 

After much research online and calling other shops around for estimates, they not only weren't making sense with their description of the diagnosis (nor the description of the sound/when the sound would occur), but the consensus is that $3600 for replacing a transmission on a 2007 Toyota Yaris is INSANE. That's more than half the value of my entire CAR.

But all of this aside, I have personally found the cause of the rattling ("grinding") noise they were claiming was my transmission... My hood-stand doesn't have a proper latch and I have a short bungee cord that wraps over the top of my car battery to hold it down (Used car. Didn't come with the piece to hold my battery in place) and I tuck the hood-stand under that cord... because it *rattles* if I don't. Problem fixed and rattling completely gone.

I also feel it is worth mentioning that I am a woman. I know a fair amount about cars and tend to do my own repairs when I can. (I live in a city and don't have a garage at the moment, which is why I was looking to have it taken in.) They took advantage of that and I'm assuming they tried to scam me thinking I would accept their word as gospel. While the transmission's inner workings isn't my strongest point in my knowledge of cars, I knew enough to be incredibly suspicious of what was going on. 

TL;DR, On 06/23/2021, Almaden Auto Repair tried to pass off the sound of my hood-stand rattling on the battery as a "transmission axle bearing problem" and attempted to get me to pay $3600 (a WILDLY inflated expense) for a new transmission I absolutely didn't and do not need.

It needs jump up if the car is not used for more than 2-3 days. I checked the car at three repair shops and got a quit different diagnosis from each shop. I pick up Almaden Auto Repair for his high Yelp review even it is more expensive than others.

I paid $195 for the testing to confirm their diagnosis. I was told that aster the testing, the root cause of the startup problem is the defected Alternator. I paid $235 for the labor of alternator replacement (the new part purchased by myself). 
After the alternator replacement, they found the car still has a problem at startup. And they asked to replace the starter. At this point, I am hesitated to spend another $400-$500 to the car which is only worth ~$2000. Who knows the car can start up smooth or not after starter replacement. I am asking Almaden Auto Repair do some more test before any part replacement. Hopefully, they can find the real root cause for the startup problem. 
I gave them two stars rating for now as I feel they are not sound in technical experience. I will update my review late time if I change my mind.

Revising/Update (change 2 stars to 4 stars rating)

I had a check engine light on and I was assisted by Minh. I explained to him all the issues i was experiencing to potentially assist in diagnosing the problem. My cylinders were misfiring.

Upon my own research, a compression test should have been done the first time I brought it in based on the issues i was experiencing and it wasn't. They are very fast paced and have a lot of cars at their shop, with what 2 mechanics. Felt they didn't really take the time to assess my vehicle, beware! The quality is as good as--or better than--the dealership, using original Toyota parts, but without dealership prices. No middleman, no customer service rep--just straight answers from the person actually working on your car. He also documents major repairs with before-and-after photos and will even check in a day or two later to make sure everything's driving well.

Most importantly, they're honest, reliable, and trustworthy. I've never had an issue in the 10+ years I've been coming here.

If you're looking for a shop you can actually trust, I highly recommend TLS Auto Service.
