text:
I'm a new customer of Anthony's shop. I'm super happy with the work and customer service. I had just purchased a used 2005 Toyota Sequoia and wanted to establish a relationship with a local mechanic with Toyota expertise, and to have the vehicle checked over by them. I had purchased it out of state and had it checked out there, but they were also the mechanic for the seller, so I wanted my own new mechanic to also check it out.

Anthony did an oil change, but his oil changes are not just simple oil changes - they include tire rotation, safety check, just all kinds of regular maintenance that I wasn't expecting.

He also attempted to fix a couple of known issues, like the back window motor being frozen. He was able to get it to work without my having to buy a very expensive new motor, although it did end up seizing again. He did try to save me money and spent more time trying to fix it than he charged me for. I've decided that it's not important anyway, and as he had advised, some things are just not worth fixing on older vehicles, if they're just not that important. I really don't need that window, anyway.

Which is my next point. Anthony is really about advising you to do - or not do - things that he would or wouldn't do if he owned the vehicle, himself. It was even kind of funny, because there were a couple of cosmetic things that I was ready to waste money on and he kind of forcefully talked me out of it LOL. He's passionate in not wasting money, which I really appreciate.

One of the known issues was that the mechanism to open the hood was missing. You could still reach your fingers through the grill and pull on the main mechanism to open it, but the arm that extends from there to the bottom of the hood, where you'd normally grab it to open the hood - was missing. I had asked Anthony to go ahead and order new parts for that.

However, some of those parts are no longer available, and I'd have to order one from a parts puller at a junk yard. Rather than have me waste money on that, his technician devised a work-around part, by attaching a wire and a rubber o-ring which was easier to grab to open the hood - and didn't charge me anything for it. So, it opens up just fine, and saved me unnecessary expenses there, too.

Another thing he saved me money on - I was going to spend money on a catalytic converter shield - which he does install, by the way - and he told me that because of the way my first gen Sequoia is built, the way the catalytic converter is placed, it would be too much of a time-consuming hassle for any thief to remove, that they'd never bother with it, so I shouldn't waste money on that, either.

He also sent me text messages letting me know where they were at with ordering parts, etc. (I'd told him there was no hurry getting the vehicle back to me), and he also sent me a follow-up text a month later, asking me how the vehicle was doing. Wow.

I was so happy with his service, I asked him to put two of his license plate covers that advertise his shop - on my Sequoia - he'll give them to you for free.

Then, the funny thing is, I had to go to the Toyota dealer across the street from his shop (where he actually used to work) to have them take care of an open recall on the Sequoia, and I had Anthony's license plate covers on the vehicle, and the customer service guy in charge of the mechanics who was helping me with the recall, saw the plates and made a comment about how Anthony used to work for them and looked a tad annoyed, LOL, because when he tried to get me to do some other maintenance stuff with the dealership, I told him Anthony was taking good care of me. He then said he was glad when his technicians were able to open their own shops, but didn't look like he meant it :-)

Go to Anthony for anything you don't need the dealership for, is my advice. He'll save you a ton of money and you'll get way better customer service, and feel confident he's not going to rip you off. He told me I didn't need a new battery or new brakes yet - the dealership tried to tell me I needed them. 

Too bad Anthony can't also do the recall work. Thanks Anthony! See you in February for my next oil change, brakes and battery and whatever else you say it needs. I totally trust you :-)

text:
OK so I have a 2002 Toyota Sienna with 200k on it.
It started to use oil, so I just topped it up once or twice a month instead of changing the oil/filter. 
Then it failed smog. Ouch. But the Sienna has been such a great beast I decided to find a smog repair man. I came to find out that fixing smog on older cars is not easy or cheap--unless "just replacing the gas cap" works.
Emission controls require really good computer diagnostics and the ability to interpret the Fail modes for the likely causes. The old Sienna had four fail modes, each requiring a new emission component and a long test drive...and then a re-check. 
Anthony stayed on it for a week, replacing only the needed components one by one and reverifying, and got the Sienna down to one problem with the catalytic converter efficiency. Rather than just replace it (very very expensive) Anthony thought that a routine oil change might help unburden the exhaust system. But it would take another long drive to flush out the carbon so I took a 5 day road trip and came back to TLS for yet another free diagnostic.
IT WORKED! Passed smog! It took two weeks total, and cost around $1000. But now I am going to get two more years out of the SIenna thanks to Anthony at TLS. Considering how much was involved, I believe I saved a ton of $ vs the Toyota dealer.

text:
First of all, I would like to be as impartial as I can with my review below. My goal is to inform customers of my experience, and not to cause any ill-will towards this business. Since there are no 1/2 star rating increments, I gave this business a 3-star review, but feel 2.5 stars is a more adequate review. 

In addition, if you have any questions regarding my review, please feel free to send me a Yelp message. 

Anyway, here's my review:

In advance I messaged two times to Anthony that I wanted the 120,000 mile service for my Toyota Camry. He confirmed my 120K service by Yelp messaging. In addition, when I brought the car to his shop, I confirmed again that I wanted the 120K service done. However, Anthony performed the 30K service. I know this because I reviewed my Toyota car manual's recommended 120K mile service and not all services were performed. Obviously I am not a car expert so I am giving him the benefit of the doubt that the services he did perform were done properly.

When I picked up my car he recommended several additional services to be done, including having the spark plugs changed, which is part of the Toyota Camry recommended 120K service. Why he did not perform this service I do not know as when I contacted him later by email and asked about this and some of the additional services he recommended, he did not give any answer. I asked two times with no reply. 

Of note, one of the additional services he recommended be done for my car when I picked it up was to replace the spark plugs.

Because of this, I will be bringing my car to another shop for a second opinion regarding my concerns and the additional work.

My recommendations after bringing my car to this location (or any location) are many:

1. When obtaining service, ask exactly what will be done (and why) if you are not sure. The reason for this is that some services are necessary but some may not be but are done anyway. After obtaining opinions from a different service center, I was informed that some services are done for the benefit of the shop and not for the benefit of the customer. Likewise, some services that should be performed may not be (see #3 below).

2. Ask for an itemized receipt of all services performed and parts/products used. I don't see why parts/products and costs of each item are not listed unless the shop has something to hide.

3. Do your homework when it comes to services needed. For example, if you bring your car in for a 120K mile service, know what services/parts are recommended by the manufacturer and find out if the auto shop you go to will or will not be doing such recommended services. If the shop is performing additional services/replacing parts that are NOT manufacturer recommended at the time, ask why. 

4. Get second or third opinions. There are many service locations available that are willing to answer your questions/concerns, either by phone or email, prior to bringing your car in for an estimate or service. 

5. Common sense says there should be honesty/integrity/trust and openness when it comes to any business relationship. A car owner is trusting the business and the business should honor that trust.

6. Lastly, take Yelp reviews with a grain of salt. A shop with many 5-star ratings doesn't always mean 5-star work of 5-star service. 

I will be updating this review once I obtain a second/third opinion(s) on the additional work recommended and the concerns I still have about my car since my service here.

text:
I really wanted to like this business, based on the overwhelming number of positive reviews here.

The first time I came here for my car was in June of 2013 for a 135k service. I bought the car at 105k, and was still searching for a mechanic I could trust with it. Dan was very thorough with his inspection, replacing spark plugs, the rear wheel cylinder, and the valve cover gaskets. 

He also listed his recommendations for repairs in the near future. These included A/C service, a power steering flush, a transmission flush, and rear shocks. Like I said, my car's fairly old, and while I wasn't happy about the scope of the possible repair bill, these seemed like plausible recommendations, and I decide I'd take care of those at a later date. 

We get the phone call to pick up the car because the repairs are done. 5 minutes into the drive, the "Check Engine" light comes on. I take it back to TLS, where Dan informs me that the O2 sensor had some oil drip on to it, causing it to malfunction. He tells me that the shaky condition of my car engine means that this was a fluke occurrence, and he's not responsible for it. 

I'm not happy with this outcome, and end up getting 2 other opinions; both other mechanics agree that this was unacceptable, and afterward, Dan agrees to replace the O2 sensor, at his cost. He's not happy about it, and he acts differently than when I first spoke with him. He gets a lot more terse, and when he does talk, it's with this defensive edge with things like, "This other shop didn't see [this other mechanical issue]" or "I always do [this good mechanical practice]."

Anyway, because he made good on fixing the problem, I'm satisfied. Not thrilled with his attitude, but I don't write critical Yelp reviews lightly. (Check my other reviews. I try to focus on the positive, because I know that it's hard running a small business.) Also, because things are now weird with TLS, I decide to find a different mechanic. 

So last week (early August, 2014), I end up going to a different mechanic for my 150k service. Things are mostly okay. Both the front and the rear shocks still need attention, and the valve cover gaskets are leaking again. I check my records and confirm that, huh, I got those changed 14 months and 14,000 miles ago.

I call TLS, and they say, yeah, that shouldn't be happening, and to bring the car back in so they can take care of me. 

I do that, and walk in through the door to explain the situation. 

Dan's behind the counter, and before I finish talking, he says very tersely, "Yes. I remember you." Not in a friendly way, but a way that makes me think, "Oh, man. This is gonna be awkward." 

He puts the car up on the rack, and in response to my concerns, including the valve cover gaskets and the shocks, tells me that none of them are problematic. The valve cover gaskets only look like they're leaking from the residual oil stains from how messy my engine was in the past, he says. The valve cover gaskets should last 100,000 miles, and there's nothing wrong with the ones he installed, he says. 
The shocks will eventually have to be replaced, but it's an old car, and it's heavy, and he says they're not a problem. The whole inspection takes maybe 10 minutes, tops. 

On top of it, he's still doing the weird attitude thing again. He points to the oil filter and tells me the other shop was sloppy. He quickly puts a little air in the tires and says nothing's wrong with the shocks (even though HE recommended replacing them a year ago!), but that the other shop didn't bother to put air in my tires. There's all this little passive-aggressive finger-pointing behavior that just makes me want to get out of there ASAP. 

So I nod, take the car in to a 3rd mechanic, who confirms the problems with the valve cover gaskets, and the shocks. FWIW, the other two mechanics not involved in this review have Yelp scores of 4 and 5 stars, respectively. And neither of them pulled any passive-aggressive communication with me, either.

3 stars for the first repair encounter; 1 star for the customer service; 1 star for the latest repair encounter. I'd like to give a 1.5, but because I can only give whole numbers, I'll have to round up to a 2.

text:
Seriously one of the BEST auto service EVER. 

Here's why:

I bought my friend's 2006 Lexus IS250 from him. He took excellent care of his car from the very beginning so I knew it was such a great deal when he was planning to sell it. After a couple of weeks of owning the car, the navigation burned out. I was so bummed out- it stopped responding and all the settings that I had on prior before it shorted out was stuck on that setting. So I was driving around with AC blasting, no music, no bluetooth, no navi-- nothing! 

After googling my car's demise, I quickly found out that this was a very common problem for this model. And that it was going to cost an unreasonable amount to get it repaired ($1800-$2500!!!! my eyes bulged as my jaw dropped).... unless I followed a DIY video and knew what to detach, cut, and solder. Yeah right. Although the tutorial was great, it might as well have been in German, because I had no clue nor the confidence to even begin such a project like that. So what next? Well, like what many of you are doing right now... I turned to Yelp to explore any other options out there. And thank god I found TLS Auto Service. 

I called for a quote and Kevin answered the phone. Super super helpful and very friendly. He referred me to Dan who was more familiar with the problem, and right away he knew exactly was going on (what a relief!!). Told me to casually stop by and he'll see what he can do. 

When I came to his shop, my hopeful feelings of getting my navigation screen being repaired at a fair price was immediately being enforced. Not only did he THOROUGHLY explained why, but HOW to prevent the issue. He ensured me that he'll take care of me and that I shouldn't worry-- and that is exactly how it was. Simple. He tackled the issue head on, got me a GREAT price, and went ABOVE and BEYOND to get everything done.

My unit was shipped to a couple places out of state, but the shops told him that it was unrepairable and they suggested to get a new unit (2000++). But Dan was persistent! When he got the unit back, he personally took it somewhere local and was able to fix it for more than HALF the price of a brand new one. He could have easily have told me that I would have to get a new unit, but he stuck to his word and sincerely did take great care of me and my car. 

What I also appreciate was the constant updates I would get via text. He responded quickly to all my texts and he was upfront about everything from the very beginning. 

I will DEFINITELY be a returning customer! And I also have my parents and husband getting their car serviced here as well. TLS Auto Service is a GEM! Excellent service through and through! It really doesn't get better than this-- seriously!!

Dan is the MAN!!!!!!

text:

Our 2006 Toyota Prius was involved in a front end collision over a year ago and required extensive repairs. 14 months later, all of the warning lights started going off and the car began running very, very sluggishly. Not wanting to take the car to the dealer, whom we mistrust, we found TLS on Yelp and decided to give them a try.

Needless to say, we were not anxious to pay for such an expensive repair on a car with 120k miles on it. With Dan's help, he worked with the Insurance Adjuster to prove that the damage to the battery was indeed caused by the accident 14 months prior - a very difficult task. But because of Dan's expertise with these cars, the adjuster approved the repair and the entire thing was covered by our insurance company. 

Now, we've got our car back and it's running better than ever. Dan kept in touch with us every step of the way and provided constant updates about what was happening and his interactions with the insurance company. I could not be more impressed or pleased with the experience I had with TLS and would recommend them without hesitation!

text:
As a proud owner of a Prius, I'm very particular about making sure that I get the right and high quality service for my car. Up until last month, I always used to take the car to the Toyota dealer service to get maintenance & repair work done. Well, I was clearly wrong. I took the car to the dealer's service center for a 5k minor service that included oil change etc that runs for about $70; however it turned out the service advisor pointed out I needed a whole bunch work done, i.e. water pump, coolant replacement, drive pump, front struts replaced, rear shocks changed, air and cabin filter replaced for just $1,800 (yes, eighteen hundred dollars). At that point, I panicked and started yelping to see which auto mechanic would be able to save me some serious dough and provide their honest opinion. So I denied Toyota dealer's service advise and repair work, and literally hopped across the street from them to get Dan & Anthony's second opinion at TLS Auto Service. He took a look at my paper work that the dealer provided, grabbed his flash light and started inspecting the vehicle. To my surprise, Dan pointed out that I didn't need half the repair work that the dealer was suggesting. That $1,800 repair work came down to under $450. It turned out that I didn't need new struts, and then the rear shocks could easily last for another 1 year or 10k - 15k miles. So remaining work that really needed was the water pump, drive belt, coolant replacement and the air, & cabin filters; all for merely $450. This included original Toyota parts, labor, and taxes. WOW, what a deal! So I scheduled the repair work within 2 days and the car was ready within 4 hours. It was delivered on time, as Dan and Anthony (partners/mechanics of TLS Auto) as promised, with no hastles, BS, or headaches that the dealer gave me. After the water pump replacement work was done, I did notice the water gushing/flowing noise when I accelerated, so I quickly called Dan; he assured me that within a couple of days of driving it should adjust automatically and stop making noise. Sure enough, there was no problem/noise within 2 days of driving. Honest Dan, even text'd me personally to follow up and ensure the car was running smoothly. At that point, I knew that these guys were honest and genuine in their craftsmanship. 

If you or your friends/relatives own a Toyota, Lexus or Scion vehicles, then definitely go to TLS Auto Service. At least get a 2nd opinion before you decide to flush your money down the pipe at a dealer's service center.

Good job Dan and Anthony: 5 stars all the way!!!

text:
My last review was about TLS service for my Toyota Sienna 2000 back in July 2013. After that service, it was an easy decision for me to bring my Camry 2003 to TLS for service.

I was facing a decision to buy a new car which is an expensive option, or having the Camry fixed up to drive reliably for few more years. I asked Dan to evaluate and to give me options considering that I do need the car for long distance trips. Dan had the car evaluated and recommended me 2 options:

1) At the minimum replacing the water pump as it was leaking, and while at it replacing all the belts, and also replacing some electrical components including spark plugs and their wires set, some tune-up, AC, and coolant service.

2) If I want to keep the car for a long time, then I should consider fixing the engine block oil leaks.

Dan told me doing option 1 will be less than the cost of registration for a new car, and option 2 is not needed unless I really want to keep the car for another 10 years.

I listened to his words and took his advise with option 1, but waited for about 3 months now to write this review to see how things would pan out. The Camry not only has a slight improvement of performance, runs fine and the AC also works well during those last hot summer days.

With this level of service, I may want to keep both Sienna and Camry for another 10 years as I have someone who is honest, cares and looks out for my interests.

text:
Great customer service, competitive pricing, friendly people, and little things that the owner Dan does which in my mind go above and beyond any expectations I have for a shop.

I had to take in my Lexus RX SUV into TLS Auto Service for the timing belt, water pump, major maintenance and in the process a number of details such as the servo motor replacement which was causing this clicking sound in the interior of the car which I've put up with for a number of years.

When it came time to get an estimate, Dan provided me with a text of the list of items that would need to be fixed and kindly asked me to stop by to ensure he could properly explain to me all the items he was quoting to do.

After reviewing the list he had quoted, and confirming his pricing was competitive, I went ahead and had him start the process. Throughout the process he had sent me updated texts with pictures on the type of work he was doing along with the genuine Lexus/Toyota parts he was replacing in my SUV.

The servo motor that he had replaced (which is a common problem in the Lexus RX model SUV's), he initially quoted me for one, but in fact there were two so he ended up replacing both of the motors, and did not charge me for the 2nd one because he stuck to his quote. Any other mechanic could have easily called me and asked me to authorize the charge for the 2nd motor, but Dan did not do that and stuck to his original quote/word - which I am truly grateful for, he saved me a few hundred dollars.

I also appreciated the fact that I could stand in his shop and look through the glass to see him and his guys working on my car. After learning that I was interested in viewing the type of work they were doing for my car, there were times where Dan would call me over (from his waiting area) and show me what he was replacing and answer any questions I had about the repair work he was doing.

Granted, I did spend a few thousand dollars in repair work, but I would rather spend money up front for preventative purposes and follow the maintenance schedule on a car, then suffer the catastrophic failure and more expensive repair later on for my neglected car, not to mention sitting on the side of the road waiting for the towing truck - which thankfully I've never had to go through as I try to keep my cars in good mechanical shape.

After the repair work was done, he provided an itemized and printed out invoice for me to keep of the work that was completed.

I was so impressed with Dan, Kevin, and Anthony's level of work that I went ahead and brought in my Acura for him to take a look at. Even though he doesn't specifically work on non Lexus, Toyota, and Scion cars, but for a customer, he treated me like a friend and still took care of me nonetheless.

I've been to other auto repair shops that have amazing reviews, but like other Yelpers commented, you have to book in advance and unless it's an emergency, they will not be able to see you right away. In addition, for little things/parts that sometimes need to be replaced, I'd prefer to take it into someone who can see me sooner than later and help take care of me versus booking an appointment at least a week in advance.

I felt that bringing my cars to Dan to help look at and repair, he gave me the personal attention that I appreciated, and also allowed me to observe any repair work they did. 

This is one of the reasons I like bringing my cars into a trusted mechanic vs another auto shop or dealership. In the past, when I brought my car into the dealership, I would wait for sometimes hours in their lounge area, only to talk with the service manager and never get to see the parts used and the type of work they did to my car, aside from an invoice.

It's not that I don't trust people, but if you end up spending a few dollars up to thousands of dollars, it's always nice to know that the mechanics are actually putting in the parts and spending the time/labor to work on the repair of your vehicle, and in my mind, being able to see them do it with my own eyes is a nice relief/peace of mind and also a good experience for me to understand/learn more about my own car and how to better take care of it.

Dan's shop also provides a 1 year warranty on their labor, the same warranty that the dealership provides on any repair work.

text:
Wow. I've used other mobile mechanics to do pre-purchase inspections (PPIs) before, but never has one been so thorough and diligent! Other mechanics only looked at the most basic stuff, and one even lead me to purchase a car with several issues that should have been obvious to him ... but not Mobile Auto Works!

Charles from Mobile Auto Works found not one but four different issues: a tire was damaged (which caused the alignment to be off), the coolant was low, there was an alarm installed on the car (that the seller didn't even mention and probably had no fob for), and the front/rear bumpers had been repainted and reattached incorrectly ... all of this despite the seller being a dealer (how did they not check the coolant?) and despite the seller reporting that the vehicle hadn't been in any accidents (when it clearly had).

In short, our $140 was very well spent saving us from buying a car that was worth roughly $1000 less than we thought. My only complaint is that the next car we're considering is in San Francisco, which is outside of Mobile Auto Works coverage area ... but I can't really fault them for that.

text:
My car wouldn't crank. These days it's easy to check the battery so i did, but the problem was further into the circuit. I didn't want to have it towed in, so called Charles.

He explained all the possibilities over the phone, including how he could have parts for the most common failures (in this case, starter motor and solenoid, and perhaps some others). He actually has a pretty good system worked out: when you decide on him, you just text him a message with your location, then confirm the day before. (I had to do it on a weekend to avoid missing work.)

Anyhow, he came out, and worked systematically from the most reachable parts of the starter circuit (the battery) towards the starter. He verified the state of the battery, and discovered pretty quickly it was the solenoid. Actually, i guess i should say the 'remote' solenoid, as this vehicle has one that's close to the top and another close to the starter itself. Charles explained all that to me, and the rationale for why it was done that way, and then replaced the unit. (He also explained why there were so many cables connected to it, besides just the switch, input, and output.) His testing was pretty methodical, going from the most accessible elements of the circuit to the least accessible ones.

Because he was so fast, i thought i'd bring up another problem that i had, which was the way the transmission had been behaving. He said, "Let's check", and did so very quickly. This was not something he could have prepped for because i mentioned nothing about it on the phone. It was low. So he verified with his database that he had the right sort of transmission fluid for the car, and brought it to the right level. He showed me how to read it, and also how he could tell that it was at operating temperature (so that the readings would be correct).

And even in bringing it to the right level, he was methodical, not just dumping in a bunch at once, but putting in a little, then a little more, and so on until the reading was just right.

So not only does the car now crank, but it drives a lot better than it did before.

He seems to have good tools, and understands how to use them well, as well as knowing a lot about cars.

So i'd recommend him very highly.

text:
I called up Mobile Auto Works on a very short notice - had decided on buying a used car and wanted to do it soon, but needed a professional opinion. Based on Yelps' suggestion I called Charles Armstrong. I asked him whether he could drive down to a dealership in a couple of hours. Can be done, he said. So that was that.

I was not sure whether spending money on another "opinion" was good idea. But I was convinced otherwise in a very short time. Charles scrutinized the car closely, uncovered that it had been in a minor accident that the Carfax report didn't show (!), spotted a coolant leak, a shock leak, and bunch of minor issues. Had I not got his opinion one or more of the following would have happened:

1. I would have discovered each of these things during my first servicing of the car and felt cheated.
2. Something would have broken down before I got to my first servicing. Apart from the cost of the fix, I may have had to suffer through hauling the car (or paying for it) from the middle of nowhere to a workshop.
3. If I discovered the problems individually, on separate occasions, I'd have to pay for service charge (say, for diagnosis) piecemeal. Now I have been told everything that is wrong with my car in one go.

You'd agree none of the above look very appealing.

Based on the report Charles handed me (he carries a printer in his vehicle, true Lincoln lawyer style) the dealer has agreed to negotiate. Now I don't know yet how much would they lower the price - too early to say - but nevertheless, I am very happy with the service and decided to leave a review.

If you're a layman considering purchase of a used vehicle, don't think twice - get this guy to look at whatever you have decided on. If nothing, it will help you factor in the costs of maintenance and fixes needed down the line.

text:
Hire. This. Guy. 
That's it, end of review. 
Not really, I'm a woman and we talk. Sooooo...

My husband and I have used Charles of Mobile Auto Works on not one, not two, but on THREE occasions. Our first experience was when we hired him to fix my possessed '05 Mercedes C230K. He came to my job and immediately went on a ride-along with me to diagnose a few issues. In short, he fixed what was wrong and then further quoted me for another job I inquired about (on top of a couple of other existing issues), but it's pretty lofty $ to repair. I told him I just wanted to get rid of it because I was about to enter the market for a new car within the next few months anyway. And he's so honest and straightforward, yet could have been greedy and convinced me otherwise so he could make money off of it, but even he said to basically be done with the car. And then... Two weeks later, Hubby's car died. So, we were kinda forced to keep the Benz and my better half wants his wifey in a new, reliable car- #realman. So, we decided to hold on to the MBZ and drive it until its death; it's a literal "ride-or-die" ride. 

Now, let me tell you about Charles and his "worth-every-penny when you have him show up at the car dealership with all his gadgets, tools, and printer to help you get the price lower" skills. 

Last March, we had him do a pre-inspection on a sickkkk '14 Ford Explorer Sport, all blacked out, might I add. He found that the vehicle is generally in really great shape, but was able to detect a few things that the dealership was trying to let slide during their "172-point(less?)" inspection. 
So, needless to say, Charles' inspection report helped us slay at the dealership and we rolled out in our new-to-us SUV! 5 days later, I went back to the dealership to get four brand new tires and a battery as part of the sales deal thanks to the information Charles armed us with for negotiations. A year and three months later, the truck is still running smoothly and we haven't needed to call Charles for anything on it!

Now remember the Mercedes? Well, she served her purpose well and we were forced to put her to sleep two weeks ago. We immediately went searching for her replacement, and happened upon a pretty, shiny 2017 pre-owned convertible Mustang. Of course, our first step was to hit up Charles again and have him come through. And come through he did as he spent a great amount of time inspecting every, single detail. While this muscle car was absolutely gorgeous from hood to trunk, the insides were a mess. And that's what I've noticed tends to happen when you have a current-year vehicle that was a... previous rental with 35k on the odometer (I know, what we're we thinking?!.). Charles was able to find a few too many issues for us to move forward with purchasing it. His exact words were, "If I were you, I'd just move on to the next." And move on we did. We opted for a brand new Dodge Challenger with 8 whole miles on its block. And you know how when you get a new whip, you take that "keys in hand, standing next to the car, huge all-teeth smile, while still at the dealership" money shot that you send to yo mama, yo daddy and yo bff? Yeah we did that, except we added one more recipient- Charles. I'm pretty sure he thinks we made a better decision... Unless he's not a Dodge fan. Lol. But Dodge fanatic or not, it doesn't matter, we are fans of Charles, and you should be too! Give him a call, you'll be glad you did. 

Thanks Charles!

replies: [{'id': 'OkeSX1iswuRV11HeOp1x6Q', 'text': "Thank you for the feedback Yu. You hired us to *diagnose* the check engine light not to fix the problem, as for fixing the problem we first have to know what the issue is before we can say we can fix it. When we ran the codes for the check engine light, you had multiple misfire codes. Every single cylinder had registered having a misfire! With only 50k miles it was too soon for spark plugs. The sensor that was in question was your mass air flow. Once we started the motor we noticed the motor was misfiring randomly. One of the first things we did was unplug the mass air flow sensor. Right after unplugging the M.A.F. the misfires went away. We have had many BMW/Mini's start running great after doing this procedure. As far as the oil being low, low or no oil would have caused permanent damage to the internals of the motor. text:
For those of you thinking about buying a new used car call Mobile Auto Works before you do. It will save you money in the long run to know if the car you intend to buy has hidden problems and Charles can help you negotiate a fair price.

Here's my experience:

I was hoping to buy a 2010 Honda Fit from a private party, but didn't know very much about the inner workings of the car. I met with the owners, seemed like trustworthy people, test drove it, and everything seemed fine. We agreed to meet up the next day to fill out a deposit form in order to hold the card till Monday, when I could get the money I need from my bank. This sounded fair to me, but I wanted to make sure everything was in order before I put any sort of deposit into the car, so I called Mobile Auto Works, I was a little hesitant to hire a mechanic because I thought I was already going to be putting a lot of money into buying the car; I didn't want additional expenses. But I'm extremely happy that I did.

I had told the car owners that I would be over with the deposit at 2:30pm and that I had hired a mobile mechanic to take a look at it before we transferred any money, they agreed. When I arrived the owner began to rush me telling me that they had to leave soon and that they had other people that wanted to look at the car, I told them that I was serious about buying the car, and so long as everything was in good condition (like they said it was) I would not hesitate to buy the car. When the mechanic arrived the owner began to look nervous and agitated asking him how long it would take, when Charles said it could take up to an hour, the owner said she had to leave right away. Charles, My girlfriend, and I were all starting to become pretty suspicious... Charles defended me and spoke up to the owner while I just stood there baffled and confused. In the end the owner then said she had to go to work and got in the car and drove away.

I don't think I need to tell you that I didn't end up buying the car. If not for Charles I would most likely have been suckered into buying that car or just leaving them a deposit and having them run off with it. It was definitely worth the money to hire Charles, I intend to do so again when I look at my next used car.

text:
Charles is knowledgeable about cars but the price is not worth it. I requested help to look at my car that was not starting and had a coolant leak. I told him over the phone that it is probably the starter and the water pump. His charges were $50 to come out to my place and another $120 per hour. I thought that if he replaces the starter then it will be worth the trip. So I made an appointment, he showed up slightly late but I can understand there could be traffic. Looked at the car showed a trick to start the car and gave me a quote of $730+ to fix both and he told me that each requires ~1 1/2 hrs for a total of ~3 hrs. Additionally, he said that he did not have that much time that day so he will have to come back. All this he finished in ~15 mins and charged me $170. I felt ripped off to come and give me a quote of $730+ initially and then bringing it down to around $675 saying that since he did not use the complete hr he can give $60 towards the repair. 
I got the complete repair done in the shop for less than $475. So in a nutshell I got charged $170 to show the trick of starting the car with a bad started which is already available on youtube. 

The lesson learn't is before picking a mobile mechanic one needs to estimate whether the job can be finished in one hour, if not then it is just an expensive diagnosis call.

text:
WORDS CANNOT DESCRIBE MY APPRECIATION FOR AKIN.

I've been egregiously overcharged and upsold for service in the past. So much so that I've taken it upon myself to learn and replace and repair common maintenance fluids and consumables. I always get nervous whenever I have to bring a car in for a repair I cannot perform myself. To put it quite bluntly - I do not trust mechanics - but Akin and his brother were different from the start.

I had a vehicle that needed an axle replacement. I conducted over 6hrs of research from collecting part numbers, to understand the technical process of how the repair, to calling up over 10 Toyota dealerships and auto shops in the Bay Area before reaching out to Akin.

I originally called late in the afternoon. I did not know it at the time, but the shop was already supposed to be closed for the day. Akin is a straight shooter. I had a long list of questions and he patiently worked overtime to explain everything to me in detail.

What stood out to me was his use of data to justify his decision for materials and I assume his overall repair process. He tries to find the best part based on hard numbers such as the lowest percentage return rate.

Another item that stood out to me was his price and transparency. The quote I received was more than fair, and I knew this after comparing his material and labor rates with the 6 other individually owned auto shops. It was refreshing when he said something along the lines of "This conversation is recorded. My word is binding. I will not charge you over X dollars if you need this specific repair"

I took the vehicle first thing the very next day and Akin greeted me by name. His brother duplicated the issue and also performed a full inspection of the vehicle. The itemized list was sent to my email for review and we discussed what items were critical and others that could wait. text:
Akin and his team deserve more than 5 stars if I could rate them higher.

I work in the automotive industry as well and typically do all car repairs myself. But there are times when you need an extra hand. When looking for a good shop, unfortunately, people do encounter places where they try to upsell you or do shady business practices. But there are good people out there! Akin and his team are the good guys -- they are amazing. 

I've been to many shops, and I have to say that Akin's Auto Repair is by far my favorite shop in all of California. His shop is the cleanest I've seen, with a comfortable waiting room for customers + great amenities (Free, FAST WiFi, water, slot machine). 

Now on to the good stuff -- There's a reason why Akin's Auto Repair is so highly rated. Akin and his team are HONEST and CARING people who will tell you everything upfront and repair what they need to repair. If he has any recommendations, he will tell you and be transparent and reasonable with the repair process. Furthermore, his team works quickly and efficiently with quick turnaround times. For the level of service you get, his prices are more than reasonable (Very competitive with the competition). 

I understand exactly where Akin comes from. From my own experience working on customer's vehicles, customers may sometimes question why other parts are needed, or want to skip out on important maintenance. Akin understands this too and makes recommendations with the customer's safety as his top priority. 

As a plus, he and his team are very friendly, laid back, and easy to talk to/ask questions. I've been to many shops where the techs don't want to interact with customers -- maybe from being too busy, or just don't want to be transparent. Akin and his team however will chat with you about what repairs need to be done, so that the customer can be educated and understand exactly what is being done. 

Tl;dr: Coming from an experienced mech, Akin's Auto Repair gets more than 5 stars from me. 

Coming from a customer point of view, he offers high level of service, attention to detail, competitive and reasonable pricing, quick turnaround, and high satisfaction.

After doing further research, I realized I can do an internet purchase of the same new dealer parts (California specs) with much less cost ($560) from an out of the state Mazda dealer. Akin's auto give me an quote for the labor cost of $300. I went to Akin's auto yesterday, and got my in-tank fuel pump (it is a dangerous job because any sparks will ignite and explode the fuel tank) replaced within 3 hours of waiting at the air conditioned waiting room while enjoy the free-wifi in surfing the internet, watching the movies from my smartphone, the experience is quite enjoyable. This morning, I did a test start on the engine, the hard starting of my Mazda 3 has gone, it started immediately. I use the new genuine Mazda dealer parts (ordered out of the state) with the very fair labor cost from Akin's auto, I saved $450 totally compared with same repair if done in Mazda dealer, my car is running very well again. Thanks for Akin for the help.

text:
Why I tried Akin's Auto Repair:
I had been taking my car to another shop for years, but recently the quality of work and business practices at the other shop went downhill. The other shop replaced my timing belt and water pump about a year ago, and since then the engine made a very bad whining. I took the car back to the other shop several times to resolve the issue, but each time they said it was fixed, charged me hundreds of dollars to replace some easy to reach part, and when I got it back it was not fixed. There were some other things the other shop did that I won't go into, but needless to say I needed a new shop and one who could fix a problem the other shop likely caused.

My experience with Akin's Auto Repair:
First off...they found the problem and fixed it. THE FIRST TIME!!! And, Akin called me several times as they diagnosed the noise. It was a very difficult noise to diagnose because it was coming from seemingly inside the engine, but you can't take the engine apart, and also run it to hear the noise at the same time. They did have to try several things, but after the first thing they tried didn't work, Akin called and was very honest that they would need to replace the entire timing belt kit and water pump (the service the other shop did a year ago) in order to rule out any of the past shop's parts or work being the cause. I honestly was happy to have them re-do the work so I knew it would be done right.

They were right, and this solved the issue. Ultimately the water pump was the problem, and it appears it was damaged, possibly by the other shop when it was installed. Now, the engine purrs like a kitten. I'm so happy.

They put a lot more time into this than they charged me. Akin is clearly a very honest guy, and he wouldn't give up until my problem was solved properly. He over-communicated with me, which is awesome. Because of this I had full confidence in his approach, and that my car would actually get fixed this time.

Akin's is my new trusted mechanic, and I'll be bringing all of my cars here going forward.

There are a few things in life that one can truly appreciate. Car is such a big part of my life, I am a single father and drive about 70 miles each day between work and kids' schools and activities. Finding a trust-worthy mechanic for my car is one I put up there!

Thank you, Mr. Akin!!! I will be taking my car and all future cars to your shop from now-on! You just gained a lifelong customer!

text: After many years of having my car serviced at the dealer where I had bought it from, 4 years ago I started bringing it to Akin's for regular oil changes and any services/repairs. Akin never tries to upsell any unnecessary services (unlike some dealers or other repair shops) and when the car needs service, we plan it ahead of time so it doesn't catch you with surprise. text:
Akin's gets five stars from me because he's the no bullshit kind of mechanic you want working on your car. He was somehow able to overnight an OEM part from GM for me and he had it installed the next morning. My car wasn't even there 24 hours.

text: I know Akin since some time and I know that if I have a problem in my car, he will definitely take care of it, or direct me to the right way. I never fixed my car over there, but I went there a week ago with a shuddering problem. I thought it would be an easy fix, Akin tried my car and told me this must be a transmission issue. Of course this just kept me surprised for a minute, I have a Camry 2012 with around 75K miles. This car should be going until 150K - 200K with no issues (other than normal maintenance). No way that a Camry Transmission would have problems @ 75K. So the most important part here, and the main reason I am writing this review, is that this guy just referred me in the right direction. Once he told me its a transmission issue, I started looking into my documents, and discovered that Toyota has sent me a letter back in 2014, mentioning that the car might experience shuddering during light throttle conditions (between 25 and 50 mph). I was like, yeaaah thats the same exact problem I am having and Toyota is aware of. Actually in this letter Toyota has mentioned that they are extending the warranty on the Torque Converter of the Transmission (cause it might fail at some point and cause this shuddering). Of course in addition to Akin's help in figuring out the problem, I went to couple of transmission professionals just to confirm that its actually a Torque Converter issue and I did my online research to be more positive. So the car is having 76K and the warranty is extended until 8 years of the first purchase of the car or 150K. So I was very lucky. The next step I did an appointment with the Toyota Dealer and they took it from there. It took them 2 days to diagnose and fix the problem. He called me the next afternoon and told me that work was 99% done, and that he had dropped my car off to have the alignment done somewhere else. Everything would be done by 11am the next morning. The next day, I came in to pick up my car, paid the remaining $1350, and off I went. So far, I'm pleased with the quality of his work and will update if anything related to the repair fails. I will absolutely come back for any other repairs I need, and highly recommend him to anyone looking for a mechanic.

text:
My 2003 Mazda 6 wanted to die right before Thanksgiving. Despite the stellar reviews here on Yelp and living reasonably nearby, I wasn't sure the car would even make it to Akins's shop, but I am so lucky it started acting up only once I got there. 

Akin initially called the same day, stated what he thought the problem was, explained the diagnostic codes that popped up, the plan, and quoted cost. He reassured me that if the problem was still persistent, he would continue to address it. Very reasonable.

Since I couldn't pick up the car till the next day, Akin continued to test out the car, discovering that the problem was more complex and tirelessly worked on it for two more days (he said my car "kicked his ass"). He drove it on the freeway and local roads, to get a feel for the problem. After taking apart the intake manifold, he found the stupid problem, fixed it and began the time consuming process of putting everything back together. Long story short, he spent way more time on it than expected, gave me an updated quote that was more than fair, and it runs smoother than before the symptoms presented themselves. He worked hard to get my car back to my in time for Thanksgiving so I wouldn't have to worry about it over the holiday.

Here are a few things to note. The shop is CLEAN. Shelves are organized. When I came in, someone was mopping the floor. Someone who takes care of their work space means that they respect their work. If they respect their work, then they will take care of your car. It's easy to excuse a shop for being being dirty because car work is messy. Akin and his crew clearly have worked hard to earn such great reviews, and deserve it. I have been searching for a reliable mechanic for quite a while and my search stops here. Akin has a sailor's mouth, which might throw you off as a new customer, but he is great, and you will walk away confident that your car is in good hands.

text:
If you're looking for a car mechanic, you're done looking. This is it. Trust me. 

I spent so long trying to figure out which car mechanic in San Jose I could trust to not upcharge me or upsell me on anything, and Akin's is the answer. 

I came in a with a list of things I was hoping he would look at, and he took it seriously and checked *everything*. I dropped my car off in the morning, I had a call by mid-morning as to what needed to be done, and by late afternoon, it was done. Literally everything; brakes, rotor resurfacing, wheel rotation, oil change, even diagnosing a particularly annoying OBDII code that had been plaguing me for more than a year (and had several other mechanics stumped). 

And when I asked about a few other things related to some ride noise, he was straight up honest with me and told me that the car was old (it's a 2005, he's not wrong), and that while we *could* go down that rabbit hole, he suggested that we instead focus on ensuring the car was mechanically sound and safe to drive. He could have taken me for a ride (no pun intended). He could have made me spend hundreds of dollars just on labor for him to chase down problems, but he chose to be honest with me, and for that, this entire shop has my utmost respect. 

Akin really treats you like family. He cares about your car and your safety. When I got my rotors resurfaced and my brake pads changed, he even gave me suggestions on making sure I don't ruin my rotors again (avoiding coasting on breaks, shifting down a gear on steep declines, etc). What other mechanic would do that!? 

You can see the pride in his eyes at the end of each servicing job. The man is proud of the auto shop he's built and he clearly deserves it. 

This is my new permanent mechanic, and will be the new mechanic for anyone of my friends I can get to listen. 

Just all around, a great experience, and great people. He'll remind you what it's like to *trust* mechanics again, as we once used to. 

Just go. You won't regret it.

text:
Finding a good mechanic is so important, and these guys are great!

I came to Akin's for the first time to get an oil change after seeing their great yelp reviews. I figure an oil change is an easy way to try out a new shop and see if they are good before you need something more difficult done. They actually ended up saving me lots of money in the end!

I called and made an appointment, it was a little difficult to understand them, but they were very accommodating. When I came in, I went to the front desk, they set up the paperwork, I gave them the keys, and they promptly went to work. 

Half way through, the mechanic called me over to take a look at a leaky seal they found. They were very honest about it, let me take a picture, and told me to have the dealer fix it under warranty. I ended up getting this fixed by the dealer under warranty. It saved me a lot of money on a difficult, costly repair that could have become more serious if not addressed. Also, I would imagine that it is good to have an independent mechanic look over you car every once in a while while under warranty, because the dealer would likely not have voluntarily fixed this seal during their inspection.

The oil change service was more expensive than I expected $50 instead of ~$30 on their website; however, I think this is because it was synthetic oil. It seems like their prices are fair and competitive with any other shop.

I will be returning here the next time my car needs service.

text:
Akin's represents the very best of old-school mechanics: top-level knowledge and skills, genuine care for his customers' safety and budgets, and insistence on doing "the right thing" above all else. My dad was a mechanic in his youth, and taught mechanics at a college, and even founded a vocational center offering mechanics classes, and I can't think of a higher compliment to give Akin than that he shares my dad's skills, his perfectionism, and his philosophy about "doing what's right" for cars and customers. 

I've taken my Honda CRV to Akin's multiple times, and Akin has always taken the time to explain what's wrong with my car, show me the parts removed, keep costs low, and have it ready when I need it. After I moved to Santa Cruz, I was in a bit of a time crunch so I had another well-Yelped shop there install new tires and brakes (how hard could that be?) - but when my car didn't feel or sound right, and that shop shrugged it off as "normal," I took it to Akin instead. Sure enough, he found the problems (without making me feel bad or criticizing the other shop), and even though I'd taken the car elsewhere (never again!), he worked late/went in early the next day to have everything fixed by the time I needed my car back - and at a discount! He even drove my car to an alignment shop, where he called in a favor to get my wheels aligned at no cost to me, because he didn't want me to drive off with it "wrong." 

PEOPLE like this are so hard to find, let alone mechanics! Every time I drive away from Akin's, I know I got a great value, and that my car is safe. From now on I'll gladly drive over the hill, or even pay a towing fee, to a) have his reliable, honest, super-savvy, value-conscious work, and b) reward his extremely strong ethic. It feels good to patronize a business owner who so clearly earns, and deserves, my business.

text: I came here for a 60K major service the other day. The price Akin quoted over the phone was ridiculously cheap; particularly for that type of service. When I dropped my car off, I was told that it would take 2-2.5 hours. It turned out to be less than 1 hour. I was astonished, especially when the final price was less than $100 out the door. Well, I just found out that they did the bare minimum for a 60K. Basically, for that price, all I got was an oil change, top-off all fluids, tire pressure check, tire rotation and a new air filter. I'm not complaining, but I think like my car requires much more than work than that. Akin is an ASE-certified mechanic himself, who has many certifications as well as 30+ years of fixing cars. The problem is, he does not fix the cars, he manages other mechanics to repair/service/maintain them. So, how well they do really depends on how much they know about your car. You drive an Audi, Volvo or other hard-to-fix cars? You might want to avoid this place. However, if you have a low-maintenance car, or just want a tune-up, without much detail work, then I recommend Akins. He doesn't rip you off, but at the same time, he really does not want to deal with troublesome and big burden vehicles. All in all, Akin is honest and I agree with many 5 star reviews on here; but think twice about bringing your car if it requires a delicate touch or strenuous work.

text:
There is a reason Akin's Auto Repair has the ratings you see and here is why. Please read this review, it is true and I did not know Akin until this time using him. Months ago I was looking for a repair shop to fix some electrical issues with my Lincoln Town Car. I was dissatisfied with other garages I went to that could not fix my car and charging me for issues they should have never taken on. Like many others, I did not want to go to the dealership. I found Akin's on Yelp with great reviews and called them about my car needing repairs. Akin immediately after hearing what my issues were he said, "take your car to the dealership." He was frank and honest and knew the problem was something that would be best taken care of by the dealership. I did, it got fixed end of that story. 

KEEP READING. 

So, I told Akin when I first called him and he gave me an honest opinion how to get my car fixed I would be back when I needed something he could do for me. I have a high end customized Chevy van that needed work that was not done properly from a shop that was closer to where I live, a simple brake job i thought after taking the van back to the other shop four times with new charges each time with my van still vibrating at times when we applied the brakes.

Here is where it gets good! 

So needing an oil change, wanting to get my brakes fixed by someone I was hoping was qualified to do the job right and get a tune up, guess what? How much do you think getting an oil change, a brake job that could need complete replacing of some if not all parts again that were not right before, and a tune up cost? It cost me $35!!! That's right, $35. Akin told me my van being so heavy with all the added parts to it, raised top, hardwood interior, large leather captain chairs and automatic folding bench seat bed I special brake drums to handle the weight better. The ones that were put in before were still good and had plenty of mileage on them and were still very safe to use. He said come back later and he can help me find better drums for my van and replace them when it needed but no need to spend the money now on parts that are still good. The occasional shaking is not always there and not bad, it was just annoying and I feared for my families safety.

Keep reading!!!

He also told me the van was not needing a tune up at this time but to come back in a few thousand miles when a major service was required and he would do the work then.

Hence, $35 oil change, great professional service advice on his nickel. He could have charged me a ton for a lot of work that was not needed. 

It does not get better than that folks. 

Akin is I think European, talks really fast and could appear to some to be rude. He works hard and moves quickly all the time which could put some people off. But he wastes no time and is anything but rude. 

His shop is a little hard to access for the first time but go on Google maps satellite and see where his shop is off Park Avenue that can only be entered to from going east on Park. You will not regret it.

text:
Called today to schedule an appointment for an oil change and to check my brakes. I left a voicemail and happened to also mention my car is a Alitma hybrid. A few hours later I received a text message saying they don't service hybrid vehicles at all. Initially I didn't see why having a hybrid would matter for oil changes and brakes. However, the owner called me back later and explained in great detail some of challenges faced. While the owner and a few of his employees can service hybrids, not all the technicians have experience working with them. He explained that even for oil changes and brakes there are certain nuances that need to be considered to ensure the vehicle isn't damaged and to ensure technician safety.

Obviously I was disappointed. The reviews for Akin's Auto Repair are fantastic and I was hoping to take my car there for much needed service. Also, in the Bay Area where hybrids are so common I'm very surprised that any general auto repair shops don't touch them. However, the owner has a great attitude and really does care about customer service. Since they couldn't service my vehicle Akin referred me to another shop that does accept hybrid vehicles. I only hope that place cares about customer service and quality as much as Akin does.

I decided to write this review, not as a bad review, but so that others with hybrid vehicles are aware of this policy before taking their car here.

I would 100% go back to Akin and his shop. I know my car will need struts and brakes soon and I am pretty much set on bringing it back to Akin.

text:
I went to Akin's to repair my BWM due to his all 5 star rating. They had a diagnostic and told me two ignition coils were not working and suggested me replace all 6. I was OK and asked them to have oil change and do the regular maintenance work. I was given a quote and it looked fine to me. At the end of day I got a call and was told that the car was ready for pick-up. So far so good. The one star is for this. 

When driving the car on the way back home, I smelled something burning, but didn't think anything wrong. But after arriving home, when I parked the car, some smoking was coming out of hood. It's so terrible. I opened the hood, and found that oil was dropping onto the exhaust pipe which is very hot, what's where the smoke came from. This is a new issue, I never had this before. I thought they might just carelessly have some oil spilled out when doing the oil change. So I called Akin's next morning and they asked me to bring the car back. 

The guy who repaired my car had a quick check and tell me there are three places leaking oil. That's where the dropping come from. However what I didn't understand was why it didn't happen before. He was kind of mad and asked me to take to other dealer to have a report to prove the new oil leaking issue was caused by his repairs. I was very disappointed at his response to my question. The other guy came to explain the reason, I didn't quite understand his reasoning. Basically he meant the old oil was thicker than new oil, so no leaking was noticed before. I wasn't convinced by their explanation. They confirmed the car can be drove safely for at least another 5000 miles, so I took the car back home. 

Days after the repair, I found there are oil drops in my driving way. This was definitely a new issue since there were no oil drops on the ground before. To double confirm this, I checked my garage ground where I mostly parted my car but hadn't parked there since the repair. I didn't see any oil drops. It clearly proves that the oil leaking issue was somehow caused by this repair. I can't figure how it's caused by their repair, but they are just relevant. I'll never go to the shop again.

text:
I moved to San Jose a few months, leaving behind the mechanic I had grown to trust for many years. It's genuinely difficult to find a reliable auto shop with fair prices, who know what they're doing and genuinely care about your experience. That being said, I will now never go anywhere else but Akin's. 

I called up yesterday to get a quote on brakes and rotors, an oil change and a look at my AC. It hasn't worked in years. The owner answered and was as nice as can be, offering extremely fair pricing and a quick turnaround. I dropped my car off around 7pm (after they closed), and sent him a text about what I needed, per his request. This morning he called -- everything was going great, and my car would be done early afternoon. Through out the day if I had a question, I texted. And he quickly replied. Who does that with their mechanic?

When I showed up to pick up my car, he let me know that his efforts on the AC didn't work, but he figured out the problem -- and it was an easy $27 relay I could install myself in 5 seconds. Instead of ordering the part (which he said could take weeks) or trying to upsell me on some expensive AC job, he called ahead to the nearest Honda, checked to make sure they had the part, then showed me on my car where to place it. He doesn't know this, but I've had several estimates thrown my way, ranging $850-1400 to fix the AC. Hence why I've driven around sweating for 2 summers. What he tried was $45, and when that didn't work, he solved the problem and told me how to fix it for $27, or $72 total. He literally saved me between $750-$1350. Plus, the new brakes feel great. 

TLDR: So all in all, on zero notice, I was able to get my brakes and rotors replaced in the front and back, oil change and AC fixed by 2pm. The owner himself was fixing cars and taking calls, and made sure I had a fantastic experience from beginning to end. I can assure you, he has earned my business, both my roommate and my girlfriend's business, and anyone I can spread the word to.

text:
I absolutely love this place! Having recently moved to the Bay area, I had no idea where to turn for a mechanic, also I am pretty clueless when it comes to repairs, parts, costs etc. So, not wanting to take any chances or get taken advantage of, I turned to Yelp which led me to Akin's Auto Repair because of all the great reviews. Not only did the place have a 5 star rating, many of the reviews were more than the typical few sentences, and they were very detailed and specific with each experience. 

Now, on to my own experience here...

Again, I'm new to the area and had been getting my oil changes done at random "drive thru" places which were less than stellar but got the job done I suppose. Tired of mediocre service and expensive prices I finally had time to look up a legitimate place to get my car stuff done. I called and made an appointment at Akin's and got in the next day. Upon arrival Akin greeted me with such energy and one heck of a sense of humor, I immediately felt like I had made the right choice. He took my information and my keys and sent me on my way to the waiting area, where he would occasionally pop in and update me on what was going on with my car. I had to wait a little longer than normal since the shop did not have my size filter (I have a tiny engine so I've had that happen at most places with my car anyway, NBD) but without hesitation Akin said they were going to get the filter right now and would finish the oil change. He also told me about my back light being out and fixed that as well. 

I always worry about auto shops preying on me since I'm not very knowledgable about cars, but at Akin's I never felt like I was being taken advantage of, some of the most honest, respectable, and friendly group of mechanics I have ever met. Not to mention this pricing at this place is more than reasonable! I had an oil change, light bulb replacement, and a safety inspection, he also explained why my automatic window wasn't working as well as why my check engine light was on.I couldn't believe it when he gave me the total, it was way less than I was paying at those drive-thru places and they were only did an oil change! I'm so glad I finally found a reliable and honest auto shop, I will definitely be going to Akin's for ANY future auto services.

P.S. Th waiting area has Wi-Fi too

text:
This place fully deserves the 5 star rating it has! No two ways about it! Driving has always been a big part of my life (More-so than the average person as my work requires me to be all over the place. Hell, at one point I even had to live in my car) and as a result I've dealt with more mechanics than I care to count - some good, most not good... Akin definitely ranks as one of the best I've experienced, if not THE best. I could write a book on everything I liked here, but I'll just break it down like this:

List of awesome for this place:

- Akin: The guy whose name is on the shop, is awesome. Straightforward, knowledgeable, and honest (And sometimes downright entertaining to overhear). His customer service is impeccable - the day I came in got extremely busy and he always gave the people the attention they needed. It was actually a marvel just watching him juggle customers that were already there, customers that were just coming in, and a never-ending barrage of phone calls. I never observed him faltering or slighting any customer in terms of the absolute attention and care he gave them regardless of the barrage of business (And if things ever got too hectic, he was always patient and clear to his customers that he would get around to them but couldn't because his hands were full). I want to say this - do this guy a favor and call in ahead of time to set an appointment (I didn't do this, but I wish I did... and I didn't even really have to wait long for my car to have its work started). This is not a requirement for the shop, but Akin deals with so much that it's the least you can do in exchange for the awesome service you will receive. 

- Work and the crew: Akin's crew of mechanics are lively, focused, and work fairly quickly (In a good way). I came in for a brake job, and it was revealed to me that I definitely needed more than just brake shoes (Rotors were completely messed up, a caliper was busted and leaking - it was a mess). Once I okay'd everything it took only about a couple hours for them to get the job done (That includes a test drive to make sure the new parts were set properly). 

- The waiting room: The room upstairs is one big waiting room decked out with leather couches, wifi, and a big flat screen. Very comfortable and clean.

- Compassion: Going in, I already had a price range in my head as to what the brake job should cost. When I saw just how awful my brake-situation really was, that price skyrocketed in my head. This is where Akin really shined - I noticed that he never tried to talk-up certain aspects of the repairs needed just to shoehorn more costs into the job. Case in point - my rear brakes and rotors were destroyed. Things like this are easy targets for mechanics to give you a "You MUST get this repair done or you can't drive out of here yadda yadda yadda" pitch. Akin, instead, said that the front brakes are more important and that if I really couldn't budget the full repairs then that's the part I should get fixed now. Of course, I had both the front and the back done, but the fact that this is how he goes about his business speaks volumes to me. Even after I okay'd all the work, he was still working with me to hash out a very very reasonable price. This is probably the only time I ended up spending more on my car than I originally had anticipated and didn't feel regret or buyer's remorse. Akin is willing to work with you. Bottom line: He really cares about his customers.
Side story: A regular at this place told me of a time that he saw someone bring in their jalopy for repairs. The car was in complete disarray and was practically useless. Akin inspected the car then told the owner of the junk-car that he refused to do any work on the car because to do work and charge the person for it would basically be cheating them out of their money. Akin turned down what could have potentially been thousands of dollars out of a person that was completely naive to their situation, just so that he could be honest and do what's best for this person... Simply incredible.

This place is awesome! Akin - You and your crew work hard, but most importantly you work honest. I hope the customers keep coming in like a downpour because you definitely deserve it! Someone get these people a cold one to drink at the end of a long day! I'll definitely be back some months later for further work on my car and I have just found my go-to place in the south bay.

text:
These guys deserve the 5 stars they have.

Getting to the nitty gritty since I am on mobile:

The phone system is pretty sucky, but just press 3 and you'll speak to someone right away.

Made an appointment and dropped off my car on Wednesday 7/9 at around 10am. Called ahead to make sure and everything was in order.

I have a 2005 Jetta that won't pass Smog, and had the engine light on, but I knew what was wrong in terms of checking codes and whatnot.

Akin was quick, friendly as all hell and had my car checked up within 5 hours... Not bad. 

Now we get to where they really shined.

I asked about passing smog, getting the car good to go and he gave me a list of what the car needed (not physical, oral), what those parts fixed (i.e. "this set of parts costs xxx and fixes problem 1, while this set costs xx and fixes problem 2") how much it would be and what he could do in terms of price to help me out. VERY extensive.

He quoted everything to be done with at $750, discounting the diagnostic fee and some smaller labor.

That seemed more than fair, but I am also waiting on the Assistance program that the state has for cars that won't pass smog. 

Akin didn't just dismiss me, he explained that they don't go through that program, but that other shops in the area do. 

As I was about to get the car, he just pointed to the car and said that he wasn't going to charge me since it would not be fair, that the other Smog Certified Mechanics are going to do their own procedures and apply their own fixes.

Shook my hand and told me that if I wanted to do the service here after finding out about the voucher, that he would honor the price he gave me, and to have a great day.

I was expecting to pay the $90 diagnostic fee, which is also VERY cheap since dealerships and other shops charge MUCH more. 

He saved me a good chunk of change, told me what was wrong and even reassured a price for me.

You want honest, fast and affordable service... Then here ya go. Akin's made my month with this simple act.

text:
Akin's Auto Repair is just plain awesome.

It was making a terrible clunking noise that sounded to me like a broken CV. Akin provided me with an estimate over the phone, but also asked that I bring the car in for him to take a look, as he did not want to order the parts without first properly diagnosing the problem. For those of you looking for a mechanic, this is important. I had called 4 other shops, and they all said they could have the part ordered even before I showed up there. How could they know that the axle was even the issue? Akin knew that it might not even be the axle causing the noise, so he insisted I bring it in.

He took it for a quick drive, and found right away that some would-be wheel thieves had removed a couple of the lug nuts from one side of the vehicle! Akin replaced the two lugs and the noise was gone! Best part, he didn't charge me for the time and effort that his team took to put the car on the lift and diagnose the issue! I think that speaks volumes for his honesty, trustworthiness, and quality.

A couple of days later, I took my own car, a 2002 Toyota Corolla, in to have new springs installed. I provided the springs, but when Wheel Works previously took 6 hours to do the same job a few years back, Akin and his team completed it in an absolutely blistering ONE hour. On top of that, they flushed my brakes as well--free of charge!

As I waited, I was able to enjoy a furnished waiting room with a great TV and wireless internet as well. On the walls are his and his team's credentials and certifications--it reads like a Wall of Fame. They are certified to work on a variety of vehicles, including hybrids, and they continue to attend training to keep their knowledge up to best advise their customers.

Akin and his team run a tight shop, they are quick, and they know what they are doing. Before I left, Akin told me some of his best practices. He told me that to stay in business, he has to exemplify what makes a good mechanic--being honest, and doing the job right.

I just found my local mechanic--he'll be getting my service for years to come!

I cannot for the life of me fathom how this business has so many 5 star reviews, as, by my experience it's clear that Akin is a crook. 

Then again, maybe Akin was just having a bad day:

After waiting for 30 minutes in his waiting room while Akin chatted up friends, I described the problem to him with my Transmission.

Without doing a diagnostic check on the trouble light, he told me the transmission was shot and had to be replaced, to the tune of $4000 or more. 

I asked him how he could know what was wrong without at least doing a diagnostic. (I told him I suspected it was the shift solenoid, as this was a known problem on my model of car) and he only gave in after I insisted and paid his diagnosis fee. 

Afterwards, he simply said "Yeah, the trans needs to be replaced." Skeptical, I looked him in the eye and asked "Well what was the code that the test returned? What did it say?" 

He only insisted in an annoyed tone: "It said the transmission is bad and needs to be replaced, which will cost you at least $4000, and your car is not worth it." As if it was his place to decide such things.

I walked out in disgust and never returned.
However, I did order my own $30 diagnostic unit which pulled the code and confirmed my suspicions: 
The Shift Solenoid B was bad and needed replacing, not the entire transmission.

I took it to another shop, who were kind, courteous, fair and honest, and paid less than $1000 to have the problem fixed. 

The only way he has so many 5 star reviews is one or a combination of the following: 1. They're all him. 2. They're all from uneducated, unsuspected customers who don't know they've been duped and are simply happy he did a "great job". or 3. Akin is a customer of Yelp, who offer to remove bad reviews for him for a fee. (Yes, Yelp does this. I know because they contacted my own business with this offer.) 

It's sad that such a dishonest businessperson has such a great reputation on here.
