text:
Akin is my hero! This review is long overdue. Akin has legendary customer service and great rapport with all of his customers. I visited his shop as a walk-in a few months back because of an alternator problem that kept causing my car to die. I knew the problem had to do with the alternator because I replaced the dead car battery and the new battery still wasn't charging. I live in Milpitas and even though Wheel Works is a local "auto shop", I wanted to take my car somewhere more... experienced, fair, honest and reliable. So I took the time to research a reliable auto shop. I kept finding Akin's shop on all the review sites. I found people with my problem going to hid shop too. This made me confident in his abilities to fix my car. In this review, I will also mention the problems I had in case you are having the same issues too. 

Even though his shop is located in San Jose... and even if it meant driving my dying car on a journey to see him... I had faith that he would be the one to fix it. So I made my journey to his shop the following morning. He opens at 8:30. I got there at 8:15 and he already had 2 customers with appointments lined up. We waited for his prompt arrival. When he arrived, he told me he knew I didn't have an appointment and that he would take care of me. I didn't have to wait very long. I told him what was going on and that he could hold onto my car over the weekend if he needed to. I also told him about some lights that wouldn't go away on my dashboard (VSC & ABS), which was a random problem I had dealt with for months... Then I went fishing. Only a few hours went by and I received a phone call. It was Akin asking for permission to replace my alternator and he also gave me a good estimate on the pricing, which was CONSIDERABLY inexpensive compared to almost any other auto shops. An hour went by and I received another phone call. It was Akin again. This time he gave me the good news that my car was fixed. He also said he was able to make all of my dashboard lights go away at no charge. I swung by to pick up my car. I was very pleased with his work. Since then, I knew he would be my mechanic for just about everything!

I recently paid Akin another visit to fix a grinding noise that returned. The grinding happened every time I turned my steering wheel. It was a problem I was conflicted with and had thought to be "fixed" way before I brought my car to Akin... (flashback) Many and many a month ago when I took my car to Wheel Works, my though process was that since they are located next door to my house... it would be convenient to be able to walk home while they fix it and easily walk back to pick it up when they were done. I'll try to make a long story short.... Wheel Works suckered me into a buying a "buy 3 get 1 free deal". Some deal that was!! They charged me $3000 and never even fixed my problem!! I was pissed! I asked for them to replace the new parts with my old parts and give my money back but they said it wasn't possible. They said they would "fix it" again for free. They took my car back, held it for weeks, and finally returned it supposedly "fixed". All they did was grease the problem up so it wouldn't make any noise for awhile. Sigh... (flash forward)

Now it's the present and my car sounds like the damn Titanic crashing into an ice burg every time i turn the steering wheel. It's a Lexus GS300. How embarrassing! A Lexus shouldn't even make hoopty noises! Anyway. I told Akin about my problem and how I had taken my car to Wheel Works before. He knew he could fix it so I let him hold onto my car for the weekend again. Little did I know, he would return it the same day... When he called me with the good news that he fixed it... I was extremely impressed! I swung by again to pick up my car and found out that he really did fix the problem AND it only cost me $175. Lol. What the hell?

I wrote this long review to tell you all that Akin is an honest mechanic. He won't sell you extra stuff you don't need. He will fix the problem you are having and ONLY that problem. He will not over charge you. He won't even touch a problem he knows he can't fix. Instead, he will give you a referral he knows that can really help you. His referrals are usually just as legit as he is. I know because I've sent a few people his way and they've all left his shop satisfied wether it's actually him who fixes their cars or not. Akin's the man! Definitely check him out if you need a mechanic!

text:

Akin gave me a price estimate for the struts and told me I wouldn't find a better price in the bay area. Since I had no idea what the job should cost, I took him up on his challenge. I was so glad to find an honest, trustworthy mechanic, I had Akin's work change my brakes, struts and a few other minor issues on my Jeep. I was very happy with the quality of parts and service provided. They charged for the time they actually worked on my car, not the maximum allowable time to do the jobs. And because Akin and his brother have decades of experience, they got the work done fast!

I have absolutely no reservations in recommending Akin's to all my family members or anyone else looking for a good, trustworthy mechanic. Although, I live on the mid-peninsula, it is well worth the drive down to have Akin and his brother work on my cars!

When the job was finally completely and the AC running better than I can ever remember, he volunteered to cut back the extra charge by half. I felt this was more than reasonable.

text:
Took my friend's Chevy Cavalier in to see what exactly was wrong with it. I had been experiencing serious issues on the road and had no idea what the problem was since I'm not exactly a car literate. He had spun out previously on the interstate and he told me she hadn't been running smooth since.

I wasn't aware you had to make an appointment so we just rolled by. Akin told us to come back two days later and he would check the car for free (awesome).

He didn't tell us what time we should come in so we did our usual morning routine and ended up there a little after noon. Unfortunately, he had set us up in the morning so we messed up his schedule (felt kinda bad that I didn't ask him beforehand what time he wanted us in).

About two hours later he finally had an empty lift and started on the Cavalier.

There was no good news about her. The entire car was rusted through and through and Akin was surprised she was still running. It was like a bomb on wheels (warped wobbly wheels).

He didn't sugar coat anything and was upfront. He wasn't willing to take any money to even attempt to touch the disaster. He spoke and pointed things out in a simple way that even I could understand. Afterwards, Akin gave us some sound advice and it looks like we'll be looking for a new car. 

He and his wife are extremely friendly and are easy to talk to. They made you feel comfortable. Safe to say when something happens to the new vehicle, Akin will be the go to guy.

Side note: My friend left my personal belongings in their waiting lounge. We called in and asked if we could come by later and pick it up and Akin was completely cool with it. Really awesome guy.

I will be happy to post this invoice to the internet upon request to show the it was issued to me.  THIS ENGINE IS NOTORIOUS FOR BLOWING HEAD GASKETS WHEN DRIVEN HOT - LOOK IT UP! I sold this Subaru - ALMOST THREE YEARS LATER - a few months ago and it passed CA smog standards with perfection the DAY IT WAS SOLD.  Three weeks later the new owner called me as she was driving the car and told me that the temperature indicator was pegged RED and she was still driving it - and she wanted my opinion what she should do.  I told her to STOP diving it and let it cool.  I had many follow-up conversations with the new owner and also with a friend of hers that identified himself to me as "Professor Jake" following this.  Even Jake admitted to me that this engine is prone to head gasket failure and that it is highly unlikely that the head gaskets were blown when I sold it because it had passed these stringent smog tests when it was sold.  I am really sorry that she apparently overheated the car and blew the heads.  I am even more sorry that Akin is being fingered for 'poor quality' by some one that has never done business with him when I know this to be absolutely untrue.  I encourage Jake H to search his conscious and to consider the facts and to retract his base-less review of a very reputable man.   YOU the Reader of this  - please take into consideration all the 5 star reviews of Akin, the review by Jake H is tasteless in its reference to venereal disease and it is NOT substantiated by facts or HIS OWN EXPERIENCE WITH AKIN.  I also fault Yelp for allowing a posting to continue despite it being FLAGGED for its bad taste and complete lack of personal involvement between the reviewer with the subject  business.  SHAME ON YOU JAKE H AND SHAME ON YOU YELP!

Signed up for a Yelp account to write this first review.

Akin's a rockstar. These guys take pride in their work, and in their customer service, and I really appreciate their hustle. I've been going here for about a year and a half, including a couple oil changes and replacing a thermostat on my A3. The prices are reasonable, but mainly I come back because I'm confident they're doing things the right way and triple checking their work. They'll do a thorough inspection even if you came in for a simple oil change, and Akin's a straight shooter. They won't tell you to replace you pads too early, but they'll find that worn axle CV boot that you weren't paying attention to. And Akin's not afraid to tell you when you need to take better care of your car (check your oil every 500-1k, Audi drivers!)

I'll be the first to admit I'm no gearhead, but that's exactly why I appreciate businesses like Akin's. I want to be sure my car is taken care of without paying the Dealership Rip-Off Premium. There are a lot of competent mechanics around, but I go to Akin's because he actually gives a shit.

I am a student at SJSU and need my car for school and work.  I brought my car in because the check engine light came on.  They looked at the car and all they said was that I was missing a gas cap.  Two weeks later the engine fails and is ruined because of an oil leak.  How did they not see this?

I was left stranded with friends at 6pm on a Sunday night in Paso Robles.  It was a very unsafe situation to be in.

I have had my car looked at by other repair shops and they always go over the car to see if there is anything wrong when I bring it in for something like this.  I don't understand why they would allow a car that was so sick to leave their shop.

I recommend that if you care for your car and your safety you should double check everything they do.  Or just  find another shop that will take better care of you.

text:
My old car has been acting wonky lately. My usual mechanic moved to Texas so I checked out Yelp for a new mechanic. Akin Auto Repair has the highest rating so I am going to check this place out.

This review is my first adventure to Akin Auto Repair along with my impression.

First of all, I thought this place gonna be in some ghetto place but I am so wrong. The location is somewhat private and Akin did install security cameras in his parking lot. So you can leave your car overnight here and it will be fine. The shop is clean, bright, cable-free. The waiting area is relaxing. Make sure you bring something to kill time because there is not much to do around this area. There used to be a LAN center near the shop but they closed long time ago.

Service: On Wednesday, I showed up and asked for help. I already narrowed down my car problems but I didn't tell Akins about it. Akin took a look at my car. He told me the problems, which I agree, with my car. He also told me about the cause and the solution. I wanted the car to be fixed on the same day but the shop is fairly busy; and my car will survive until Friday. So Friday came. I supposed to be at the shop at 8:45 AM ( I am not a morning person ) but I overslept until 10AM. I drove to the shop around 10:15 AM and I was like I may have to come back another time. Akin was like no, I just hope you bring something to kill time because we are going to take care of your car. Two hours later, my car is fixed in timely manner. 

Price: The price is fair. I am fairly pleased with the price for fixing my car. 

The owner: Akin is a very enthusiastic guy. He is straightforward about what need to be fixed and done. 

Overall, Akin Auto Repair did impress me about their services. Bringing car to the shop has always been a crappy experience for me because who knows if the car mechanic suggested to fix some extra stuff on top of fixing the already known problems. It was pleasant at Akin Auto Repair and b.s free and I spent less money than I thought I would. So 5 star for this repair shop.

P.S: The repair shop is a bit far away from my place. They should move to my neighborhood. :D

text:
I recently came home from a cross-country trip when my A/C went out in Bakersfield at the end of July! My wife, my dog and I drove home dripping in sweat and was frustrated at now having to pay to have the A/C fixed. 

I looked on Yelp and found Akin's Auto Repair with over a 100 5-star ratings. I was skeptical since almost everything was positive. I decided to call and see for myself and he was very helpful immediately as he asked detailed questions after I told him the make, model, year of my vehicle and my issue. (This is not a given since some mechanics do not know multiple vehicles well enough without looking under the hood!)

I took my vehicle to him and he was friendly, knowledgable, and compassionate about getting my A/C fixed in the middle of summer. He should have charged me for a diagnostic test (A/C recharge) but he quickly noticed that the compressor had locked up (frozen). So, instead he told me he will not charge me for something that would be a waste of money anyways. 

I am fairly knowledgable about cars having repaired power steering pumps and other maintenance issues before, but not a compressor, evaporator, etc. So when Akin took me over to another vehicle he was working on to show me why my compressor locked up I really appreciated his time and teaching. He told me that Honda should have made a recall on this but has failed to do so. He also said I could save money by changing just the compressor but I would be back to him in a month to have it fixed again. He said the only way he would work on the vehicle was to change all of the components to the A/C system. But, instead of trying to sell more parts to me he wanted me to go home, do my research and call other mechanics. 

I researched parts for this job and called 3 other mechanics. Akin's price (with a cash discount) was less than a $1000 but I could not find another mechanic that would touch it for under $2000. He told me that the A/C components came as a kit and would save money that way. One mechanic I spoke with did not even know enough about my vehicle to ask me the right questions. He even told me I only needed to change the compressor which would bring me right back to him weeks later with the same problem.

Akin was straight-forward, honest and dependable without charging me ridiculous fees. I have enjoyed ice cold air in my vehicle since the first week in August and have recommended him to all of my friends. This many 5-star ratings are not a scam and what can you lose by getting an estimate?

text:
I honestly cannot praise Akin enough for his honesty, pricing, integrity, and overall great personality. There is a reason why his place is 5 stars with over 100 reviews. Keep in mind that not many auto repair shops even reach 40 on Yelp so his rating speaks wonders. The only reason why I am writing such a long review is because he deserves to get the same respect in return with a great review! 

I had been without AC since June and had fixed it that month by replacing freon at another shop. They said it was a simple fix so I replaced it for $80. However, not even two weeks later, my AC was blowing warm air so I knew it had to be a leak that I read cost upwards of 1k. I went to another auto repair shop that my friend highly recommended and he diagnosed my problem as a leak in the compressor. He gave me a lower price than the 1k but I still called around to 10+ shops for a compressor estimate. I stumbled upon Akin's shop and his pricing for the compressor was very competitive, so I brought my car in there.

When I first called Akin, he put me on hold for five minutes so I just decided to give him another call. I was somewhat perturbed by that but when I finally arrived at the shop, I understood why he didnt call back or forgot I was on hold. His shop gets calls every second! It is ridiculous and he would rather keep his focus and attention to the customer who is right in front of him. That is what I experience so when people called, he put them on hold and made sure I was satisfied with his service and response. So my first advice is to keep calling and make an appointment even though you get put on hold or dont even get through.

I told Akin that I had my car diagnosed and it was the compressor. The other place did not charge me for the diagnosis and I know other places would have charged so I did not feel a need for him to diagnose this problem. He said that he would check to make sure that the other guy was not lying and he did not want me to fix a part that was not broke to begin with. Thank goodness he did!!!! It turned out that my AC compressor worked PERFECTLY FINE and it was my CONDENSER that was leaking! I knew he was not ripping me off either because the condenser part is cheaper than the compressor by $200 so I knew that he giving it to me straight. Once he called me and confirmed the problem, he was so ardent in telling me that the other business was ripping me off and even if they replaced the compressor, my AC would still not be working. I dropped my car off at 10am and I needed my car to be done by 2pm. He still had to order the parts and was unsure of whether he would finish in time but he definitely kept his word and called before 2pm saying it was ready for pick up. My car was running for a while with the AC blasted just to make sure that there was no fluke and my AC was legitly fixed. I cannot thank him enough! That week was a blazer for sure. 

Akin is truly an honest man and I respect him immensely for his business ethic. His pricing is also very reasonable so you cant really beat that. I will be taking my car to his shop for all future car repairs. If you are reading this Akin, I thank you again! 

**TIPS*
1) If you are put on hold for a long time, keep calling back and make sure you make an appointment well before the day you bring your car in. He will recall your conversation and car problem and will help you when you get there.
2) He is EXTREMELY busy so if you bring in your car for a pretty big service, expect a couple of hours. It is worth it though.
3) Check in and you can get 15% off your service. When I called for the compressor quote, he gave me the rock bottom price so the 15% could not be applied. I guess I will save it for my next visit.
4) He is open every day except Sundays. Too bad because Sundays are so convenient haha.
5) Enjoy the great service, honesty, hospitality, and savings!

He says "look here - see that this pressure valve has a little bit of coolant visible, which would be normal if you have added coolant - since you haven't, I bet this valve is leaking". Akin did say that IF there was a very slow leak (in the "several months to empty system" variety) then his vacuum test might not find it. But he added some UV (black light) sensitive dye to the refrigerant so that if the A/C starts "losing its cool", there will be traces on the part that is leaking.

I know the owner, Akin, from his previous, good quality work. So, needing repairs for my Infiniti G35 and having heard that he had opened his own place recently, I visited the new shop without hesitation. Again without hesitation, I must say I am extremely glad that I did.

I was astonished to see how much noise such a small part could make! He then ordered the original replacement from the Infiniti dealer, and had it repaired the same day, along with the brakes. Unlike other mechanics, he also advised that the struts were in very good shape, therefore preventing unnecessary repairs of several hundred dollars.

In addition to the great work he did, Akin also took the time to explain the repairs in detail, is very honest, and prompt (not to mention he runs an extremely clean shop). My family and I used to come here for all our car needs. I had a bad experience here a year and a half ago after I had them replace my clutch, master cylinder, and slave cylinder for my G37. I took off the review because the business is their livelihood but I feel people should be aware.

When they overhauled my clutch, they didn't replace my master cylinder as agreed. Everywhere in the manual says you must replace both master and slave at the same time. I picked up the car and almost get home to find that the pedal is stuck to the floor and I can't shift. They towed it back to the shop and replaced my master cylinder and it is working again. Note that after picked up the car the second time I told them that it was driving funny. So I drove the car with Chuck in it and had him drive it but he told me it drove normal. Wouldn't I know what normal is if I am the one that's been driving it every day? I let it slide and thought it just needed to be broken in.

Just recently I was not able to get into ANY gear. I thought my clutch had worn out prematurely so I took it to another shop to get it replaced. Turns out the clutch was never adjusted correctly so I was not getting full pedal travel and the clutch was not fully disengaging. The new shop readjusted my clutch and it finally drives like how it should be.

text:
I have had a very good experience dealing with Chuck, Sunny, and Joe at Tech 3 and I thought I would share that experience to benefit others. 

I had read positive reviews about these guys on Yelp and their labor quote was very competitive which made me decide to try them out to install Struts and sway bars, which I had ordered online, on my 01 Civic. 

The installation was perfect and my old ride was being to feeling new. However, around 2 weeks after installing the struts, there was a terrible squeaking sound coming from the back of the car. I brought the car back in, and the guys took a look and we found out that the brand new rear struts that we had installed had collapsed. Because they were under warranty, I was going to replace them.

I asked Chuck to order new struts and install them himself. Chuck gave me a very discounted quote on the labor. The new struts were installed and the ride was back to feeling new again. But within an hour of installation, the horrendous squeaking noise started again. I got my car in the same day. Chuck and Sunny took the bushings apart and greased all of them. They also lubed the sway bar bushings in case it was the one making the noise. I drove off feeling confident that it would solve the issue. But, it did not solve it. The squeaking sound was still there.

I did a lot of research about what could be causing the squeaking noise and there was a service bulletin issued for bushings on the trailing arm knuckle. I called Tech 3 and informed them about the bulletin. They ordered the parts for me from Honda and this time gave me a very good rate on labor and threw in a free alignment. I got my car in the next day. They installed the bushings and did the alignment. I rolled out expecting the squeaking sounds to come back. However, they did not, and they still haven't and I think we hit the nail on the head with the bushing for the trailing arm knuckle.

I enjoyed this experience of dealing with the guys from Tech3 because throughout this traumatic ordeal of identifying that squeaking sound, I got excellent customer service from all of them. From rides back to my house, discounted labor, information on various parts being installed and upgrades. and even Chucks wise words of wisdom. 

I will soon be dropping in to install Eibach Sportsline lowering springs and camber kit. I recommend Tech 3 to anyone without batting an eyelid.

text:
When I moved to the Bay area a year ago, one thing I worried about was finding a good, reliable mechanic. I initially went to Tech3 based on my sister's high recommendation. But since she's not very knowledgeable about or familiar with auto services, I chose to do my own assessment on the shop.

After 3 visits to Tech3, I can definitely say I've found my go-to mechanic shop. I will give Tech3 my business from now on. Granted two of the 3 times I took my cars in were for oil changes, I was still able to get a good feel for the place by observing the activities in the shop, the conversations taking place among the workers, and asking some questions. I could tell these guys knew their cars, cared about their customers, and were meticulous when working on the cars. 

What really sealed the deal for me was the third time when I took my daughter's Prius to them for some advice (second opinion). When the Prius was recently in the service department of the Toyota dealership for one of their million recalls (okay, not a million but a lot lately), they told me the water pump needed to be replaced. I was a little suspicious since the water pump had been replaced two years/10K miles ago. I wanted to do some research before spending $610 to replace it again. 

I called Tech3 for advice and Chuck (owner) told me to bring the Prius in. Minutes after I drove it in, he personally took a look at the water pump and said he didn't think there was a leak. He invited me into the work area to take a look myself. He took a flashlight and a mirror to show me the water pump from all sides. He thought the pinkish residue (which was probably what the Toyota service tech noticed) was from the last time the pump was leaking and needed replacement. After thoroughly cleaning up the old residue with water and air drying it, he advised me to monitor that area by checking for new residue after driving it about 100 miles. Tech3 did not charge me anything. 

I have been checking under the hood for the past week and there's no sign of a leak. Tech3 likely saved me a good bit of money and time. Chuck said if the pump needs to be replaced in the future, Tech3 would charge about $280, less than half what the Toyota dealership wanted for the same job. 

If you need any service for your cars, give these guys a visit. You won't be disappointed. They seem to be focused on earning your business and trust the right way.

text:
This review is based on my first experience to have some handling upgrades installed.

My impression of their work is Tech3 does quality work and see's to it the job is done properly. I can feel the buddy/family vibe of the place. I don't have too much doubt they can't get it done.

My impression of communication and follow up customer service is so-so. I showed up for my appointment on time. However I ended up waiting an entire hour before my car could be started on. I believe Tech3 did try and reach me 20 minutes before my appointment -- at that point I was already on the road, 1/2 way there since I work 30 min away -- but somehow even when I answered either they couldn't hear me or my signal was bad. I just wished that when I arrived I was informed it would be an hour wait.. I wasn't. It was also a bit uncomfortable waiting -- because of the remodeling there was no comfy seating inside, and while sitting outside it was running out of shade as time passed on a pretty warm afternoon and the uncomfortable sweating began.

Acknowledging that my car took a while longer to get to, they did their best and fast work and finishing the job. Took only 30 minutes and I was impressed! However despite waiting an extra hour, and the job taking less time than quoted, I was still rang up to pay the full hour of labor estimate -- which isn't necessarily cheap. As a first time customer I was a little disappointed in this piece, and definitely feel like if the charges were knocked down the a little bit in regards to extra wait, lack of communication while I was waiting, and first time customer, I'd for sure be more eager to come back. For reference, even with other shops I've worked with they immediately lowered the charge on labor when it's been overestimated. Would I come back? Depends on if I don't mind spending the extra cash and if I had no other convenient, reliable options.

I wanted a new GM crate motor installed I just didn't have a shop in mind that I knew could do the job correctly. I immediately started looking here and elsewhere and making phone calls and I just didn't have a lot of confidence in the shops I was talking to. They mostly specialized in lightweight type auto repairs, oil changes tune ups etc. and the people on the other end of the phone didn't sound very knowledgeable about removing and replacing engines.

I called a shop I used in the past who does great work but only works on rear ends and they recommended leales. This recommendation along with the great Yelp reviews and the knowledge of Jim on my initial phone call I decided to have Leales do the job. 

I picked up the truck a little over a week later my total bill came in within the initial estimate, technicians JL and An did the work. Leales did find a couple related issues with my truck that needed fixing that I already knew about and was glad they took care of them. My first impression picking up the truck was no greasy fingerprints on the outside or inside of the truck, I expected some on a job this big. I have 1000 miles on the new engine and the truck runs like new, I couldn't of asked for the work to be done any better. Early on at one point I called a GM dealership and their estimate to do the work was more than two times what I ended up paying at Leales. If you need a major auto repair I highly recommended Leales, I'm sure they can handle the small stuff too.

text:
Leale's rebuilt the transmission in my old '98 Ford Explorer a few years ago. 2 years and 10 months ago, to be exact. 
The car broke down on my kid up in the Sierra's and ended up in a transmission shop in Modesto, where they explained to me that the converter had fallen apart and gotten into the transmission and needed to be completely rebuilt.
I called Leale's and because I had a 3 year warranty, they took care of it. They COMPLETELY took care of it. They tried to get it repaired in Modesto for us, and when that didn't work out, they had it towed to San Jose and fixed it. It turns out it just needed a torque converter solenoid. text:

text: On the way home to the East Bay from a wedding in Sacramento, my 2001 BMW 525i blew a transmission pump spewing oil all over the cars following me (serves you right for tailgating) and sending the transmission into 'safe' mode.  Since I knew the transmission was toast ... I just kept driving home ... and limped the car into my driveway.  Despite the 212K miles on my car - it is in pristine condition, mechanically and cosmetically ... I religiously maintain the car ... and I don't really want a new car payment in this sketchy economy.   So I phoned my regular BMW mechanic in Berkeley ... and he told me to junk the car, adding that he would NEVER install a used transmission (my only economical option).  I phoned another mechanic in my hometown of Lafayette ... and he told me the same thing.  I even phoned my LandRover mechanic ... and he never phoned me back.  So I went on a search through all the BMW boards, yelp, craigslist, etc. to find a transmission shop in the Bay Area who would be willing (and expert-enough) to install a quality, properly-matched, used transmission into a vintage BMW.  I had set my salvage project budget at 2K.  Leales name kept popping-up as I progressed through my search.  So I phoned Lyle at Leales and proceeded to give him the 5th degree about my transmission project.  Lyle inspired me with his confidence and knowledge about BMW transmissions, and the success-rate of swapping-out my particular model of transmission.  I was so impressed, that I was willing to ship my car from the East Bay to the South Bay to have the work done.  Lyle even hooked me up with an excellent towing company who only charged me $2.00/mile to ship my car.  An extra $220.00 ... but well worth it for finding the "right" transmission mechanic.  Lyle assisted in sourcing a quality used transmission (I ended-up buying on my own from Bavarian in Ranch Cordova - a mistake I will never make again).  Lyle FIRST evaluated the transmission to determine whether he could re-build for less money and a better warranty, but it was beyond repair.  So, instead, he installed the Bavarian transmission (perfectly) and the car was back-to-new !  Less than a week later, we discovered that the transmission from Bavarian was taken out of a 3-series BMW, not a 5-series, and it locked-up into safe mode.  I had to return the car to Lyle.  He had to reprogram the transmission ecu to run a 5-series BMW.  An unfortunate glitch in the project ... but I actually BLAME Bavarian for failing to properly advise us of the donor car model.  Lyle made all the changes necessary (and more) for FREE.  My wife has now had her beloved car back for about 3 months ... and it continues to run perfectly.  Believe me ... if you need and want quality transmission work (esp. for your BMW) ... Leale's is THE place to go.  BTW ... the project came in well-under my 2K budget ... including; the used transmission cost, the labor, and even the towing (x2).  And I am not buried in a new car payment.

text:
Leale's is not much different from any other auto shop. I took my car in around 10am on 

Day 1:
They did a prediagnostic (listened to it) and gave me an estimate on when they could get it into the garage. (1.5hrs) I opted to leave the car with them, and be shuttled home. (Bad idea?!) By 1:30pm Leale's had not called me with my diagnostic info. I had to call them! They had already looked at the car and figured out the problem, and were calling to order a part.

1. Firstly, they need to call ME when they find the problem and let me know
2. Secondly, don't order a part before I agree to service or know a price.

I was told I'd be contacted if they cold find a place with the right part for them to order. Leale's closes at 5pm. I called a 1:30 remember? No one EVER called be back that business day.

Day 2: 
I call Leale's just after 10am. They open at 8am. You'd think that they'd get back to me by now. The girl who answers says Mechanic-X is finishing my work order and he will call me in 10minutes. At 11:30am I've still not been contacted. I call them again. Finally, I'm told the extent of the problem.

"When can it be done?" I dunno, depends on when the part is delivered. So they ordered a part without my consent and no I don't know when I can have my car. (This is why you call people after you look at their car) The guy on the phone has that "I can't estimate the length of the job" tone of voice. Do mechanics always see every repair as unique, that they can't give us ballpark info? Finally upon more questioning, the dealer usually delivers the part around time-o'clock, and the labor is 30-45minutes, but likely my car won't be worked on today because the estimated date to get it back is DAY 3 at 2pm. Seriously?

"What's the approximate cost?" How can people do business and just hide the cost until you show up to pick up your car? I hate shops that just assume everything and go on to fix shi* before you even agree. I wanted an estimate! As you can see Leale's didn't have the part. I had two other places close by I could go to that might have stuff ready. Also these places might not have so much business they can't do a 45 minute job, and push me to the end of the next day. After prompting I found the total job was under $200.

Day 3: 
As you may have guessed there was no call when my part arrived or when work started on my car. I must have the best timing - right when I called they were done with the install and going to test-drive it. I'm not sure if I should fall for this last coincidence. I'm not sure when they came back from testing it, because they didn't call me. Yes, the trend is apparent now. Two hours later I finally get the car back. Job well done: as far as repairs go.
-----

Conclusion:
Leale's doesn't impress me. That's not how you do business.
Unless you want to keep tabs on them yourself, don't go here.
Unless you plan to sit in their office and remind them every half hour your car needs to be looked at for a diagnostic... don't go there.
If you don't mind them ordering parts on your behalf and going to work on your car before you agree on a price - then go to Leale's, because that's how they operate. They don't understand the customer's perspective.

They get 3 stars because they have the "service" part down, but the other half of a good business is the "customer" i.e.
CUSTOMER SERVICE, which they suck at.

text:
Alright, here I am posting a review to express the kindness of a mister at Leales's transmission. I pulled a transmission down from a BMW 2004 325i because it was leaking oil, I took to the auto repair, on behalf of someone suggestion. When I arrived at the place I explained that the transmission was leaking oil and that the car was making a noise under the back seat, they were very kind and helped me unloading the transmission from the trunk of my running car. 

I gave my info and was told that they were going to inspect it and let me know what was wrong, 4 hours later I got a call and was told the transmission was beyond repair/it would cost around $3500 to fix it.
So I said, I don't have that kind of money, then picked it up and BIENG HONEST THEY DID NOT CHARGE A PENNY FOR CHECKING IT. I went home and I got a call from the shop and they offered help to find a used transmission for $2000 to $3000 dollars. 

I said I didn't have that kind of money.

Long story short, my transmission was still good, i run the risk of fixing the leak and put it back on my car is running perfectly fine. 

The problem was the driveshaft, u joints were too stiff and that was causing a friction which shook the transmission multiple times and caused the seal by the oil pump and Tork convertor to loosen and leak oil. 
DO NOT ALWAYS BELIEVE WHAT YOU ARE TOLD.

So for the fact that my transmission was not inspected or it was inspected incorrectly I am giving 2 stars yelp review.

Again, the guys were very helpful, but were they truthful???

When there is an issue with a vehicle, the advisor is supposed to point it out. Every time I would ask, he would mumble something and walk away. text:
This store just charge and nothing else. Problem is never solved.

Last year I took my car to them with the issue that my car overheats, they told me radiator ,thermostat have gone bad and charged me $90 for the diagnosis. Those were replaced at a cost of ~$1200 here. Few months later again the same issue happened, that time they said car was low on coolant and they refilled it, they didn't even inspect the car.Just refilled it. Problem of car over heating was never addressed.

When issue happened again as I had lil/no confidence in them I took my car to another mechanic and he told me there's an issue with the radiator and the thermostat. Similar thing was informed by another mechanic who told coolant wasn't circulating well enough, that could be due to bad thermostat or any other reason , which causes car to overheat.
And finally I took my car back to them today as both radiator and thermostat were under the warranty. They tested the radiator and thermostat and confirmed its not whats causing the car to overheat. When I asked what the issue is , they said its has to be diagnosed and would charge another $90 bucks for that. 
Isn't this exactly the same problem for which I came here before and for which I've already been charged heavily and the problem was never actually solved, then why another fees for the same diagnosis ?? I along with my friend tried best to understand why I need to pay again but failed to. The problem of overheating should have been identified when I first came to them or for that matter even on my second visit. Why shall one customer pay again for the same issue if due diligence was not done at their end.
All they could say they've verified the radiator and thermostat and that's not what's causing the issue.As professionals they are the best person to confirm which component of car is faulty which is not. For me as a driver, I only see my car is overheating, I dont' understand my radiator is at fault or my thermostat has got jammed or any other issue . That is their job to identify and fix if they do take charge of customers's trust and vehicle. 

It make no sense to be charged again and again for the diagnosis of same problem that has been plaguing since months, just becuz the parts they replaced were not faulty. What if I replace another component on their suggestion , and issue still stays, do they expect me to pay another $90 for the diagnosis as the part they replaced is not causing the issue ??? Seriously ?

They need to understand customer comes up with a problem of a vehicle as a whole and not with a problem of component.

A harassing experience it has been here.

text: I recently bought a 2013 ford escape from what I thought was a reputable car dealership. Unfortunately even though the mileage was very low (under 30,000 miles) it was over the 3 year warranty, so I bought it as is and did not purchase the extended warranty. Well under 1000 miles of driving and 41/2 months of ownership the check oil light came on. So I took it into Preferred Auto Repair, and Fernando had advised me that the oil was still pretty clean, but could change my oil for $30 if I wanted it I figured even though the car came with a carfax, I really didn't know anything truly about it's mechanical history, and at least I would have a start time to when I needed the next oil change. Much to both Fernando's and my surprise, once the car was up on the rack he discovered two big problems.....the front passenger axle was leaking oil, and the a/c hose was leaking coolant. I was not happy to have to spend over $900 for these repairs, but Fernando went thoroughly through my car and reassured me that there were no other problems, and with the repairs done the car was like new. He made me feel very comfortable with his diagnosis and his sincere desire to correct the situation. Not happy about having to spend that kind of money on a newly purchased car, but thankful for the peace of mind that it is fixed, and I have found a honest and reliable service center.

text:
5 stars across the board from other yelpers, seems too good to be true.

In order to get 5 stars from me, you must have excellent customer service, quality, honesty, respect, integrity, love for the craft, and of course, a clean bathroom. All elements must be present. I am virtually insatiable. 
But you know what? The only negative thing I have to say about my overall experience with this place is that yelp should have given me the option of adding a bonus 6th star to my rating for Preferred Auto Repair (PAR). 

From the initial phone call, which by the way was crisp and clear with no static or call dropping, I already knew that this place was the one. I recently moved back to Santa Clara after a few years and had some trouble with the voltage regulator of my wonderful 1991 Toyota MR2, Cassandra. I was in denial about replacing the alternator as I had just done so within the last two years, but El Nino's torrential downpours shorted something in it and did damage to Cassandra's ventricles. I explained this to Fernando, who listened. Wait, what? Yeah! He LISTENED! I find it very rare to compel a mechanic's full attention to my ceaseless gushing about my car - but that's what sets PAR apart; they employ empathetic automotive professionals.

Anyhoo, the tone, the politeness, the courteousness, all of it. Excellent customer service. I hung up the phone so happy to have found a trustworthy shop. I'm usually a pretty suspicious-of-everything, skeptical type of person, especially when it comes to my car because I perform most of my repairs and have had many experiences where opportunists have attempted to take advantage of me, whom they presumed to be a clueless girl. PAR won me over!

Dropped my car off - got an oil change and a proper diagnosis. Received a call informing me of the issues: yes, I need a new alternator; OEM is better, more reliable, but I had the option of opting for the cheaper alternative OEM part not currently in stock, but their vendor could have it shipped to them within a few hrs to one day and it would still be ready by the end of the following business day. Oil change - high mileage (Cassandra's got like, 340K miles on her) done done done. Battery - fried by the alternator, don't need to buy a new one, just return it to where I purchased it because it's covered under warranty. 

They provided me with the prices of everything, estimated time for repair, suggested alternatives, and accommodated my time/travel needs. I also got free wiper blades for checking in via yelp! Did I mention the warranties on parts and labor? YEP. I really can't emphasize further how impressed I am. 

I'm going to be replacing Cassandra's bushings and clutch relatively soon, so I'll be back to write a follow up of how great this place is, that is, if I haven't already convinced you.

I went here when I had purchased a used car and wanted to check if everything was okay. The service then was great. Fernando delivered excellent customer service. This was ~2 years ago. 

Recently went in because my coolant light was on and I was worried something bad was going to happen. I think because I had been a customer before Fernando had felt he had built up trust with me already. I was quoted $125 for an hour of diagnostic test, which I complied to because I was desperate. He then quoted me nearly a $1900 of which to repair my water pump and engine coolant. That's a lot to front up at once so I made a few phone calls and researched via google of what these services would normally cost. Low and behold, the quote I received didn't sit right with me, I was almost taken advantage of. 

I called other places for quotes to see if what I had researched was correct and I was appalled by the quote Fernando had given me. The price others had given me was LESS THAN HALF of what Fernando had quoted. One place even told me that I was clearly getting taken advantage of and to take my car out of the shop immediately. Needless to say I paid for just the diagnostic test and took my car out of his shop. I later went to a different shop and got exactly the same services done for MUCH less than what I was quoted here at Preferred Auto Body. 

Don't be fooled by Fernando's charm in handling his phone calls to you. He is very professional in how he explains things to you and how he treats you but in terms of fair pricing for services, he charges way more than other places. 

Needless to say, I will not be coming back & wouldn't recommend my friends or family to come here either.

text: We brought our van in back in July to have an oil leak checked out, expecting at worst for it to be a few hundred dollars. Two hours later the price escalates to over $2000. Nobody ever called back, finally I call them at 7pm Saturday and the guy apologizes, they got busy and forgot... the van wouldn't be ready until Monday. Monday rolls around, it's finally finished just before noon, total damage is just a few dollars shy of $3000. They apologize for the skyrocketing price, and insist that everything is fully guaranteed for a year. A month later, on the first out of town trip we take, the transmission fails completely (yeah, they serviced the transmission), leaving me stranded roadside for half a day. Local shop says the transmission has completely failed, estimate is over $4K. Rather than standing behind their work, they tell me they can replace the transmission for $3400. Don't trust their estimates, don't trust their workmanship, don't trust their guarantee.

text:
I brought my RV in for a safety inspection to the owner Fernando, on July 30, 2015 because I was going to take it on two trips soon. He agreed to inspect the vehicle and brakes for $50. After doing so the only thing he recommended was a front brake job since the brakes pads were at 15% and an oil change. He agreed to apply the inspection fee to the work and charged $350 to "Perform Front Brake Service, INCLUDING Installing New Premium Front Brake Pads" and $50 for an oil change. 

A couple of weeks after Preferred worked on the brakes of my RV. I was on the way to Monterey today when I started smelling the brakes overheating as I was driving. A short time later the brakes would pull to the left when I hit them, and the front end felt a bit jerky. I also started to notice some brake fade. I pulled over in Morgan Hill and checked under the car. Both the front brake were radiating a lot of heat, even 6 inches away. I got in and noticed the brake pedal went all the way to the floor. After the brakes cooled off for about a 1/2 hour I could get enough pressure in the brakes to carefully drive it home. 

Since I could not use the RV for the trip, I needed to get up at 4 am tomorrow to drive down to Monterey in my car since I have a job there from Friday through Sunday. 

After this trip, I dropped off the RV for three days, at the end of which he was able to duplicate the problem. When I asked if Fernando if he turned the rotors or bled the brakes, he admitted all he did for $350 was change the pads. 

At this point, he pointed out that the rotors were warped (which they were not before he worked on it, or he would have replaced them instead of just changing the pads. He gave me a quote for $2000 to fix the front brakes and change the master cylinder (which is working fine).

Since he miss-represented what he charged me for on the front brakes I brought the RV to Mission Valley Ford for an inspection since I had my next trip coming up soon. The Service Advisor for Mission Valley Ford agreed to inspect the brakes to determine what was causing the problem. The service manager called me the next day and stated that the brake pads were installed incorrectly, which caused the severe dragging and the rotor and caliper damage. He also said that the original inspection missed problems with the rear brake cylinders which could have caused them to fail. 

In addition to the $2300 incurred by Preferred's poor workmanship, I spent hours getting the brakes fixed correctly, and I had to cancel one trip. And their work could have resulted in an accident which may have led to a car crash, and worse yet bodily harm had I not canceled by trip and turned around.

text:
I found Fernando on Craig's lists when searching for someone to provide a brake job at a reasonable price. My search started after MIDAS quoted almost $450 (parts and labor) per axle (even with their special). I call Preferred Auto for and estimate; Fernando answered and said I could buy the parts or he would buy them and give me close to whole cost. 

After taking information he said he would call back in a few minutes with a quote. Fernando called back in 15 minutes with three prices (cheap, OEM, and performance). I had been looking around and found his estimates competitive with web wholesale prices and asked him to get the parts. We made an appointment for the afternoon.

I arrived on time and Fernando already had the parts. On this day he was quite busy but still found a way to get done in a very reasonable amount of time. Not only did I save over $230 per axle, I found a reliable, honest, mechanic that I will use again and again.

Preferred Auto Repair is a small business with Fernando and one tech to meet their customer requirements. His place is a little hard to find but worth the challenge. He is great to talk with and is very interested in making his customer come back because of the service. He does not take checks (cash or debit only) but does guarantee his work.

Since this first experience I brought in a second car for a brake job that was suggested by the dealer. In this case I already had the parts since I was looking for a specific brand. Fernando evaluated the breaks and said that unless I was having problems, there was over 50% of the pads left and that the rotors were fine. I had him perform the service even though he said the service was not needed. He did a great job and his honesty will have me returning especially as he adds more services (alignments in September).

I will be using Preferred Auto for most of my repair needs in the future.

text:
Here's the short and direct review: Fernando is a great kind of mechanic that you want to have for as long as you own a vehicle. I just moved to San Jose and didn't know any mechanic down here and didn't want to get ripped off from some untrustworthy mechanic. Stress really began to set in due to desperately needing to have my van's brakes fixed because I suddenly needed to be the caretaker for my elder mother recovering from a stroke! I had a very limited budget and worse very little time to get my van's brakes done. While searching on craigslist, I found Fernando's ad.(thank goodness for that).A bit weary, at first I called to get an estimate from this place called, "Preferred Tire and Auto Repair." To my relief, Fernando was polite, professional, and most importantly trustworthy! Needless to say, Fernando got the job done while getting me a great price.

This is the type of mechanic you can count on. If you're in San Jose, CA then Fernando is the mechanic you want to trust to get the job done right the first time as well as being thorough. You will feel confident to recommend him to your friends and family. Bottom line, if you're in a jam, you will want to call Fernando to help you with your car situation.

So, it all started when I kept hearing a terrible noise coming from my van every time I stepped on my brakes. The noise kept getting louder, so I felt it was time to have it checked out on my 2005 Ford Freestar cargo van. Having recently moved down to San Jose, Ca from San Francisco, I felt a bit stressed out because I didn't know of any honest and trustworthy mechanic down here. Other mechanics provided me with terribly overpriced estimates. Thus, I began to get that sinking feeling as to where to start and add to that having little time to do the research due to having to drive up to the city to help my senior mother that just got discharged from the hospital. 

The stress factor began to set in.with needing to have my van's brakes fixed in order to transport my elderly mother. Like most people, I decided my first starting point would be a Ford dealership, bad idea. The Ford dealership would have charge me a ridiculous amount. Talk about sticker shock from that quote, I knew I had to find a much better place to get my brakes fixed. As with most people, I am on a very tight budget, this brake problem really put me in a tough spot., especially with my mother's health situation. I called a few other mechanics but the results were less than favorable due to: terrible price quotes (too high), terrible response from worker over the phone, communication problem due to a very heavy foreign accent, lousy customer service, or just plain rude. Things started to look quite grim. Finally, I remember to check www.craigslist.org under, "auto" I found Preferred Tire and Auto Repair. 

I was still a bit apprehensive since I did not know anything about this auto repair shop, but with a limited budget and severe time constraints, I decided to give him a call. Very good decision! Fernando was polite, professional and most importantly very responsive. He called me back in about 10 minutes after doing some research to secure quality parts for my brake job. I needed to make arrangements for my roommate to help me out since I could not leave my ailing mother for too long up in San Francisco despite Fernando being down in San Jose. (I live down in San Jose). So, my roommate was very kind enough to meet me at a halfway between cities in Redwood city and from there drive down to Fernando's auto shop. 

Fernando was a great help to get my van's parts ordered a day prior so he could work on the van right after my roommate dropped off my van. Fernando was even kind enough to drop off my roommate at a near by Starbucks while he was fixing my van. I think he will have another new customer because of that.

Midpoint into fixing my van, Fernando kept me apprised of his progress. Finally, when he was done, he gave me a call at which point I provided him my credit card. The next day my roommate dropped off my van to me up in San Francisco. My brakes were working perfectly to my great relief and my mother's! 

Needless to say, Fernando did a superb job and eased a great deal of stress for me. Thanks so much to Fernando, who is a great representative of the kind of mechanic you can trust and have for as long as you own a vehicle. Plus, he is a solid local shop, entrepreneur, and family guy! He knows how important a vehicle is to individuals and very understanding, so support this solid mechanic and trust your business to him, I did and I am so relieved that I made that decision to do just that.

UPDATE: I have since used Fernando again (rear brakes and cv joint replacement). As one would expect, he again along with his one employee, Jeremy came through for me on a Saturday! Not many mechanics work on Saturdays but Fernando does because he knows what it takes to accommodate busy and for me stressed out customers.

text:
I set my CAR for service on 8/13/2021.
The request was for Engine oli change, break check, Engine check as there was some noise at the start of the car and engine light blinked couple of times.

After the thorough check they suggested to change series of things: Coolant flush, Engine Flush, Fuel injector cleaning, Spark Plug change, Valve cover Gasket change & Variable Valve Timing Control Solenoid change & Break change. To service this they charged me $2.2K for my 2007 Mazda.

Took the car on Friday and added 30~35 miles and the car broke down near to Santa Cruz on Sunday 8/15/2021. There was lot of smoke in bonnet and inside car. We were not able to see anything outside. It was dangerous. The car didn't start. Called Service guy to check the fault about this. They stated that this might have not happed because of their service, he needs to check for details and notified that he will do repair if its his issue. I towed the car to his service station for check.

The next day, he stated that there was no coolant and oil, the pressure got built up and the engine exploded because of weak Engine & Piston rod. The connecting rod and cylinder has ruptured creating hole on top of the engine cap. This has nothing to do with Service is what he claims.

I don't believe this. The whole thing look like there was a coolant arrest and the Engine got heated up. The pressure was built and the cylinder exploded because of heat arrest. This is possible only if the coolant is not getting circulated to Engineer while it is running. I suspect the above service would have caused this. May be mis alignment of gasket or engine assembly or some thing left out in the process. If everything was done well, the service guy should have checked this before he delivered me the car.

Value Added Cost of going to this Service is: Engine replacement - 4K to 6K as per the Fernando, on top of the 2.2K service charge which was spent for nothing. I feel that i got robbed.

All this happened in just 2 days. Just be careful with this service team. He charges exorbitant and claims no fault of his, if it fails.

text:
People, people, people.... if you drive and occasionally have car problems, then THIS is where you have to take your car. Whether it's a domestic or import vehicle, Hung is your man.

What he lacks in ambience, he makes up for with honesty, know-how, and hard work. 

I've been going to him for probably ten years, if not more. I used to drive a little '89 Nissan Sentra. Once it started to get old and used, I had to get work done on it. I didn't even get a quote from Hung most of the time because it was my only car, and I'd just ask him to "fix it!"

And fix it he would The price of this was ALWAYS less than I'd expect to pay. In fact, a couple times after he told me how much, I'd ask him if he even looked at the problem because it sounds like he just changed the oil. He used to do that without asking because I never was consistent with that kind of stuff, and then he wouldn't charge me for it, either. 

One time when I got my car back, I realized something was odd... my radio was working. It never worked because I didn't have an antenna. Well, Hung found one at the P&P for my car, and connected it without charging me, or telling me! THAT'S SERVICE!!

Now that I have my Mini, Mini of Mountain View does all the work. (It's part of my service package, and I don't get charged.) So Hung only gets to work on hubby's Civic now. But he does it with the same kind of service, the same low prices, and with the same results: HAPPY DRIVERS.

If you speak Vietnamese or English, then you won't have a problem communicating with him. I think he has some help now that speak Spanish. So go on in and let him know that you heard about him on Yelp from Shari (who now has a Mini, but had a Nissan Sentra) and even though he'll probably look at you funny over the word "Yelp", he will probably know who I AM. 

He rocks, people!

text:
In terms of honesty and helpfulness, Thanh goes above and beyond what one would normally expect from an auto mechanic. It's obvious from his actions that he cares very much about establishing and maintaining his reputation.
Here's my story. The check engine light lit up in my Audi A4, and the power seemed a little weak, so I found Thanh via yelp and gave him a call. He said he could diagnose it, but he was really busy and told me to come by around 4:30 (a couple of hours from when I called.) I showed up at 4, and sure enough he was pretty busy. I guess word gets around. He let me know that he'd get to me as soon as he could. 

I ended up waiting for about 10 minutes and then he rushed out of his garage with computer in-hand to diagnose my problem. He found the high-level problem, but the computer didn't give enough details to show what the actual fix was. It just said that the engine was "running lean." He said that it would require a full diagnostic which would take a few hours, and gave me a ballpark of $300-400 for this repairing this type of thing, but of course he wouldn't know until after the diagnostic.

He then noticed the mileage on my car. I actually thought my car should be out of warranty because I crossed the 40K mark. text:
I have never had a bad experience with the Yelp recommendations until this one. I was in desperate need of an oil change because I was about a month over due and having my old mechanic move out of town, I needed to find another mechanic. I went on yelp and found Thanh's Auto Service & Repair to be highly acclaimed and excitingly made my way to the Auto Shop. 

Well, it was Saturday and granted, I should have called to see if they could fit me in, but i decided to drive anyways. I made it to the shop and true to my gut feeling, Thanh said he was too busy and said to come later in the week. So I made an appointment for the following week. 

Well, I arrive at my appointment a couple of minutes late and was excited to get my oil change. Well, no one was there to receive me and one of the mechanics that didn't speak English just said to wait 5 minutes because he was on a test drive. Well, 5 minutes turned to 20 minutes. Not too bad of a wait, but seeing that I had an appointment, I was disappointed. Minus 1 Star for that. 

When Thanh came back from the test drive, I met him in the office and I told him I needed an oil change. He told me to wait outside and that he'd be 5 - 10 minutes. Well, seeing that there was no seats to wait inside, I went back to my car and waited another 20 minutes for him to even acknowledge me. Thanh then came back and told me, that it'll be 5 minutes again, and that he was going to service my car. Well, from the beginning till this point I waited around 45 minutes till he said that he was finally going to work on my car. 

Well, another 10 minutes later, he finally got my car not on the lift but under the lift and had to jack up my car to get the oil changed. Well, the oil change itself took another 20 minutes and I was expecting to get my free tire rotation (which is proudly displayed on his website) but he didn't do that also! *Another reason why I took off a star. 

Well, I was already annoyed because, I've been waiting around an hour and a half, I saw that my tires weren't rotated even though he boasts that he does it for free, and he didn't even check my tire pressure and fluid levels. *Another star taken off. 

He was gracious to take a dollar off because it took so long. And he did shake my hand and apologized for the wait. But I did make an appointment and he said I arrived 30 minutes late. I know I was 5 minutes late, but you don't argue and call your customer a liar. Overall, not satisfied at all. *Another star taken off.

I called at 11:30 am and was told the next available appointment was at 12:30pm.... got there at 12:30pm and was greeted by Thanh. I told him what the stealership said I needed... he personally inspected the mini cooper and told me that I actually did need the rear brake pad replacement and the brake fluid flush... but not the coolant flush... after the work was done on my car he said he didn't replace the rear brake pad sensors because they were still in-tact (and since i didn't need the brake pad sensors replaced he didn't charge me for the part and saved me money!). Quick, friendly, inexpensive, quality work.

For ~$320 (includes parts, labor, and tax), my mini cooper received
rear brake pad replacement
brake fluid flush

I am sold. I'll be taking my car to Thanh's for all future maintenance work.

fyi, I asked how many mini cooper cars he has worked on - my mini was his 2nd. Impressed, I am.

text:
Based on Yelp reviews, I took my car in last February knowing it needed quite a bit of work. Having hit over 100K miles, the car needed a water pump and gasket replacement (I think, though this was -already- replaced at 70K miles), a new timing belt, power steering pump belt, alternator belt, and a few other parts replaced. My rear struts had also been leaking. Not a lot of places fix struts so this was another reason I came to Thanh's.

I know my car quite well and lately felt that something was wrong in the rear -- perhaps the brakes. My regular mechanic just told me my brake pads are fine, except that my rear struts are leaking again. I know that good struts will last you about 50K miles -- and the only driving I do is around the South Bay, mostly just to and from work (a 20 minute drive at best). 

I pulled out my old work orders and noticed that Thanh's only has a one year warranty on all of his work. I called him and explained the situation to him and he proceeded to say that it could be due to faulty struts which is not his fault, but rather the vendor's. He told me to bring the car in to assess it, and he would give me a new estimate which would likely not include the parts -- as again, he would have to discuss it with the vendor. 

Last year I paid $1,207.62 for all the repairs on my 2002 Honda Civic, which has never been in an accident ($467.39 parts, $697.00 labor, + tax). I find it questionable that the shop would use poor quality parts, which may be why his repairs are much more affordable than other shops. 

In addition, last year, Thanh told me there was a leak in my oil pan, which to this day I believe was not true and that I needed some type of Honda caps replaced that were "cracked". We have a two car tandem garage, and I'm the only one that parks in our garage. There are no oil spots on the ground where I park. In the past year also, I've taken my car to my regular mechanic as well as a Honda dealership for regular maintenance -- both of which NEVER mentioned any type of leak or parts that needed replacement. You would think the Honda dealership would try to upsell...

I would hesitate to take my car here based on my personal experience -- though the pricing for the repairs was not astronomical, I did feel that I was being duped with extraneous repairs. I'm debating whether or not I still want to take my car back in with his offer -- I'm not sure that I want his shop doing any more work on my car. That being said, because I haven't allowed him to assess the problem, am I giving this service and repair shop two stars instead of one for my negative experience -- though if he offered to fix everything, I'd definitely bump up the stars.

text:
After purchasing my first car, I decided to go on this car journey alone. It is time for me to venture out and find my own solutions on where to go and who to trust about maintaining a car. Plus, my family haven't been having much luck with car service and repair shops.

So, when I decided to take it for it's first oil change by me I decided to go find out who will fit me and my car best.

The first one I actually approached was located across from Thanh's Auto Service & Repair. I pulled up to the front and stepped out. A fairly handsome looking fellow and a Mexican accent greeted me with a smile.

I asked if I can have an oil change. He smiled and said that they were too busy today for an oil change. He said I could come by later on in the week. I smiled back and said, "oh ok."

Mind you, when I plan something to get done, I will get it done. So, on this day, I plan on getting my oil change done and I know there were plenty of places to get it done.

I moved on to the next, and it just so happens to be "Thanh's Auto Service & Repair."

I walked over (okay, I lied. I didn't pulled up to the front. I parked in between the two shops so it doesn't look like my car belonged to any shops) Thanh's front office. When I first walked in, I didn't see anyone. Then I saw two eyes peering barely over the computer screen, "Hi! Can I help you?"

I asked for an oil change. "Sure. Where's your car?" He grabbed my keys and took it to the back. (yeah, it was that quick)

Perhaps he saw me walking into the other shop and notice I was refused service and wanted to grab a potential long term customer. Or maybe he wasn't as busy that day and was able to squeeze in a new customer. (I guess I will never know)

Shortly after (and when I say 'shortly', I meant the time was short enough for me to stay there and wait for my oil change to be finished instead of me leaving and coming back later to pick up my car) he rang me up (about $20) and then off I go.

Heres the kicker that I left out, between the phone calls, managing his employees, running to and from the back, he manage to hold a conversation from beginning to end. He's a multi-tasker; rare indeed. Thanh's very genuine in his concern of our expenses and car. He's very honest of what needs to be done right away and what can wait. I often times push him and his crew to give me a tune-up every 2-4 months, but he always tell me that not to worry that your car is fine. "You're very good at maintaining your car. And you get things that need to be fixed right away. You're car is fine. I will let you know when you need a tune up. For now everything's fine." Now, how many mechanics you know tells you that?

6 Months later, I ended up moving out of the city. At this point, I felt attached to my mechanic. He understood my car, understood how I like to get things done and of course -I trust him. I decided to keep him.

Yeah, he is worth the 30 minute drive just for an oil change.

On June 16th I was in distraught due to the fact that one of my headlights had gone out . I reached out to my close friend Diane who referred me to this place. On the phone , I explained to him the situation where I needed my ballast replaced . I gave him all the information needed and he quoted for 150 in order to do so. He told me he was able to take me in the next morning and have it done within 2 hours . I woke up the next morning of June 17th , excited and arrived at 7:58 am. I gave him my car keys and took an Uber home . 2 hours later he contacted me saying he wasn't able to replace the ballast ( provided by me ) because he didn't know how to open the headlight and he thought something was taped and was leaking and what not . He also suggested that I needed to purchase the whole entire headlight assembly. His perplexing various reasons on why he couldn't do the job got me even more confused when he said he still needed to charge me for the labor . I agreed and gave him the money because at the time he had my car keys and If I disagreed Lord knows what would happen to me on his property .
I took it to Bright Auto Lights the next day and Tony installed my ballast and had my light working within an hour . Tony asked me who worked on my car previously because they did not put the parts back properly . 

At this point , I was exasperated at Thanh auto repair . If you were going to tell me you were able to replace something you should at least know if you were capable to do so instead of promising you could and quoted me and asked me to come at 8am . Not only you weren't able to fulfill your duties , your employee did not put my car back properly and you had the audacity to charge me for labor ? For "spending time putting my car back" . I'm enraged due to the fact that Diane , my best friend who has your personal number and trusted you and referred me to you as a personal friend and you did me dirty like that . 
I'm truly disheartened and traumatized by the unethical chain of events that had happened here .

text: I read the excellent reviews on yelp and decided to give Thanh's a try. My truck was running poorly - I thought the rear wheel bearing was seizing up - lot of grinding. I limped my truck to Thanh's and that very same day he called me up and said the wheel bearing was worn but that it wasn't the problem and said he needed to open up the differential. He told me that they won't start any repair work without my approval. The next day on Thursday I get a phone call: Bad news - the differential was badly damaged (case, gears) and recommended that I get the whole rear axle replaced. I was given the option for a new rear axle or a used one - he said for only $400 more I could get the new axle instead of the used one. I liked that he gave me that option and even said he shopped around to get the lowest price. Also, he got the part from the dealer who said a customer had ordered it but changed his mind. He said he could have it done by Saturday but to give him a call on Friday. Called up Friday afternoon - the truck was ready! Well I got the truck and it ran perfectly - they even adjusted my parking/emergency brakes. It's been 5 days since I got my truck back, no fluid leaks or any other problems. It was an expensive repair, but my model truck and year are notorious for the rear differential to disintegrate - I read a lot of blogs from other owners of the same truck who paid MUCH higher prices to get their rear axle replaced. If your vehicle is having problems, you might want to give Thanh's a try like I did. They may not be as fast repairing your vehicle for a lot of reasons, but when they get to work, they don't mess around.

text:
Long time customer with long overdue review. Thahn runs a very professional and ethical business. I've come to him with write ups from the dealership for expensive repairs and he'll look it over and give his honest opinion. 

I'm very comfortable with all his recommendations and trust his judgement. He'll let me know if the work is warranted and quote me a reasonable estimate, or he'll say we can wait and watch to defer to a later date, or he'll tell me that the other write up is bs and isn't needed. This happened once when I took my car in to Toyota for a recall item and they "recommended" I replace my water pump and timing chain. Thanh laughed and said he already did that work a few months ago!

Today I was witness to someone trying to shake him down. A date was missing on an inspection he did and the customer was very rude and angry. But he said he would "forget" about it if Thahn gave him a $20 discount. If he didn't, he would give him a "bad review".

Thahn apologized and offered to refund the whole inspection fee of $40, which would go back on the credit card. The funny thing is the customer didn't want the credit card refunded, he wanted the cash ! Obviously the $40 would go on his employer's card but the $20 would go into his own pocket. 

The customer stormed off without either a refund or his shake down. I was impressed that Thahn even offered a full refund over such a insignificant oversight.

Don't let any negative reviews dissuade you from going to Thahn. He is the best!
