text:
Thanh seems like a very good guy and I would come back again, but there were definitely some issues in this recent visit regarding my Toyota Prius that I'd hope to not experience next time around. Assuming he and his team provide the level of service I think they can deliver, I would be happy to adjust my review to 5 Stars! The story is below.

The car was brought in for a timing belt cover repair after Thanh quoted a good price for the work over the phone (a similar price was later also quoted by another independent and both were about 40% less than the dealer estimate).

When Thanh and his team checked out the car, they also recommended a repair to the water hose - something the dealer did not identify or recommend. Thanh graciously showed me the water hose area stains and offered a good price to do the work so I agreed. At that point, I also pointed out a repair for the antenna and he indicated they could install a new antenna at a low price so I agreed to that work also. We agreed on a target date for the work to be completed (only a few days later) and he was going to call me when the car was ready for pick up.

I never received a call and called in later that day that it was to be done. He said the car was ready and I could come by to pick it up.

When I came by to pick it up, the antenna repair was not done. Apparently, he'd forgotten. This happens, no big deal. He agreed to get right on it and see if he could fix it right then. He was very apologetic and I went to run a couple of errands. After some further research, he realized the antenna repair required was going to be a big project because the wire to the antenna as well as the base needed to be repaired. This would require disassembling a number of parts in the interior of the car and take a lot of time. We agreed this did not make sense and I later recalled a similar assessment from the dealer a year or two prior.

After getting the car home, the next day, the car would not start. I called AAA to get a jump and it started fine. They recommended I get a replacement 12 volt battery which I proceeded to do- another $150 of cost. However, I also noticed as I drove the the auto supplies store that the Prius digital display was not showing the arrows that usually appear when the car runs and when the engine is charging the battery for the motor. 

I called Thanh to explain and he took my call, was very patient, listened and made some suggestions about what I may have done. I inquired if it was possible something happened when they did the work, maybe they did not put back a belt or some kind of connection. He assured me not, however was willing to take a look.

Without getting into all the various other details, I eventually made it back to Thanh's shop and I had pushed together a couple of connectors to see if something was loose. We also found the interior signal light indicator clicking quickly which Thanh told me indicated that one of the lights was out. We pressed and a couple of those connectors and the light signals began working properly again. While we never definitively found out why the battery for the motor was not recharging, I continue to believe it was because something did not get re-assembled properly when the work was done. My sense is that it could have been an innocent, unfortunate mistake, oversight. It may have not been the issue. We just don't know.

The car seems to drive OK now, although there is a sort of "clunking" sound that I don't recall from before. We continue to drive it cautiously and I'm hoping it will be just fine.

Thanh was a true gentleman throughout this process and I wanted to share the feedback with him, my view of the story through this review, so he can take it to heart and maybe slow down just a little bit. He seemed quite busy and possibly just a bit too busy. I wish him the best and plan to come back, hoping for a 5 star experience next time.

text:

text:
It's official -- I was a total believer in Thanh's shop. I took my car there repeatedly for a few years while I lived nearby. Fast forward to a few months ago. I take my car in for a routine oil change and fluid flush and Thanh calls to tell me there's a problem -- I need a new clutch, so I should wait to flush out my manual transmission fluid until that's replaced so someone can do all of the work at one time. Now, my 03' Toyota has had all sorts of crazy problems, so I wasn't all that surprised about my clutch. I tell Thanh that I can't afford it now, but I'll return with the car so he can do the whole transmission/clutch at the same time. Well, we move to Santa Cruz and a month or so passes when I take my car into another Yelp favorite, a repair shop near my home. I tell the owner what Thanh told me, so he takes my car for a test drive, puts it up in the air to look at the clutch AND the fluid, and tells me that he sees no evidence that my clutch needs to be replaced (or that my fluid needs to be flushed). Not only that, but he spends AN HOUR doing these diagnostics and doesn't charge me a penny -- only a "Come back when you need an oil change!" send-off. 

Now, I know what you're thinking -- maybe it's a difference in professional opinion, right? Well, maybe. But having a clutch replaced is very expensive and a pretty significant repair, so I would have to think that it's pretty clear one way or the other if this repair needs to be done. Accordingly, I lost my faith in Thanh -- especially because, during that conversation where he made the recommendation, he said, "You know, I don't recommend things that you don't need. I'm very honest."

So, if this shop recommends a big repair, get a second opinion. It might save you a lot of money.

text:

The battery checked okay and the cable connections were clean and secured to the battery terminals. I called the dealer and a couple of shops to get an idea of what can it be and to get an estimate on the cost to diagnose the problem. The quotes for diagnosis only ranged from $128 to $155 and nobody was willing to say what are the various things that can be wrong. I searched the internet and found Thanh's shop which had excellent reviews. I called Thanh who quoted me $45 and said that if it's something "quick" there will be no charge. I drove the car to Thanh who checked it but the problem didn't occur so I left the car with him. Thanh was kind enough to have one of his employees give me a ride home. The next morning I got a call from Thanh that he was able to duplicate the problem and that the fault is with the starter. Replacing a starter on a Lexus is a big job because the starter is under the intake manifold. Thanh quoted $680 out of the door. Checking prices with other shops it was almost double that.
The car was ready the next day, starting perfectly and my invoice out of the door was lower than Thanh's original estimate. It was a pleasure to be Thanh's client, he is friendly, hard working an honest businessman who really cares about customer satisfaction. I highly recommend Thanh's shop to anybody who needs quality work for a fair price.

Within a week of having the cars serviced by Than fluids started POURING out both! At first I thought they just forgot to top off the fluids. Turned out he Honda had a badly leaking water pump, and the Subaru had a loose lug on the power steering line, was missing a bolt from the oil pan, and had a leaking gasket that was allowing oil to get to the spark plugs! When I took the cars back (Prior to having someone else look at them) Than immediately said the Subaru must need a new rack and pinion due to the power steering leak - $800. 

Well, needless to say I got a second opinion, and then talked to some other mechanics about the diagnostic techniques... The question is: why - when I brought in both cars and said they need major tune-ups - would Than steer me towards only doing minimal work, when those major tune-ups were really necessary? 

Maybe Than's a victim of his own success, I don't know. I never got a sense that he was taking any responsibility for his guy's work. 

Yup, it's cheap... And you get what you pay for! I'm not going back.

text:
THE GOOD:

This small shop is ran by a guy name Earl. Seems to have been in business for quite some time. I go to him on a Monday 10/20/25 for a smog diagnosis that he charged $95, about the standard price. He was able to complete the inspection and gave me a diagnosis back same day (approx. 4 hours total time). He offered a free throttle body clean because upon their inspection, the throttle was dirty and had a lot of carbon build up. I was notified the vehicle would be ready for pick up at 4:15PM, I told him I was going to be there 4:30PM. When I had arrived, earl was nice enough to wait around after they had closed for me to receive my vehicle.

THE BAD:

After I paid him for the diagnosis, he told me what was wrong and gave me the keys, then promptly left with a friend that was awaiting him. Right after I pulled off in my car, something was awfully wrong. The idle RPMS was sitting at almost 2K RPMS on a cold start and would come to about 1500-1900RPMS the entire time. As I was driving while hitting the gas you could hear what sounded like was a vacuum leak somewhere and car has some minor lost power. I call Earl immediately after, but he was already gone from the shop; Earl told me to just bring it in first thing in the morning. I bring the vehicle back to Earl on 10/21/25 a day later and present to him what had sounded like a vacuum leak. He was quick to check into but also VERY QUICK TO DENY RESPONSIBILITY. I told him that the vehicle was 110% not like this when I had brought it in and they definitely may have knocked a hose or two loose or something. 

They first told me they would not doing anything like that, and wanted to run a smoke down test in-front of me to check for vacuum leaks. I was told by Earl, they only took off the air intake boot to access the throttle body to spray carb cleaner and there's absolutely no way they caused any of the issues presented. They run the test, and there shows no leaks from the smoke. They also run a brake clean spray to see if it will choke the RPMs down (another method to check for vacuum leaks). We go for a couple of test drives back and forth, the mechanic that Earl has working for him, poor guys age is catching up to him and cannot hear a huge vacuum leak for his life.
Earl claims to hear it as well, but cannot figure out what it is. Earl first blames the brake booster, and is adamantly asserting that he or his shop did not cause this. 

***Earl THEN DISCOVERS A MISSING connection on my VSV, but the old mechanic claims it won't cause any vacuum leaks or noises and just caps it off.***. 

They then proceed to say the noise and high RPMS is an exhaust leak and show me where it is leaking. You can see exhaust smoke coming out the pipe right below the manifold but I wouldn't say it was sufficient enough to be causing such a vacuum leak noise. They adjudicate the issue is an exhaust leak, therefore, they did not cause it and cannot fix it anyways. 

It is worth mentioning I am not by any means a mechanic. I am what you call a garage monkey. I understand some concepts, but no way am I to be at the SUPPOSED level these guys are at. I have my doubts so I go home and take apart the air intake boot and further inspect the throttle body. There it is, lo and behold a vacuum line disconnected from the throttle body that was suppose to be connected the VSV. 

To summarize everything , 
Earl is a truthfully a honest guy it seems, but is seemingly incompetent on the work and guys working for him do rushed, shoddy, crude, messy work. It's not hard taking off an air intake boot and reconnecting all necessary hose lines back. Paid $95 for some problems they claim they didn't cause and don't believe the customer, ONLY to take it back home and undo the bad work they did. Crazy stuff and would not go back. Be wary of what you're doing here.

text:
The only good thing about this place is Earl can usually get you in right away. I went to him for years and had a lot replaced on a used car, and now I don't trust any of the work he did. 

I stopped going to him after having to redo a few of his repairs that were done incorrectly: one time I had a big engine oil leak after I had replaced a filter myself. I had used an aftermarket part and learned it was a bad fit. Instead of replacing the filter with an OEM one, Earl put *orange silicone* all over the aftermarket filter, and the solenoid valve it led to--all over inside my engine. And it still leaked after that! I ended up replacing the filter with OEM myself, which fixed it, and then later when I had the money took it to another shop to clean out all the orange silicone from the engine. Everyone I've mentioned this to said to never take my car back to him, so I didn't.

Ever since I bought my car, I struggled with mysterious engine problems that didn't present themselves on the test drive. It was a real pain. Later, after trying several small repairs myself and taking my car to other shops, one place found the *wrong spark plugs* were in my Honda. They were spark plugs meant for a VW or Subaru... I had had the wrong spark plugs in my car ever since I bought it, because I'd taken it straight to Earl for a tune-up. For YEARS afterward I dealt with mysterious misfiring and loss of power that resulted in a number of attempts to repair whatever was wrong, some of which I paid Earl to do! I've probably wasted thousands of dollars with this guy. The problems disappeared after the correct spark plugs were put in. 

I could tell more stories. But I think my point is made. Don't go here.

text:
Fair, trustworthy, and friendly service in a pinch! 

I was out and about running errands in North Oakland yesterday. At one point, I was getting gas at an Arco. After I filled up, my car wouldn't start! So bizarre. We eventually got a tow truck to take us to Mizuki Auto - I'm so glad I happened upon this place randomly!

I called to check availability before the tow truck brought my car in. Earl sounded really friendly and was available to take my car in. Some car shops book up and aren't available to take you - so make sure to call a shop to make sure they can check out any emergency issues. 

The car in tow got to Mizuki before we did. They were already evaluating my car by the time we got there. Earl and team needed some time to check out the car - and hey, this isn't the worst area to be stranded in lol. 5 min walking is Triple Rock - a classic Berkeley establishment! We snacked in their outdoor parklet and had a beer as we waited for the car diagnosis. Lol at that point, I was pretty confident I wouldn't be driving home. 

Earl called maybe 30 minutes later and said I needed a new starter. He gave me a quote, and I gave him the green light! The part would arrive in the morning and he would call me when the work was done the next day. 

I later Googled what a fair price was for a new starter, and to my pleasant surprise, Earl's quote was on the low end of that range that Google search came up with! I felt good know that I wasn't being crazy overcharged - I always struggle to trust these dang auto repair shops always tryna upsell!! And I'm confident that I'm not alone - I see other reviews mentioning the fair, reasonable rates here! 

Also, Earl was so friendly- my phone was going to die yesterday and he let me borrow his portable charger and cable! The homie right here!

Overall, it was a pretty seamless experience and I definitely recommend these guys if you have any car troubles.

text:
I am sad to leave a bad review, but it feels important for the benefit of the community. 

Very new car owner, have a 2012 Prius. The check engine light went on. Carlos gave me a diagnosis of bad spark plug and ignition coil, also quoted me a few other things like the filter and break for over $3000. After denying other services, I did spark plug and ignition coil and two filters. It was over $1600 dollar. (Way over priced according to Google.) 

Soon after, I started hearing rattling sound coming out of the front of the car. I went back. Carlos was perplexed at first, then upon some "looking and hearing", told me that it's from the transmission - gears getting old and rattling, $5000 to replace the transmission and I should consider selling the car as is. I was very sad and confused. 

Finally got the wisdom to go to another shop that many friends had recommended. This shop seemed to know their job much better. Upon hearing my description of the symptom, already guessed that it's the head gasket, which is very common in gen 3 Prius at this mileage, and very worth fixing than selling. The diagnosis confirmed that it was the head gasket. I went to gasket master and fixed it for under $2000. 

Be careful.

text:
I went to this shop to see if they were honest and fair with their pricing, and unfortunately, that was not the case. They charged me $283 for a diagnostic scan, which is outrageous considering most shops offer this for free. Then, they tried to sell me a $1,200 coolant flush and hose replacement.

I have professional automotive experience, so I let them do the job to evaluate their work. The hose they replaced is right on top of the engine bay, an easy fix that takes minutes. After they finished, I inspected everything and found that they never flushed the coolant at all--they only replaced the hose but charged for a full flush. A real coolant flush costs around $80 max at a reputable shop.

This experience showed me that they overcharge for basic services and recommend unnecessary repairs. If you're looking for fair pricing and honest work, I'd recommend going elsewhere.

text:

With that said, Carlos, the new owner/business manager, brings in an entirely different story. He incarnates that shady mechanic that we all dread.

He'll start by charging you a $150/$200 diagnostic fee before doing any actual work, even if you come prepared with specific items to get done and are not interested in anything else, or if the work is obvious or about standard maintenance.

This guy does not have a care in the world: he's here to make money and being a mechanic is only a facade.

Long story short: don't bother, and go next door. There are plenty of other mechanics nearby that will do a fantastic job for a much better price and without deceptive tactics.

text: I had my 2012 VW GTI towed to Berkeley Auto Service after it wouldn't start. I mentioned that the brakes had been squeaking a little, and asked them to let me know if the car was in need of anything else. Carlos got back to me the next day with a $4000 estimate that included a new fuel pump (reason the car wouldn't start), new shocks/struts (which they said were leaking), and new breaks (which they also said were leaking). Also included were new wipers ($60 for parts, and $210 for labor). I replaced the wipers myself last winter, so I know they were not needed. I also know that they take about 2 minutes to install. I called the shop and told them I was going to have my car towed somewhere else for repair. When I got to the shop, the car was running (they failed to mention this on the phone), so I drove it to a shop down the road. I shared the estimate with them, and they checked out all of the supposed issues. Turns out, the diagnoses were totally bogus! I picked my car up the next day, no repairs done, and it's been driving fine since. I understand that fuel pump issues can be intermittent, so it's possible I will encounter problems in the future, but I will not be taking it to Berkeley Auto Service when/if that's happens. My uncle, who is a mechanic, looked it up and told me it is supposed to take 0.9 hours for a qualified technician to replace a fuel pump on a 2012 GTI. They were going to charge me $420 in labor. Save yourself the trouble, find a trustworthy mechanic!

text:
My first (and only) 5-star review, and it's as 100% accurate and valid as they come. 

My Dad worked as an airline mechanic for 34years. When I grew up, he fixed the family cars. Everything shy of balancing the tires or swapping out a transmission. 
When I moved out to California from New York back in 90, one important piece of advice my old man told me, "find a good, honest mechanic for your ride."

I met the owner Roger in 1996 with a friend of mine who was rollin an old BMW 530ie (a beast of a car). I was wondering why we went Berkeley Auto Service with a BMW, when the venue clearly said "Specializing in Volkswagen & Audi". That's when Roger chimed in letting me know that he'll fix any car if he can. OK... lets see.; Here's my 94 Acura Integra with issues..

Now I know the basic markup for wholesale auto part suppliers, and a ballpark idea regarding labor amounts to fix numerous problems (how much time to do this, swap that, clean this, flush that, etc..), so I'd know if someone wasn't being honest. And being a New Yorker, I have a zero tolerance for bullshit. 

It's 2013. I'm now having my 3rd Acura regularly serviced by Roger, his brother Dan, and Mikael. I'm smart enough to give the guy PLENTY OF NOTICE because the place is always on overflow. I'm hoping this 5-star review adds to their workload. 

In short, they are as honest as they come. They are fair and competitive with their pricing (if not a deal...), and lets face it.. everyone should be making the money they're worth. They're always busy for a reason. 

Hope this helps..

text:
After reading the reviews and my brother's experience with his Audi, I thought I have found the trust worthy VW/Audi auto shop. However, I did not have a very good experience there. I brought my Beetle for timing belt change, and asked them to check on a coolant leak problem. I got back the car on the same day (very pleased about that), but I found that the driver side automatic door lock switch doesn't have tension to bounce back to its original place. I asked the owner, he said nobody touched it, because we did engine work... this kind of switch always have similar problem. I let it go and drove the car back home. No doubt that they did a great job on changing the timing belt, and water pump, but the coolant started to leak again after couple weeks. I called the owner again, to see what the problem was and brought the car back to the shop. He called me back and said he replaced the coolant temperature sensor that he replaced earlier, because its seal did not seal the coolant very well, and there's no charge for the replacement. When picking up the car, the automatic transmission stick gear switch button cover came off. I thought just popping the cover back in should be fine, and drove home. However, the coolant leak problem did not get fixed, and now the gear switch button seems to loose tension just like the door switch.

For the button problem: After the button got depressed, a lot of the times it stays depressed and never bounce back. I looked at it closely, and it is clear that it got replaced for some reason. The original button had some wears after years of depressing, such as smooth stripes on the button's surface after years rubbing with the plastic cover (yes, I did notice this detail). The "new" button doesn't have any of those wears.

For the coolant problem: Since I have some professional auto mechanic tools and Bentley manual for my car, I decided to dig to the problem myself to see what's up. It turns out that they used silicon glue to seal the plastic coolant housing with the engine block, instead of using the o-ring as printed in the manual. After I bought the o-ring from dealer for $6, putted it in and put everything back together, a lot of work, but the problem got fixed.

That's my story, and thanks for reading.

text:
What is this unicorn that I've found?!

A car shop that treats you (male or female) with respect? A place where the people don't try to weasel as much money from you as possible? Where they care about getting your repeat business? Mechanics that are knowledgeable, friendly, and who are trying to not explode your pocketbook?

How is this possible?

BUT IT'S TRUE!

I went here for the first time today. I called up, spoke to Marc and was told to just bring my little Honda on over for an oil change. 

I had done some research trying to figure out what prices would be in this area and I was not looking forward to the hit my wallet was going to take but it had to be done. 

I showed up, dropped my car off and asked Marc to also take a look at the tires and filters to see if they needed rotation/changing. I asked him where I should go wait, since I didn't have a ride and had to stay in the area. He gave me some great guidance and I ended up at Santana Row, sitting outside in the breeze, enjoying some coffee and free wifi. 

A little while later (they were busy, so it did take a few hours but I was informed of that ahead of time and didn't mind) I got a call and a text from Marc that I was all set!

I get back to the shop and Marc went over what was done and showed me the cost. It was a full $40 less than I was expecting, according to the Googling I had done before my arrival. Marc even told me that my filters were still fine, and the tires as well. So he COULD have charged me for things I did not need, since I had asked them to be done if needed, but he declined to do so! 
I would have had no clue if the filters / tires needed to be done or not. 

So - if you want an honest and affordable place that will take care of your car and not overcharge you, this is your spot!

Thank you Marc! You've earned a customer for life!

text:
Don't take your car for smog checks unless your car's computer reports 0 missing monitors.

On 10/15/20, I drove in for a smog check. It did not pass or fail. Instead, the car's on-board computer reported several monitors as not ready. I paid for the service, though the car did not pass, which I was fine with since they offered a free re-test within 30 days. I took my car home, connected my $50 OBDII analyzer tool to the car and indeed, several monitors were reporting as incomplete/not ready. As instructed, I drove the car to allow the monitors to fully test the various systems. I ended up driving 417 miles. I then plugged in my OBDII analyzer tool and noted that only one monitor reported as incomplete (INC), the EVAP monitor. My analyzer also returned a green light this time so I figured I was good to go; see images. Today, 11/13/20, with two days to spare in my 30 day re-test window, I took my car back to Quality Car Center. When I pulled up, the tech asked me if all monitors were ready. I said all but the EVAP were ready. The technician refused to test my car saying that all monitors needed to be in ready/Ok state. I was skeptical because, though my analyzer stated that the EVAP was not ready, it gave me a green light. He said I should continue to drive the car. But, I had already driven it over 400 miles. 

I took my car directly to a different Smog testing shop. I explained the situation to the tech and he said that smog shops get graded. And, by accepting a car that has the EVAP monitor in a not ready state, their grade gets negatively impacted. He admitted to not liking having to test cars such as mine because of this but that he would do it. He did and it passed. Yes, ideally, we'd all like our cars to have every monitor in a ready state, before testing, but CA does allow the EVAP monitor to be in a not ready state and still pass smog.

After that conversation, it seemed to me that Quality Car Center does not want their grade negatively impacted, so they wouldn't test my car even though they knew it would pass. They were trying to protect their grade though I had already paid them.

I drove back to Quality Car Center. All of us shared our sides; I'll admit that we argued. One of their techs even walked away during our conversation. I said that I understood their desire to protect their grade by not re-testing my car, and to make me whole, I asked for a refund. They refused. They did offer to re-test another car or get a discount on an oil change. But, that misses the point. If my car can pass smog while missing one monitor that is allowed by the state of California, why should a shop deny me a re-test after I've already paid?

While we were talking, I suggested that they connect an OBDII analyzer to each car that comes in before running smog tests and taking money. That way, they could protect their grade and the customer would not have paid anything. They said that California Smog rules don't allow that. Instead, they are supposed to connect to the car to the California Smog computer so that it can record how many monitors are/aren't ready. In the end, he said that he refused to risk his Smog certification license on just one car. If it's true, I guess California would give his shop a lower grade by testing a car with a missing EVAP monitor. Again, to protect his grade, he refused to re-test my card knowing that it would pass.

I will allow that the Quality Car Center is not entirely in the wrong... it seems that California has a share of the blame as well.... why is California negatively grading shops from testing cars that miss one allowed monitor?

In the end, my car has passed smog with the allowed missing one monitor but I've paid two shops for the privilege.

Don't take your car to Quality Car Center to get a smog check unless all your monitors are in the ready state because they want to protect their grade with California. I've pasted a link to a scanning tool below to check your monitors before going to Quality Car Center.

See research from sites below...

https://www.bar.ca.gov/Consumer/On-Board_Diagnostic_Systems.aspx
"A number of monitors are "not ready." This means the vehicle has not had the opportunity to complete one or more of the required self-diagnostic checks of the vehicle's OBD system. The number of allowed unready monitors varies by model year and fuel type."

text:
** there is a $10 off Synthetic Oil Change coupon on Yelp!** 

TLDR; Marc and his colleague were very friendly and professional. I would highly recommend coming here for car services! Their prices are very reasonable as well!

~~~

I called multiple oil change locations (Pepboys, Jiffy Lube, Honda dealership), and decided to come to Quality Tune Up because after the $10 coupon, it was the cheapest (~$55). 

When I arrived, Marc was very nice and welcoming. He collected my information and told me it would take around an hour to complete, and that he would call me after everything was done. I mentioned to him that I had the $10 off coupon, and he told me he would apply it at the end, when I picked up my car.

During the wait, I was able to walk across the street, and wander around Santana Row. This place is located right across the street from Maggianos. 

After a little over an hour, I decided to walk back to the shop. Marc told me that my service light indicated 3 things based on the 3 different service letters and numbers. I needed an oil change, tire rotation, and air filter change. He told me that since he didn't have any air filters available, he could order one for me. I told him that I wouldn't be able to wait for the air filter change today, but he told me I could stop by another day to get it replaced (it would only take a couple seconds).

When he was processing my payment, he forgot to apply the coupon, and was very apologetic. He said that he would be able to apply the synthetic oil coupon to the new air filter, when I get it done. He also wrote it on my receipt.

I was very happy with the overall service, and will definitely come back here again! Also, the location is perfect, because while you wait, you can walk to the mall or to Santana Row!

text:
I've been bringing my cars here for quite some time now. All the guys there - Gilbert, Mike, Lee, and Mark - are not only very knowledgeable but also genuinely nice, friendly guys who treat you with respect. They never try to sell you something you don't need. For example, I was told by another repair shop that the wheel cylinders on my truck were leaking and that I needed new brake shoes. After taking it here, Lee inspected the rear brakes. He said the brake shoes are fine, and the wheel cylinders are just starting to leak and that I didn't need to replace those yet. Anyway I decided to go ahead and replace the wheel cylinders.

Recently my 2008 Honda Civic overheated. I had the car towed into their shop for diagnosis. The head gasket had blown, and the entire engine was destroyed. Even the ignition coils were melted! Well we did a little research and discovered that the 2006 - 2008 (and some 2009) model year Civics have an issue with cracks developing in the engine block. This of course could lead to a loss of coolant and the engine overheating. What's more, it turned out that Honda had extended the warranty to 10 years so my Civic was still covered. Gilbert reviewed the technical service bulletin (TSB), which indicated three possible locations on the engine block where cracks could develop. However, after an initial inspection, neither Gilbert, Lee, or myself could find any signs of cracks in the engine block. So I decided to have them proceed with replacing the engine; I knew they would do a good job at a fair price. Once they started to remove some components in preparing to remove the engine, they performed another inspection since now they were able to get a much better look at the engine block. I received a phone call from Gilbert that they indeed found a crack at one of the locations detailed in the TSB. I was ecstatic! I had the car towed to my local Honda dealership. We weren't sure if Honda would replace the entire engine under the extended warranty, but even if they only covered the engine block and the labor, it would have still saved me a lot of money. As it turned out, Honda replaced the entire engine free of charge: the engine block, the engine head, the ignition coils, and the spark plugs.

Well long story short, Gilbert, Mike, and Lee saved me several thousand dollars. On top of that, they only charged me for 2 hours of labor even though I am pretty sure they spent at least twice that much time on my car. Five stars is not nearly enough - these guys rock! I'm a customer for life, and I recommend them every chance I get.

text:
Stay the eff away from this place. This has to be the single worst auto repair facility I've ever dealt with. 

I will admit my van is old enough to give an archeologist an orgasm. It is the last thing I have left of a person who was like a father to me. He passed away in 2008. That's why I can't bring myself to Old Yeller the sucker yet. It'd make his death feel final. I'm not ready for that just yet. 

I'm pretty car savvy. I've been doing the repair work on it myself for the last 4 years but we moved into a new apartment and it's against the lease. I knew the fuel pump was emitting noises that signified it as terminal but I was planning to hunt down a pump at a decent price and pop over to Sears with the part like I always do. The blasted thing had other ideas and let loose its death rattle in the driveway. 

Since getting it towed to Sears was likely to cost signing over my first born, I looked for a closer location that could get to it within the next day. This place said they could. It just went downhill from there. 

The moment I walked in they talked to me in the most condescending manner - like I was a bleeding toddler! They would only talk to my husband (who knows as much about cars as goose knows about God) and refused to listen to a word that came out of my mouth. Multiple times they asked a question about the car and wouldn't accept MY answer until it came out of HIS mouth. The van was already there and the tow truck had left. I was stuck with them. 

Despite promising to get to it within the next day, they didn't go near it for three days. It took a week to for me to get it back. 

They tried to cornhole me on the price of the part. No fuel pump costs $850 for the part alone. The cost of the pump plus labor wouldn't cost that much. They're $300 MAX. I had to go back with multiple quotes and threaten to go buy the part myself before it got down to a more reasonable $260. 

I had also asked them to replace a fuel fill valve while they were at it. I was repeatedly told "you don't need one, honey" even though I was standing in front of the fool holding the broken part. Needless to say, it wasn't replaced until I took it to Sears.

Vacuum hoses are in the engine. You didn't need to replace them with the fuel pump. You probably never even looked at them. Nice try, Skippy. 

I had to have my husband call to get a pick up time because they wouldn't give a solid answer. He was the one to go get the van and pay. That was probably for the best as I already wanted to clobber one of them at this point.

I wouldn't go near this place again if THEY paid ME. If you have any sense, you won't either.

I still don't see why someone couldn't check our car out for 5 minutes and make sure the tire pressure was okay and that it was safe to drive. text:
So in Jan. 2010, I brought my wife's Toyota Highlander to this shop since it was conveniently located near Santana Row and the movie theater. The car just needed an oil change and some brake work to fix the shimmy/vibration when braking. 

So I get a call from them while I'm out waiting for the car, and they tell me they're gonna need to replace the front brake pads and re-surface the rotors, which made plenty of sense since I was at 48K and the front brakes had never been serviced. What didn't make sense is they said the rear rotors needed replacing, but the the pads were fine. This is odd because usually the front brakes last about 3 times that of the rear brakes, since the front brakes do most of the work. It was strange that only the rear rotors would need replacing. I asked if they could just resurface the rear rotors, but they said there was not enough thickness left to do that. I wish I would have come back and asked to see the rotors myself. Then maybe I could have called them on their BS. 

That is not even the worst of it... Not long ago (30K miles later) I took the same car into another very reputable shop to have the brakes inspected for a shimmy/vibration. The car again needed to have the front brake pads replaced, and the rotors re-surfaced which is about normal after over 3 1/2 yrs. (30K miles later).

The CRAZY part is the shop found 1/2 the THREADS on one of the LEFT FRONT CALIPERS STRIPPED OUT WITH EPOXY HOLDING THE BOLT ONTO THE CALIPER! They had never seen anything like that before, and they noted they were surprised the epoxy held for that long. They saved the part so I could see it with my own eyes. 

So basically someone at Quality Tune-up screwed up big time, and tried to cover their mistake, creating an unsafe condition for the customer. Brake failure is no joke. Luckily for us that didn't happen. I really hope the guy who did that brake job is not working at this shop anymore. I'd strongly advise not going here for the dishonest unsafe shady work that was done on my car.

text:
Proceed with caution! I took my car here for a standard oil change. They told me it would take about 45 minutes, so I hopped on over to Chipotle for a leisurely lunch. When I came back, everything seemed fine, and I went on about my merry way. A few days later, I started noticing that my engine sounded "throatier" upon starting than it ever did before. I don't know much about cars, so I kinda brushed it off as the car getting older. Come to find out about a week after my oil change that they never screwed the oil cap back on and it was just resting there. While I didn't lose a ton of oil, enough splashed out over the course of the week to really muck up my engine bay. I went back, told them what happened, and requested they clean my engine bay. Without so much as an "I'm sorry," 
they took my keys and told me to come back in an hour. Uber lame.

Came back an hour later to find my car sitting in the back, running, windows down, ac running, and windshield wipers going - for no apparent reason. Who knows how long they'd left it running. They showed me it was clean and then tried to tell me it must have rattled off. To which I replied that it was sitting UPSIDE DOWN and placed on top, which means they FORGOT to put it back on. Mistakes happen, but I wish they would have at least been willing to admit it! Definitely not going back there again.

text:
Good Day,

I have been wanting to send in a review but yelp is ok but I wanted you to know this. Marc at this location is a keeper and I hope he is still there. April 13, 2023 my husband and I flew in to San Jose to pick up a 2000 Subaru Outback from an auction we had won from an estate. It needed a battery and oil change so we can drive it to Las Vegas, NV and then our son was flying into drive it to college in Iowa. I share that so you can know some backstory on this adventure. Car we don't know, area we don't know, people we don't know to trust. To say we were short with each other is being nice. Also 5 min before we had purchased a battery from one of the worst AutoZones I had ever been in.

I called around and found Quality Car Care Center on 425 S Winchester Blvd. and talked to Marc. He was nice on the phone and told us to come on over. He greeted us and did the intake for the car. We told him our crazy adventure and he said he would make sure to let us know of any issues. We asked what was in the area. He told us of coffee shops, areas to walk and the Winchester House. Having no idea what that was we walk down to see it. (Totally Cool!) Just as the tour ended Marc called.

Marc told us everything they had found and what we wanted to address when we got to Las Vegas with our mechanic. We even got a printout. There were no scare tactics or over charges. Marc had earned my husbands respect, which is not given out easily for this veteran. Marc's great attitude and kindness turned the trip for us. If we were in the area this would be our go to from then on. 

I know this is long and thanks for reading. We promised Marc a review on Yelp but I wanted corporate to know the kind of people on the ground. Wish you all a great Labor Day Weekend.

text: Took my car to this shop for oil change. Month and half later, when I checked my dipstick, it was showing twice above the line (overfilled), so I decided to return it. I spoke to Marc; he double checked the dip stick confirmed it was overfilled. Then they proceed to drain the oil to measure it and found 8 quarts of oil. Turns out the tech who did the oil change did not drain the old oil and just added new oil (double filled). The tech also did not change the oil filter because the old oil filter from Toyota was still attached on the car. My car ran for 1 and half month with 8 quarts of oil and probably messed up the engine.

Which is a really good price considering the repair work that I needed to have done and what a competitor would have charged me.

I could go on and on about the great service that I've received with Quality Tune Up Car Care Center but I'm short on time so I'll leave it here for now!
